seams.title: Wellsprings and Families
seams.summary: The five texts use only a few Wellspring names. Most are among the canonical Sixty and carry the right Families: Mortalis, Anamnesis, Dissolution, Luminalis, Tenebra, Judicium, Ascensio, Fixatio, Benediction and Sublimatio. Malphas's card is clean too. The serious trouble is upstream, where canon disagrees with itself in two places, and neither disagreement is in CONFLICTS.md. First, the Lists sheet, Fracture of Worlds and the physics register leave Calcination and Distillation out of the Sixty, while Alchemetrica, the live rule R18-5 and about eight cards call them Wellsprings. Second, sources disagree on which of Sublimatio and Sublimare is sublimation. Both must be settled before Mu-jin's card or the Great Work passages are converted. Canon never numbers the Wellsprings, so "the forty-ninth" is an invention. The texts' Mortalis (a river whose current animates the dead) and Anamnesis (a Wellspring that stores the past at a place) drift from the physics register, where Mortalis is a boundary and Anamnesis is a reading instrument; the Heresiology already carries the Codex's readings. Calling a Wellspring a place is a mechanical rename to "site", but Genesio's rung (strength rating) needs a decision. Outside this seam but worth routing: Vol II docx:67 says "fourteen Temperance stages" and docx:149 names "Sovereignty" as a Stage.

findings.topic: Calcination and Distillation (Distillatio) named as Wellsprings
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:81 counts them among "the sixty Wellsprings": "Calcination burns away false structure. Dissolution unravels cohesion into base frequencies." Mu-jin card:48 lists them as harmonizations: "Alchemetrica — Coagulatio, Distillatio, Fixation, Calcination." The Codex itself (Vol II docx:149) names them only as Great Work stages.
findings.canon: The Sixty exclude both. The Lists sheet's Wellspring column ($WOTR_TRUE_CANON/The Master Codex.xlsx, rows 2-61, read through build/codex.py:39-43) holds 60 names and neither is among them. FOW V (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/V. Wellsprings….md:29-128) lists exactly 60, with Caloria at ten and no Calcination. wiki/The Magic System/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings.md:158 says "Sixty-one listings against sixty unique currents." The Master Codex Spell, Glyph and Alchemical indices never use either one as a Primary or Secondary Wellspring. On the other side, the live rule R18-5-ALCHEMY_DOCTRINE_BINDING (rules/pack-18-eighteen.yaml:274-280) "fixes the eight Wellsprings that are simultaneously Wellspring, cosmic principle and alchemical operation" and names Calcination and Distillation among them. Alchemetrica.md:23-35 and :266 agree with the rule, as does rules/doc-shared-soul-crystal-mechanism.yaml:126 ("Calcination running Caloria"). Cards repeat the claim: Ossuary Choir:46 ("The only Wellspring in the sixty…"), Ignatius:50, Vaelen Mourcrix:37, Vorynth:17,43, Karasaki:14, Silas:14, and The Open Crucible:61,71-75,167-170,185-188. R18-2-CODEX_FIRST_MANDATE (pack-18-eighteen.yaml:16-22) takes Wellspring assignment from the Lists sheet "never from memory". Isaac's 2026-09-12 ruling was "FOW/Codex names win everywhere, sweep the rest" (RULINGS.md:318-321). Canon is split, and the split is not recorded in CONFLICTS.md.
findings.why_it_matters: Mu-jin's harmonizations (the Wellsprings his soul is tuned to) shape how the new Codex author thinks and talks about alchemy. Whether the stages are currents or procedures decides how alchemy connects to the Sixty. The answer also reaches about ten other canon pages.
findings.question: Are Calcination and Distillation real Wellsprings (currents a soul can tune itself to), or only alchemical procedures (steps done at the bench)?

options.label: A. Hold the Sixty (the Lists sheet wins)
options.consequence: Both become procedures only. Alchemetrica's "eight" table and R18-5's list are corrected through a logged ruling. Mu-jin's card, The Open Crucible and about six other cards are re-pointed to canonical mirror currents (see ws-02). Canon ends up clean, but this is the biggest sweep.

options.label: B. Keep them as trade names for two of the Sixty
options.consequence: The words survive as the alchemists' names for existing currents (for example Calcination = Cinerion, Distillation = Sublimare), recorded on those Wellspring pages under R50-25-WELLSPRINGS (rules/doc-naming-law-2026-09-26.yaml:601-608). The Sixty stay intact and the card wording survives with a gloss. The risk is that readers mix up the current with the bench step of the same name.

options.label: C. Admit them as new Wellsprings
options.consequence: This makes 62 currents. It breaks the number sixty in FOW, the Lists sheet, the Family counts and R5-A-SKELETON_UNCHANGED (pack-05-five.yaml:26-31), and it needs a demonstrated-absence proposal under R18-2-NO_NEW_CATEGORY_WITHOUT_CHECK.

findings.recommendation: A. It follows the Lists-sheet mandate and Isaac's own 09-12 precedent, and ws-02 gives every stage an existing current, so the texts lose nothing. Record the conflict in CONFLICTS.md before anything is swept. B is the fallback if the card sweep costs too much.
findings.correction: The split is real and is Isaac's to decide, but three details need fixing. (1) Necrocursica:81 names only Calcination, Dissolution and Sublimatio as operation-Wellsprings. Distillation appears elsewhere, as an alignment: "Distillation-aligned glyph chains" (:161) and "Distillation-aligned separation" (:213). Those two lines also need a fix once this is decided. (2) Canon itself uses the non-Sixty name "Distillatio". Alchemetrica:102 says Distillation "mirrors Distillatio", and the same name appears on Mu-jin's card at :83 (Diegetic Read keyed to Distillatio) and :99 (Distillatio Seal), in The Open Crucible at :48, :61, :129 and :185-188, and in The Spirit Rune Arts at :45. The blast radius is larger than the card line alone. (3) RULINGS.md:318-321 ruled on Stage-naming collisions and one Family misattribution. It is precedent, not a ruling on Wellsprings. On the same day, 2026-09-12, Isaac ratified R18-5 "wholesale" (pack-18-eighteen.yaml:262-289), and R18-5 names Calcination and Distillation as Wellsprings. Both sides of the split therefore carry Isaac's ratification, which is the real reason this belongs in the questionnaire. Also note that the cards already give Calcination a Family, Caloria (Ossuary Choir:46, Ignatius:50, Vaelen:37, Vorynth:43). That makes Option B's Calcination = Cinerion (Caloria) a Family-preserving choice. Keep the recommendation (A, with B as fallback), but base it on R18-2's "from the Lists sheet (never from memory)" rather than on the 09-12 Stage ruling.
findings.verify_evidence: Read the Lists sheet through build/codex.py: the Wellspring column has 60 names in rows 2-61, with no Calcination, Distillation or Distillatio. FOW V:29-128 has 61 listings and 60 unique currents. Eight Families:147-158. Alchemetrica:23-33, :102, :266. pack-18-eighteen.yaml:9-23 (R18-2 mandate) and :262-289 (R18-5, ratified "Isaac, 2026-09-12… wholesale"). RULINGS.md:318-321 is headed "Stage-naming collisions". Necrocursica:81, :161, :213. Kwon Mu-jin.md:48, :83, :99. Open Crucible:48, :61, :129, :185-188. Spirit Rune Arts:45. Ossuary Choir:46, Ignatius:50, Vaelen:37, Vorynth:17 and :43, Karasaki:14, Silas:14. rules/doc-shared-soul-crystal-mechanism.yaml:126. grep of CONFLICTS.md: no row for Calcination, Distillation, Sublimare or Sublimatio.

findings.topic: Which of the Sixty, if any, each Great Work stage draws on
findings.doc_claim: Vol II docx:149 gives the seven stages: "Calcination, Dissolution, Separation, Conjunction, Fermentation, Distillation, Coagulation." Vol I wiki:165 says each corruption comes from a principle "severed from its Wellspring root."
findings.canon: Only two stages have a current in canon. Dissolution is itself a Wellspring (Limina; Limina page:68-73; Alchemetrica:27). Coagulation "mirrors Coagulatio" (Alchemetrica:101), which FOW V:82 calls "the alchemical operation that gathers substrate". Alchemetrica:104 says Conjunction has "no single Wellspring mirror". Separation and Fermentation have no mirror anywhere. The physics register suggests candidates by physical analogue. Cinerion: "Pyrolytic char and its catalytic residue" (Caloria page:42). Sublimare: "Fractional distillation. Separation by differential volatility" (Vectoria page:49). Rebirthine: "Catabolism pays for anabolism" (Vitalia page:42). Manganthra: heterogeneous catalysis, which holds incompatible reactants together (Caloria page:56-57). Judicium: the Wellspring of discernment (FOW V:48), matching Heresiology:83, "It should culminate in judgment and action." The Great Work itself is canon: "The seven-stage curriculum of Alchemia" (Lexicon:70).
findings.why_it_matters: Isaac wants alchemy tied more tightly to the magic system. A stage-to-current map turns the Codex's "Wellspring root" line into literal mechanics, and it gives each of the Seven Corruptions a Wellspring-injury axis, which the Heresiology already uses (Heresiology:166-174).
findings.question: Should each of the seven Great Work stages be tied to one of the Sixty, so the Codex's "Wellspring root" line is literally true?

options.label: Physics mapping
options.consequence: Calcination→Cinerion, Dissolution→Dissolution, Separation→Judicium, Conjunction→Manganthra (as the mediator Alchemetrica's Rupture rules call for), Fermentation→Rebirthine, Distillation→Sublimare, Coagulation→Coagulatio. Alchemetrica's table and some cards change, and no new names are needed.

options.label: Minimal mapping
options.consequence: Only Dissolution and Coagulation mirror currents; the other five stay pure procedure, and Vol I:165 is reworded. This is the least canon change and the weakest link between alchemy and the Sixty.

options.label: Moral mapping
options.consequence: Stages are matched by the Heresiology's glosses (for example Calcination→Catharsis, "release, purgation", Heresiology:173). It is emotionally apt but ignores the physical analogues that R18-2 points to.

findings.recommendation: The physics mapping. It uses only existing currents, so it needs no R18-2 proposal, and Mu-jin's Caloria undertone (card:43) fits Cinerion. Isaac should confirm two sub-choices: Cinerion rather than Pyreveil for Calcination, and Judicium rather than Sublimare for Separation.
findings.correction: The status should be ambiguous, not absent_from_canon. Canon has two partial maps the auditor left out. (a) Alchemetrica's Four Operations table maps operations to currents: Coagulation mirrors Coagulatio (:101), Distillation mirrors Distillatio, a non-Sixty name (:102), Sublimation mirrors Sublimare (:103), and Conjunction has "no single Wellspring mirror" (:104). (b) Alchemetrica's Twelve Turnings (:108-140) put the stage names into a workshop sequence: Burning = calcination (:113), Taking = dissolution, Parting = separation, Rot = putrefaction (:116), Wedding = conjunction, Rising = sublimation (:119), Setting = congelation (:120). The Sealing Turning draws "heavily on Fixatio's chains" (:138). There is no Fermentation or Distillation Turning. The Heresiology also lists the seven stages (:44) and calls them "disciplines imposed upon both matter and maker" (:45), which is canon's own "procedure, not current" reading. The question stands as Isaac's. Two fixes to the options: the Physics mapping's Conjunction→Manganthra overrides Alchemetrica:104 outright, and its consequence should say so. The Moral option's cite, Heresiology:173, is the Wellspring-injury table and not a stage map. Also add an option: "stages are procedures; each working's Wellspring root is whatever current it draws". That option is canon-neutral and matches Heresiology:45.
findings.verify_evidence: Alchemetrica.md:96-104, :108-140 (mermaid lines 113-120; Sealing at :138). Heresiology of Alchemy.md:42-47 and :57-143 (the seven Perverted stages, with no Wellspring assignments). Lexicon:70. Vectoria:49, Caloria:42 and :56-57, Vitalia:42 all confirmed as quoted. FOW V:48 (Judicium).

findings.topic: Sublimatio against Sublimare: which one is sublimation
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:81 says "Sublimatio elevates without intermediate states." Necrocursica:233 prescribes "a Sublimatio-aligned cleansing of the Aether Shell to elevate and separate the superimposed resonance".
findings.canon: Canon is split. Vectoria page:42 gives Sublimatio the analogue "Sublimation. Solid to vapour with no liquid phase"; Vectoria page:49 gives Sublimare "Fractional distillation. Separation by differential volatility"; Eight Families:194 says "sublimation skips a phase, fractional distillation separates a mixture." Against those, Alchemetrica:30 reads "Sublimare | Elevates without passing through the states between", and Alchemetrica:103 says the Sublimation operation "mirrors Sublimare". R18-5 (pack-18-eighteen.yaml:278-279) names Sublimare as the operation-bound current. The split is not in CONFLICTS.md.
findings.why_it_matters: Necrocursica:81 matches the physics register and contradicts Alchemetrica, so the correct fix depends on which source wins. The answer also decides whether Distillation already has a home among the Sixty (Sublimare), which settles half of ws-01.
findings.question: Which twin is the sublimation current (a solid turning straight to vapour) and which is the distillation current (separating a mixture by boiling off its parts)?

options.label: The physics register wins
options.consequence: Sublimatio is sublimation and Sublimare is distillation. Alchemetrica:30 and :103 are corrected, and Distillation now mirrors Sublimare. Necrocursica:81 stands as written, and Necrocursica:233 becomes Sublimare-aligned because it separates.

options.label: Alchemetrica wins
options.consequence: Sublimare is sublimation. The Vectoria page's analogues and failure modes are swapped, Necrocursica:81 becomes Sublimare, and Distillation still has no current.

findings.recommendation: The physics register. It is the register that gives each twin a physical analogue and a failure mode, the Eight Families page already records the split explicitly, and it gives Distillation a canonical current with no new Wellspring. Log the conflict in CONFLICTS.md first.
findings.verify_evidence: Vectoria — Mechanics.md:42 (Sublimatio = "Sublimation. Solid to vapour with no liquid phase") and :49 (Sublimare = "Fractional distillation"). Eight Families:194 records the split and favours the physical reading. On the other side: Alchemetrica:30, :103 and :119. R18-5 names Sublimare (pack-18-eighteen.yaml:268-280). One more site follows Alchemetrica and belongs in the blast radius: Kytheris · Mother of Spores.md:17, where Sublimare "elevates without passing through the states between". FOW V:62-63 does not say which twin skips a phase. Not in CONFLICTS.md (grep).

findings.topic: Mu-jin's harmonization line: Fixation, Vocatia and Alchemetrica
findings.doc_claim: Kwon Mu-jin card:48, under Wellspring Harmonizations: "Alchemetrica — Coagulatio, Distillatio, Fixation, Calcination." and "Vocatia — trained, not latent."
findings.canon: The Wellspring is spelled Fixatio: Lists sheet row 23; FOW V:81 "What is held by Fixatio stays held." Canon uses "fixation" as Obsession Force vocabulary (FOW V:152; Alchemetrica:330). Vocatia is a Magical Category, "Invocation by recognition and correspondence" (Magical Categories:166-169; R10-1-CATEGORIES_AXIS, pack-10-ten.yaml:24-28), not a Wellspring. Alchemetrica is the Guild Accord Division and its practitioner's codex (card:27; Alchemetrica.md:11-14; Descent of Parun:13), not a Wellspring and not one of the eight Families (Eight Families:147-156). Coagulatio (Materia, FOW V:82) and Anamnesis (Limina, FOW V:122) are canonical.
findings.why_it_matters: This card is the new Codex author's source sheet. As written it lists a discipline, a Magical Category and a misspelling as Wellsprings.
findings.mechanical_fix: On card:48, change "Fixation" to "Fixatio". Remove Vocatia from the Wellspring line; it already appears as a Trait at :84 and as a technique at :98. Drop "Alchemetrica —" as a Wellspring heading and name the Division as his discipline instead. Add Families: Coagulatio (Materia), Fixatio (Materia), Anamnesis (Limina). Calcination and Distillatio wait on ws-01, ws-02 and ws-03. Optional: "Fixation array" (:28, :168), "Fixation Anchor Sense" (:82) and "Fixation delay" (:96) are names of workings rather than Wellsprings, but spelling them Fixatio avoids the Obsession Force word.
findings.correction: The card line groups harmonizations by discipline. "Alchemetrica —" is glossed as "His founding discipline", so it does not claim Alchemetrica is a Wellspring, and moving that label is formatting, not a conflict fix. What remains mechanical: "Fixation" becomes "Fixatio" (Lists row 23; FOW V:81; Alchemetrica:138 "Fixatio's chains"), and Vocatia comes out of the Wellspring Harmonizations list. Vocatia is Magical Category 16 (Magical Categories:166-169; R10-1), and the card already carries it as a Trait (:84) and a technique (:98). Distillatio's fate also reaches card:83 (Diegetic Read keyed to Distillatio) and card:99 (Distillatio Seal), not just :48. All of these wait on ws-01 and ws-03.
findings.verify_evidence: Kwon Mu-jin.md:27, :28, :43, :48, :82, :83, :84, :96, :98, :99, :168. Lists sheet row 23: Fixatio. FOW V:81 and :82. Magical Categories:166-169. pack-10-ten.yaml:10-30. Eight Families:147-156. Alchemetrica:11-14 and :138.

findings.topic: A Wellspring treated as a place
findings.doc_claim: Vol III docx:122: "the Wellspring of Anamnesis there is one of the oldest and densest I have ever encountered". docx:194: "The Wellspring node is in a natural hollow". Corrant:205: "the Codex identifies a Wellspring of Anamnesis".
findings.canon: Eight Families:50: "A Wellspring is not a place. But a Wellspring pools." Eight Families:52: "A Wellspring site is the aquifer. The current is the water table." Tier Ladders X:443 defines a site as the pool and a vein as the channel that feeds it. X:466 reserves "Wellspring Core" for the Fountainhead rung. Canon already names Wellspring-specific places this way, for example "The Oblation vein" (X:500).
findings.why_it_matters: The whole Genesio section rests on this term. Canon's site and vein vocabulary comes with a ready-made strength ladder, which connects the texts to the system Isaac wants them tied to.
findings.mechanical_fix: Where a text means a location, say "site" (or "vein" for the feeding channel). "The Wellspring of Anamnesis at Genesio" becomes "the Anamnesis site at Genesio" at Vol III docx:122,150,160,174,176; wiki Vol III:72,102; Corrant:205,209,211,247,251,261,265. "Wellspring node" and "primary node" (docx:176,194) become "the heart of the site"; use "Wellspring Core" only if ws-06 places Genesio at Fountainhead. "Anamnetic Wellspring pressure" (docx:142) becomes "the site's density". Keep "Wellspring" where the text means the current itself (docx:112). The Vol III title "What the Wellspring Keeps" and the Thom Submission's title follow ws-08.
findings.correction: The mechanical fix is right, but its line list is incomplete. Add Vol III docx:256 ("sitting in the Anamnesis Wellspring of the Genesio mountains") and Corrant:209 (already listed). Note that docx:176 ("not as a landmark or a structure but as a quality of attention") already half-agrees with Eight Families:50, so keep that sentence when renaming the heading at docx:174. The two report titles, Vol III docx:404 and Necrocursica:497 ("Anamnetic Wellspring Activation"), follow ws-08 and the missed "Anamnetic" item.
findings.verify_evidence: Eight Families:50, :52. X. Tier Ladders:443, :466. Vol III docx:122, :142, :150, :160, :174, :176, :194, :256, :404. Wiki Vol III:72, :102. Corrant:205, :209, :211, :247, :251, :261, :265. A wiki-wide grep found canon almost never phrases a Wellspring as "Wellspring of X at <place>".

findings.topic: The Genesio site's rung, and why heavy drawing made it "push"
findings.doc_claim: Vol III docx:136: "a spring, drawn from that way, long enough, begins to change its own pressure. It begins to push." docx:142 blames the Tempus drift on "the increase in Anamnetic Wellspring pressure".
findings.canon: X:482: "A site drawn on steadily falls as it is drawn", and a site worked past what it can give "gives out". X:480: a site under Obsession Force "takes, compatible or not, and stands one rung higher than its density". Eight Families:131 says corrupted sites are "Drawn from without reciprocity." The rungs: Millrace (X:463, where staying brings Wellspring Baptism), Whirlpool (X:465, "time wrong") and Fountainhead, the Wellspring Core (X:466). Eight Families:106 says Cores are "Extraordinarily rare, mostly New World, mostly unmapped." Heresiology:211 already makes the Genesio Activation Sequence canon, with its "distortions in Wellspring pressure and celestial correspondence". No rung is recorded for Genesio.
findings.why_it_matters: In canon, drawing on a site weakens it, so the text's rising pressure contradicts X:482 unless it is read as Obsession Force corruption. The rung also fixes how strong a visitor must be to stand there, which matters now that the author has changed.
findings.question: How strong is the Genesio Anamnesis site, and why did Vaughaus Thom's heavy drawing make it push harder instead of fading?

options.label: Whirlpool (Veil-Thin Nexus), corrupted by Thom
options.consequence: The push is the site taking, as Obsession Force, and it reads one rung higher while corrupted. "Time wrong" carries the Tempus drift, and completing the oldest Trace restores clean recognition. A visitor needs S to SS output to hold his own law there, which constrains when the author can visit (timeline seam).

options.label: Riptide, corrupted to read as Whirlpool
options.consequence: Gentler, so the author could stand there earlier in his career. The Tempus effect is less natural at this rung.

options.label: Fountainhead (Wellspring Core)
options.consequence: The site's law is the only law operating, including on the visitor, which explains the Trace completing into him. But an Old World Core cuts against "mostly New World" and would make Genesio one of the rarest places in canon.

options.label: Leave it unplaced
options.consequence: Treated like Halloway Mire (X:500), with no numbers. The push still needs the Obsession Force reading.

findings.recommendation: Whirlpool, corrupted by Thom. It keeps the text's effects, turns the push into canon Obsession Force, and ties the Tempus drift to the documented behaviour of a Veil-Thin Nexus.
findings.verify_evidence: X. Tier Ladders:447-466 (rung table; Riptide = A, Whirlpool = S/SS Veil-Thin Nexus, "time wrong" at :465; Fountainhead = Wellspring Core at :466), :480 (Obsession Force, one rung higher), :482 (a drawn site falls or gives out), :500 (not placed). Eight Families:106 and :131. Heresiology:211 (Genesio Activation Sequence, "distortions in Wellspring pressure and celestial correspondence"). Supporting detail the auditor could add: Heresiology:158 lists "local time-slippage" as an environmental sign of corruption, which strengthens the corrupted-Whirlpool reading. Vol III docx:136 "It begins to push" and docx:142 verified.

findings.topic: What Mortalis is and does
findings.doc_claim: Vol II docx:31: "Mortalis governs not death as an event, but death as a process… It is a river, not a reservoir." docx:103: "animation the Mortalis Wellspring's residual current will sustain." Vol III docx:372: "dissolution and terminus". Vol I wiki:85: "a loan from the Wellspring of Mortalis".
findings.canon: Mortalis is a Vitalia current (FOW V:98). Vitalia page:48-51 gives its analogue as "The non-equilibrium steady state" (a body kept alive by constant spending of energy): "Death is not an event added to that structure; it is the cessation of the expenditure and the return to equilibrium". Its failure is "Equilibration… they cool toward it without noticing." /home/oridon/wotr-vault/true-canon/Fracture of Worlds.md:1045: "Temperance through surrender; ending becomes passage." Heresiology:170, which drew on the Codex: "It does not preserve the dead in storage. It governs passage", glossed "dissolution, threshold, completion". Master Codex Pantheon: the Archon Auren, "The Keeper of the Still Gate", lists Mortalis among its Wellsprings. The Titan Sylorin's "Wellspring of Etherea" is "a translucent river of light running through all planes", with the edict "All souls return to the river." The Alchemical Index has two Mortalis products, Stillgate Ash and Gravetide Ink (both Vitalia). Mortalis strengthens Persistence, which resists "Nospheric intrusion" (FOW IV:91). Canon never says Mortalis's current powers animation. Several points already agree: death as a process rather than an event; Wellsprings are "not stored anywhere" (Eight Families:29); the Aphorism matches Heresiology doctrine; and Necrocursica:85's "continuous negotiation" fits the non-equilibrium analogue.
findings.why_it_matters: Mortalis runs through all five texts. Canon puts the river of souls with Sylorin, not with Mortalis. Using "dissolution" as Mortalis's gloss collides with the separate Dissolution current, which matters now that Malphas, who carries both (Malphas card:51,54), is an author.
findings.question: In the rewritten texts, is Mortalis the river the dead travel, or the gate (the boundary where a living body stops holding itself together)?

options.label: Gate, not river (recast to the physics)
options.consequence: Mortalis becomes the Black Gate, Auren's Still Gate. The river moves to Sylorin's Etherea, and the practitioner's "loan" becomes canon Equilibration. The impression-body is held by its Draft and sealed at the Mortalis boundary instead of running on the current. The Aphorism survives word for word. Rewrites Vol II docx:31,67,71 and wiki:30,54,57, plus Corrant:189.

options.label: Keep the river as older hermetic language
options.consequence: The imagery stays, framed as a pre-physics register the author knows is metaphor. This is the least rewriting, but readers may take it as mechanism, and it collides with Sylorin's river.

options.label: Extend canon
options.consequence: Add a necromantic sustain mechanism to the Mortalis entry. This stays truest to the old texts but writes new canon on the Vitalia page and must pass R18-2's absence check.

findings.recommendation: Gate, not river. It links the texts to canon that already exists (the Pantheon, the physics register, the Heresiology) without inventing anything. As a sub-choice, in Malphas's Necrocursica gloss Mortalis as "ending" or "passage", never "dissolution".
findings.correction: The core finding stands. Two fixes and one addition. (1) Option A moves the river to Sylorin's "Wellspring of Etherea", but that name is not among the Sixty. It exists only in the Codex Pantheon (Sylorin row), in the [Au] Death glyph's attested list, and at Spiritual Seat:170. Adopting it imports another non-Sixty "Wellspring", the same problem as ws-01. Option A's consequence should say the river is Sylorin's soulstream, not a current of the Sixty. (2) The sub-recommendation "never 'dissolution'" contradicts canon's own gloss: Heresiology:170 glosses Mortalis as "dissolution, threshold, completion". Vol III docx:372's "dissolution and terminus" is therefore canon-consistent, and avoiding the word in Malphas's voice is a style choice, not a correction. (3) Stronger support for the gate reading: the Spell Index row "The Still Gate's Mercy" is Auren's Signature Invocation, has Mortalis as Primary Wellspring, uses [Au] Death + [Vor] Return, and says "the glyph opens a threshold, it can't create death". Sylorin's glyphs are the same pair, so canon already links river and gate through one glyph chain.
findings.verify_evidence: Vitalia — Biochemistry.md:48-51. FOW V:98. True-canon Fracture of Worlds.md:1045. FOW IV:91. Heresiology:170. Master Codex through codex.py: Pantheon Auren (Associated Wellsprings include Mortalis; Signature Invocation "The Still Gate's Mercy"); Pantheon Sylorin ("Wellspring of Etherea (Continuance & Passage)", Glyphs [Au]+[Vor]); Spell Index "The Still Gate's Mercy"; Alchemical Index #16 Stillgate Ash and #27 Gravetide Ink. Spiritual Seat — Sylorin page:170. Vol II docx:31, :67, :71, :103. Corrant:189. Wiki Vol I:85.

findings.topic: What Anamnesis is and does
findings.doc_claim: Vol I wiki:117: "The Wellspring of Anamnesis holds memory because nothing that has been is erased from the Aetheric record." Vol III docx:112: "The Wellspring keeps the record of what souls were committed to." Corrant:207: it "governs memory, recollection, and the Aetheric preservation of experience."
findings.canon: Anamnesis is a Limina current (FOW V:122). Limina page:63-66 gives the analogue "Remanent magnetisation and thermoluminescent dosimetry" (materials that physically record their past) and says: "Objects genuinely store their history in physically readable form. Anamnesis is the instrument, not the miracle." Its failure: "a careless practitioner erases the record in the act of taking it." Veil:73 says "objects store their history readably; it reads a location's Mnemata", and Veil:76 that "thermal resetting erases what it reads". /home/oridon/wotr-vault/true-canon/Fracture of Worlds.md:1089: "remembering as a form of waking". Mnemata is the Magical Category covering temporal imprints and historical echo-law (Magical Categories:186-188). Heresiology:171, which drew on the Codex: "preserves not mere memory but charged records of lived commitment". Mu-jin card:48: "reads inherited intention and unfinished formulae with real fluency." Some points agree: reading records by contact; the Volitional Traces (unfinished commitments) fit Mu-jin's card closely; and docx:136's "sensitive to use" anticipates the canon failure mode.
findings.why_it_matters: Vol III's climax and the whole Thom affair depend on where the record lives. Vol I's claim that nothing is erased contradicts Anamnesis's canon failure mode. Corrant's claim that Anamnesis is the "foundation of correspondence" has no support in canon.
findings.question: Does the Anamnesis Wellspring itself store the past, or is it the tool that reads a past already stored in objects and ground?

options.label: Instrument (the physics reading)
options.consequence: The records, including Volitional Traces, live in the Genesio ground as its Mnemata. Anamnesis reads and wakes them. Thom's harm becomes erasure by coarse reading plus corruption of the site. Vol I's "nothing is erased" stays as the young author's error, which Vol III corrects. The Vol III title changes or is kept as irony.

options.label: Keeper (the Heresiology reading)
options.consequence: Amend the Limina entry so Anamnesis also preserves. The texts stay nearly intact, but the page's line "instrument, not the miracle" has to change.

options.label: Leave it as in-world theory
options.consequence: No change; the claim is marked as the author's hypothesis. Canon and the texts continue to disagree.

findings.recommendation: Instrument. It matches Mu-jin's own card, lets the canon failure mode supply the plot's harm, and leaves the Heresiology's "charged records" true as records held at the site.
findings.correction: The doc_claim leaves out that Vol III already denies storage. docx:112 opens "The Wellspring of Anamnesis does not store memories. This is the central misunderstanding", and Corrant:251 says it "does not hold souls. It holds the harmonic record of experience." The live contradiction is narrower than stated: Vol I wiki:117 ("holds memory… nothing… is erased") and Corrant:207 and :211 ("storage system") against Vol III's "keeps the record of what souls were committed to" and canon's "instrument, not the miracle". Codex support for the Instrument option: Master Glyph Index [EchoS] Echo-Scar ("Permanently burns a traumatic event into a location's Essence", Anamnesis primary) and [Sed] Sediment ("Reads the geological record of a site") both put the record in the place, with Anamnesis working on it. The question and recommendation stand.
findings.verify_evidence: Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md:63-66. Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:73, :76. True-canon FOW.md:1089. Magical Categories:184-188. Heresiology:171. Kwon Mu-jin.md:48. Vol III docx:112, :136. Corrant:207, :211, :251. Wiki Vol I:117. Codex Glyph Index [EchoS], [Sed], [Ma].

findings.topic: "The forty-ninth": numbering the Wellsprings
findings.doc_claim: Vol III docx:372 and wiki Vol III:199: "Mortalis — the forty-ninth, dissolution and terminus".
findings.canon: Canon never numbers the Sixty. The Lists sheet is alphabetical (Mortalis is 34th, row 35). FOW V's page order puts Mortalis 41st. Neither gives 49. Silas card:14 corrected a roman-numeral Wellspring list on exactly this ground: "the numbering does not correspond to anything in the register." R5-A (pack-05-five.yaml:26-31) keeps the skeleton "exactly as it is".
findings.why_it_matters: An ordinal in a canonical-sounding text invites a numbered list of all sixty that does not exist.
findings.question: The Codex calls Mortalis "the forty-ninth" Wellspring, but canon never numbers them. Keep a number?

options.label: Drop it
options.consequence: Write "one of the sixty" instead. No canon impact, and it follows the Silas precedent.

options.label: Keep it as an old archival number
options.consequence: Framed in-world as an older codex's count, not the Measurewrights' order. It adds texture but invites the question of what the other 59 numbers are.

options.label: Number all sixty
options.consequence: This is new canon that has to go through the Lists sheet and FOW, with a large blast radius for a one-word flourish.

findings.recommendation: Drop it. Canon has no numbering and has already struck one invented numbering.
findings.verify_evidence: The Lists sheet Wellspring column is alphabetical, with Mortalis in row 35 (34th). In FOW V page order Mortalis is 41st: Caloria 10 + Fulguria 6 + Vectoria 8 + Spatium 3 + Materia 9, then Anima Spirare, Verdantia, Benediction, Rebirthine, Mortalis (FOW V:98). Silas Briarend Wytherm III · Gravebinder.md:14 has the quoted line. pack-05-five.yaml:26-31. Vol III docx:372 and wiki Vol III:199 verified.

findings.topic: Minor Wellspring usages in the Necrocursica (three items merged)
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:81: "Each Wellspring is simultaneously a principle, an operation, and a presence." Necrocursica:277: "Ascensio, Fixatio, or Benediction — the constructive-alignment Wellsprings". Necrocursica:177: the chain "ends with Mortalis itself — the Wellspring inscribed as the final boundary".
findings.canon: Alchemetrica:23 says "eight of them" double as operations, not all sixty. Eight Families:29 defines a Wellspring as "a standing current in the Aether that carries a fixed law", and :39 says "A glyph is a boundary condition." Ascensio, Fixatio and Benediction are canonical but belong to three different Families: Vectoria, Materia and Vitalia (FOW V:61,81,96). Canon has no "constructive-alignment" grouping. The Master Glyph Index has no Mortalis glyph; its death and passage glyphs carry other Primary Wellsprings ([Au] Death: Somnalis; [Ob] Obol: Oblation).
findings.why_it_matters: These are small, but each one puts a claim about the Wellsprings into Malphas's mouth that canon contradicts.
findings.mechanical_fix: Necrocursica:81: change to "Some of the sixty are at once a principle and an alchemical operation"; the exact count follows ws-01. The operation list in the same line follows ws-01 and ws-03. Necrocursica:277: drop "the constructive-alignment Wellsprings" and present them as three currents from three Families. Necrocursica:177: a chain cannot end in a Wellspring; choosing the closing glyph goes to the Glyphica seam.
findings.correction: The fixes for :81 and :277 stand. For :177, the Glyphica seam should get two canon facts the finding leaves out. First, Alchemetrica:138 says the Sealing Turning draws "heavily on Fixatio's chains", so canon's sealing current is Fixatio, not Mortalis. Second, the only Mortalis-primary working in the Codex is the Spell Index row "The Still Gate's Mercy", built from [Au] Death + [Vor] Return. The Glyph Index has no glyph with Mortalis as Primary Wellspring; [Rt] Return lists Mortalis only as attested, with no primary. A natural canon close for the Category Three chain is therefore Fixatio-sealed, with a Mortalis boundary expressed through [Au]/[Vor]. That choice still belongs to the Glyphica seam.
findings.verify_evidence: Necrocursica:81, :177, :277. Alchemetrica:23 and :138. Eight Families:29 and :39. FOW V:61, :81, :96. A wiki grep found no "constructive-alignment" grouping anywhere. Codex Glyph Index: [Au] Death primary Somnalis; [Ob] Obol primary Oblation; [Rt] Return has no primary and attests Mortalis and Somnalis. Spell Index: "The Still Gate's Mercy".

findings.topic: Canon housekeeping outside the five texts (two items merged)
findings.doc_claim: Malphas card:107: "Pyraeon is attested as a Wellspring in the Thunn-Gorr sheet."
findings.canon: Pyraeon is one of the Sixty, in Caloria (FOW V:40; Lists sheet row 46). Separately, the Lists sheet spells "Monlithion" (row 34), while FOW V:85 and Eight Families:31 spell "Monolithion", so build/codex.py check 37 would flag the correct spelling. Neither discrepancy is in CONFLICTS.md.
findings.why_it_matters: The card undersells a canonical Wellspring. The typo on the Lists sheet will trip the vocabulary check on any converted text that names Monolithion.
findings.mechanical_fix: On Malphas card:107, write "Pyraeon is one of the Sixty (Caloria)". Log the Lists-sheet spelling "Monlithion" in CONFLICTS.md; do not edit the workbook from this audit.
findings.correction: Two claims are wrong. (1) Check 37 would not flag "Monolithion". Its unknown-word test only catches coinages matching COINAGE (build/codex.py:21), which requires endings in atio, antia, orath, ivale, thrae, ilithe or aeon, and "Monolithion" matches none. (2) "Monlithion" is not a lone Lists-sheet typo. The whole Master Codex uses it: Lists row 34, Glyph Index [Inr] Inertial (primary) and [Vt] Vector, and Spell Index "Inertial Chorus". FOW V:85 and Eight Families:31 spell it "Monolithion". That is a Codex-against-FOW spelling split, and RULINGS.md:318-321 ("FOW/Codex names win") cannot settle it because FOW and the Codex are the two sides. No converted text names this Wellspring, so it is out of seam: log it in CONFLICTS.md and route it on. The Malphas:107 fix is harmless, but "undersells" overstates it: the card's point is that the academy's name is a coincidence, and it does call Pyraeon a Wellspring.
findings.verify_evidence: build/codex.py:21 (COINAGE regex) and :92-103 (the check). Codex scan: Lists row 34 "Monlithion"; Glyph Index [Inr] primary Monlithion; [Vt] attested Monlithion; Spell Index "Inertial Chorus" primary Monlithion. FOW V:85. Eight Families:31. Malphas · Ferment of Stars.md:107. FOW V:40. Lists row 46 Pyraeon. A scan of the five texts plus the meta page found no Monolithion or Monlithion. grep of CONFLICTS.md and RULINGS.md: no row for it.

findings.topic: Names already consistent with the Sixty
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:137 names Luminalis and Tenebra; Necrocursica:277 names Ascensio, Fixatio and Benediction; Corrant:19 names Judicium; Vol II docx:161-169 names Dissolution. Vol III docx:50: "primary Wellspring is Mortalis but whose secondary is Anamnesis". Malphas card:51-54: Dissolution (Limina), Mortalis (Vitalia), Solfatara (Caloria), Nihiloth (Limina).
findings.canon: All of these are on the Lists sheet, and their FOW V Families match: Luminalis, Fulguria (:52); Tenebra, Limina (:124); Judicium, Fulguria (:48); Ascensio, Vectoria (:61); Fixatio, Materia (:81); Benediction, Vitalia (:96); Dissolution, Limina (:123); Mortalis, Vitalia (:98); Anamnesis, Limina (:122); Solfatara, Caloria (:37); Nihiloth, Limina (:127). Alchemetrica's Coagulatio, Transmutatio (Spatium, :72), Materia Primordia (Materia, :83) and Fixatio are canonical, as is the Heresiology's Catharsis (Caloria, :41). The Primary and Secondary Wellspring columns come from the Codex Spell Index. "Wellspring Communion" fits the Sage Arts' "Terrain-anchored Wellspring communion" (FOW V:167). None of the five texts assigns a Family, so they contain no Family errors.
findings.why_it_matters: This tells the questionnaire what needs no question: these names can be converted unchanged.
findings.correction: Remove Vol II docx:161-169 from the list of consistent Wellspring usages. Those lines use Dissolution as the second Great Work stage ("Dissolution Perverted, or the Corruption of Submission"), not as the Limina current. Whether a stage name doubles as a current is the open ws-01 and ws-02 question, so those lines are not settled. The rest is confirmed. Drop the sentence "The Primary and Secondary Wellspring columns come from the Codex Spell Index"; it does not apply to Vol III docx:50, which is prose.
findings.verify_evidence: Necrocursica:137 and :277. Corrant:19. Vol III docx:50. Vol II docx:161-169, read as stage and Corruption text. Malphas card:51-54. FOW V:37, :41, :48, :52, :61, :72, :81-83, :96, :98, :122-124, :127. A scan of all five texts against the Lists sheet found only Anamnesis, Mortalis, Judicium, Dissolution, Ascensio, Sublimatio, Luminalis, Tenebra, Benediction and Fixatio.

missed.topic: "Anamnetic fabric": a cosmic memory medium that canon does not have
missed.detail: The texts repeatedly treat Anamnesis as a Continuum-wide fabric or record into which the dead dissolve and from which Traces are drawn. Necrocursica:85 says Mortalis governs dissolution "back into the Anamnetic fabric of the Continuum"; see also :357 and :397. Vol III uses "Anamnetic fabric" at docx:112, :136, :204 and :248, plus wiki Vol III:82 and :104. It also coins "Anamnetic activation", "Anamnetic record" and "Anamnetic practice" (docx:122, :180, :284, :314, :350, :402). Canon never uses the adjective "Anamnetic" and has no Continuum-wide memory medium. Canon's nearest equivalents: records live in objects and places (Limina:64, "Objects genuinely store their history"), a location's record is its Mnemata (Veil:73; Magical Categories:184-188), and the cosmic ledger of lived experience belongs to Maelor, per the Codex Pantheon Sylorin row ("Maelor (Memory) — keeps the ledger of all lived experience"). This is separate from ws-08 because it puts a cosmology claim in Malphas's own voice, and it changes where Mortalis sends the dead.
missed.evidence: A grep of the five texts found "Anamnetic" 25 times in total (Necrocursica 4, Vol III docx 14, wiki Vol III 6, plus titles). A wiki-wide grep outside the Alftian Codex folder found 0 hits. Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md:64. Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:73. Master Codex Pantheon, Sylorin row, Bonds & Alignments.
missed.question: The texts speak of an "Anamnetic fabric": a world-wide memory record the dead dissolve into. Canon keeps records in places and objects (their Mnemata, the memory imprint a place holds) and gives the cosmic ledger to the Archon Maelor. What should the rewritten texts call it? Options: (A) Recast to canon. The dead leave Mnemata in the places they touched, and the world-ledger is Maelor's; drop "Anamnetic fabric". This has no canon cost but changes Necrocursica:85's account of death. (B) Keep "Anamnetic fabric" as a scholar's term the author glosses as the sum of all sites' Mnemata. This keeps the prose, adds one in-world coinage, and needs a gloss on first use. (C) Make it canon: a Continuum-wide record read through Anamnesis. This is new cosmology that must pass R18-2's absence check, and it collides with Maelor's ledger. Recommendation: A, or B if the prose rhythm matters. Both keep canon intact, and A pairs with the Instrument answer to ws-08.

missed.topic: Three alchemical sequences coexist; the texts use only the seven-stage Great Work
missed.detail: Canon has three alchemical sequences: the Four Operations (Alchemetrica:96-104), the seven-stage Great Work (Heresiology:44; Lexicon:70; Derivation of Practice:122) and the Twelve Turnings (Alchemetrica:108-140). The Turnings include putrefaction, cibation, sublimation and congelation. Several cards were corrected for treating Putrefactio, Cibation, Solution, Sublimation or Fermentation as Wellsprings (Silas:14, Karasaki:14, Iskaron Thalnaris:161, Kytheris:15-17, Morphaene:17). This is precedent that stage and turning names are "Great Work operations, not currents", which bears directly on ws-01 option A. The auditor cites Karasaki, Silas and Vorynth only as Calcination-is-a-Wellspring evidence and misses that these same correction notes classify the other stage names as non-currents.

seams.title: Death, residues, impression-bodies
seams.summary: Canon already has its own account of death, and neither source list of residues matches it. wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md says the Soul Crystal comes apart into three products: the Echo, the Temperance Residue and the Name-record. The Temperance Residue follows a nine-day clock that the Class IV trade and the funeral rites are built on. The Codex, the meta page and the Corrant Papers all credit the Necrocursica with a three-residue list (Harmonic Imprint, Sympathetic Bond Trace, Parunic Echo), but the Necrocursica itself gives a different four (Corporeal Residue, Aetheric Shell, Nospheric Echo, Volitional Trace). The seven residues can mostly be mapped onto the Crystal layers through the Crossing, Attraction Force and Mnemata (memory stored in places). The Sympathetic Bond Trace is already implied by canon's bonds that survive death. The Volitional Trace is not implied by Obsession Force; it survives only as an unnamed idea in the Heresiology's Anamnesis row. Canon already uses the dead as material through Class IV identity-shaped carry and Threshold products, and it already has the word "impression-body", but nothing says how one is built; Vocatia summoning on an alchemical vessel is the closest fit. Malphas is a lich because his Crossing never finished, not because he came back. That makes "resurrection is impossible, not merely unauthorised" the only framing that agrees with both R60-04 and the Crossing.

findings.topic: Two incompatible residue lists, both credited to the Necrocursica
findings.doc_claim: Codex Vol II (docx extract:99): Noxinus "described the three categories of Aetheric residue": Harmonic Imprint, Sympathetic Bond Trace, Parunic Echo; repeated in wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:58 ("Three residue categories, from the Necrocursica") and Corrant Papers:57, :171. The Necrocursica itself (:93) lists "The four canonical residue categories, now formalized ... through the collaborative work of De Raits, Thom, and Trismegistus": Corporeal Residue, Aetheric Shell, Nospheric Echo, Volitional Trace (:97-111). Only the Volitional Trace appears in both lists. The chronology also breaks: Vis reads the Necrocursica partway through the Codex (Codex II docx:189), yet the Necrocursica credits Vis with its own list.
findings.canon: Canon has a third account: "The Crystal does not depart. It comes apart — into three products" (wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:22). They are: the Echo (memory, habit, voiceprint), which goes to the Soul Plane within hours; the Temperance Residue, which diffuses through the body back into the Wellspring over nine days; and the Name-record, which is filed permanently in the Archive of Names (wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:26-34, :42-59). None of the seven named residues appears in canon. 'Nospheric' occurs once and is undefined ("Nospheric intrusion", wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/IV. The Eight Primaries and the Sixty-Four Sub-Stats (Part Twelve).md:91). In canon, 'residue' also means the trace left by a working, not by a death (Aetheric Residue, wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:40; "The Residue Position", wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:77).
findings.why_it_matters: Three documents credit the Necrocursica with a list it does not contain, and neither list matches the Crossing. Whichever list survives becomes the vocabulary for every Mortalis scene, forensic reading and impression-body in the converted texts.
findings.question: The texts disagree on what a dead person leaves behind, and canon (the Crossing: three things part at death) has a third answer. Which list should the converted documents use?

options.label: Keep both lists, one for each time window
options.consequence: The Necrocursica's four become the Accord's forensic list for the first nine days after death, which is what an investigator reads at a death scene (its Category One). The Codex's three become what is still left in the world after the nine days: a place-imprint, the mourner's bond and the name. That is exactly what a reconstruction two years after the death (Codex II docx:27) could draw on. The Necrocursica gains a short section on the after-window three, which makes the Codex and Corrant citations true. The Crossing's nine-day window becomes the hinge between the two lists.

options.label: Replace both with canon's three products plus the Trace as a disputed fourth
options.consequence: This is the tightest canon fit, and 'three known products plus a disputed fourth' mirrors the Codex's premise. But the Temperance Residue is gone by day nine (wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:54), so the Codex's commission two years after the death has nothing to build from. The Sympathetic Bond Trace, which Codex III (docx:276) and the Corrant plot depend on, also disappears.

options.label: Unify on the Codex three plus the Trace
options.consequence: The citations become true with small edits. The Necrocursica loses its forensic chapter and its Tria Prima of the dead, which is built on the Corporeal Residue.

options.label: Unify on the Necrocursica four
options.consequence: The Codex, the meta page and the Corrant Papers all need rewriting, and the bond residue that Madeleine Ault's commission works through loses its name.

findings.recommendation: Keep both lists, one per window. This keeps both authors' material, anchors each list in canon through the Crossing's window, and explains the chronology: the Codex quotes the after-window chapter, and the four-part forensic scheme is the later Accord formalisation that the Necrocursica itself describes. It also invents the fewest new mechanics.
findings.correction: The conflict is real and the question belongs to Isaac, but three details need fixing. (1) The chronology citation is wrong. Vis reads the Necrocursica at Codex II docx:89-99, not :189. Line :187 is De Raits's letter, and it makes the conflict sharper: the fourth residue is 'Not described by Noxinus'. Yet the Necrocursica as it stands contains the fourth (:109) and cross-references Codex I-III and the Corrant Papers (:109, :497). So the text we have postdates the trilogy. Add an option, or a note under option 1: the extant Necrocursica is a later 'formalized' edition (its own word at :93), which the Codex's three-list quotes from the earlier version. This matters for the Malphas attribution. (2) Corrant Papers:171 uses the Codex list but does not credit the Necrocursica; only :57 does. (3) In option 1, the Parunic Echo is not 'the name'. It is 'the glyph-trace inscribed in the fabric of the world by any Temperance-active practitioner' (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:84), so the post-window three are place-imprint, bond and working-trace. Also, Veil.md:77 does not support 'residue means a working, not a death': the Residue Position counts Echo Beasts and Drift as residue, and the Crossing itself says 'Temperance residue' and 'pooled residue'. Recommendation stands.

Not described by Noxinus.'); Necrocursica :93, :109, :497; Corrant Papers :57, :171; wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:82-84; wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:58; wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:22-34, :126; wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:77

findings.topic: The seven residues mapped onto the three Soul Crystal layers
findings.doc_claim: Harmonic Imprint: "frequency-signature left in the ambient Aether of the places a person inhabited" (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:82). Sympathetic Bond Trace: "does not sever entirely at death but attenuates" (:83). Parunic Echo: "glyph-trace inscribed in the fabric of the world" (:84). Corporeal Residue: "The physical body" (Necrocursica:97). Aetheric Shell: "the Aether Shell ... now detached from its generating core" (:101). Nospheric Echo: "a residue of the mind having been there" (:105). Volitional Trace: "where the soul was pointing at the moment of its severance" (:109).
findings.canon:
The layers are defined in wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:28-30 and :58-60. The Essence Core sits on the Soul Plane and holds "identity, memory, and Traits". The Aether Shell sits on the Material Plane and "Converts inner truth into outward force". The Attraction Layer sits on the Plane of Fate and holds "bonds, Domains, and Wellspring harmonizations"; its failure state is Obsession Force. In life, all three radiate: "the Shell's Resonant Tone, the Core's emotional frequency, the Attraction Layer's recognition hum" (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:78). Canon never says which layer each Crossing product comes from (wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:26-34).

Derived mapping:
(1) Harmonic Imprint: the Shell's tone and the Core's frequency, laid into a place over a lifetime. This is canon's Aetheric Residue (Core Vocabulary:40) or Mnemata read through Anamnesis (The Veil.md:73; wiki/The Magic System/The Magical Categories — Unified Taxonom.md:184-188). It outlasts the Crossing.
(2) Nospheric Echo: its place-imprint half duplicates (1). Its personality and possession half is the Crossing's Echo (Core layer: "memory, habit, voiceprint", The Crossing.md:28) held out of the Soul Plane, which is a Lawful Echo, Class II (The Crossing.md:112; wiki/The War Cycle/The Rites.md:86). Its Resonance Lock is canon's Melancholic Erosion, "the taking-on of memories that are not yours" (The Crossing.md:101).
(3) Sympathetic Bond Trace: Attraction Layer, and already implied by canon. Attraction Force lets "spiritual relations survive time, death" (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/V. Wellsprings, Attraction and Obsession, Magic Integration (Parts Thirteen–Fifteen).md:142). Axis "sustains the Spirit Bond between two Crystals" (:143). The clean form carries "bonds past death" (:147); the Obsession Force form preserves them "in broken, predatory form" (:157). On the mourner's side it shows as Soul Drift, where the bereaved's "Attraction Layer is reaching for an anchor that has moved" (The Crossing.md:113). Threads are "not severed ... extended" (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Crossing and the Making of the God Hand.md:75). Under R26-1, a co-donor's death that the survivors will not release "curdles into Obsession Force" (rules/doc-shared-soul-crystal-mechanism.yaml:88-93).
(4) Parunic Echo: no canon match. The nearest is the Name-record, filed permanently in the Archive (The Crossing.md:30, :57-59). For Stage XIII and above, the nearest is the law the Continuum registers (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VI. The Sixteen Temperance Stages (Part Sixteen).md:71).
(5) Corporeal Residue: the Shell's physical body. Traits are laid into flesh: "A body is a Trait record and a corpse is a better one" (Core Vocabulary:107). The body carries the Temperance Residue for nine days (The Crossing.md:52).
(6) Aetheric Shell: the Aether Shell. Canon is silent on what happens to the Shell at death. What it reveals forensically is the Temperance Residue's "every seated carry and harmonisation" (The Crossing.md:29) plus the Essence Signature (Core Vocabulary:46).
(7) Volitional Trace: no canon category. Obsession Force does not imply it, because Obsession belongs to a living person who cannot let go (Core Vocabulary:48; FoW V:150-158). See ws-04.
findings.why_it_matters: Isaac asked for alchemy to connect to the Soul Crystal. The converted texts need one reference so that every residue a scene names lands on a Crystal layer and a Crossing product. The mapping also shows that two of the seven residues are one thing (Harmonic Imprint and the place-half of the Nospheric Echo).
findings.question: Canon never says which part of the Soul Crystal each of the three things that part at death comes from. Should the converted texts use the mapping above, and should that mapping become canon?

options.label: Use it in the texts and have it ruled canon
options.consequence: The Crossing gains a line tying the Echo to the Essence Core, the Temperance Residue to the Core's refinement carried through the body, and the Name-record and bonds to the Attraction Layer. Every later Mortalis document inherits it. It goes through CONFLICTS.md and the docket as a new row.

options.label: Use it in the texts only, as in-world scholarship
options.consequence: The documents read coherently against canon without amending the Crossing, and the gap between products and layers stays open in canon.

options.label: No mapping; keep each author's own vocabulary
options.consequence: This is the least work, but the residues float free of the Soul Crystal, which is the opposite of what the conversion is for.

findings.recommendation: Use the mapping in the texts only for now, and log the products-to-layers gap as a CONFLICTS.md row so the docket can decide whether to raise it to canon. In whichever list survives ws-01, fold the Harmonic Imprint and the Nospheric Echo's place-half into one residue. Rename the Parunic Echo: R51-11 reserves 'echo' for its WOTR sense (rules/doc-vocabulary-law-2026-09-26.yaml:273-285), and a glyph-trace is not the Crossing's Echo.
findings.correction: Two parts of the mapping are wrong, and the claim that canon never says which layer each product comes from is overstated. (a) Canon half-answers it. The Temperance Residue carries 'every seated carry and harmonisation' (Crossing.md:29), and harmonisations sit in the Attraction Layer (Core Vocabulary:60). So option 1's line 'Temperance Residue to the Core's refinement' is wrong: the Residue straddles the Core, where Stages and Tempering Coherence live (R26-1), and the Attraction Layer, which holds harmonisations, and it diffuses through the Shell's flesh. The Echo ('memory', Crossing:28) maps to the Core by the Core's own definition (Core Vocabulary:58). (b) The Parunic Echo does have a canon match: Aetheric Residue, 'Traces left behind by an Essence working. A permanent ... change to the location' (Core Vocabulary:40). A glyph-trace left by a practitioner's workings is exactly that, and it is a better fit than the Name-record. The Harmonic Imprint (the frequency of inhabited places) fits Mnemata/Anamnesis location records (Veil:73; Taxonomy:184-188), not Aetheric Residue. Swap those two lines. The rest checks out: Sympathetic Bond Trace = Attraction Layer (FoW V:142, :143, :147, :157; Crossing:113; God Hand:75; R26-1), Nospheric Echo = held Echo (Lawful Echo, Crossing:112), and Obsession Force does not imply the Volitional Trace. The R51-11 renaming advice stands, and the question remains Isaac's.
findings.verify_evidence: wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:28-30; wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:40, :58-60; wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:73, :78; wiki/The Magic System/The Magical Categories — Unified Taxonom.md:184-188; FoW V (Parts Thirteen–Fifteen).md:142-158; rules/doc-shared-soul-crystal-mechanism.yaml:80-93; rules/doc-vocabulary-law-2026-09-26.yaml:273-285; wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:84

findings.topic: How long a dead body holds anything
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:97: the Corporeal Residue lasts for a period "ranging from hours in Stage I practitioners to years in Stage VII and above". Necrocursica:133: "The bones of a Stage VII practitioner are, for Aetheric purposes, still doing something, decades after death."
findings.canon: The residue "diffuses through the body, which remains its medium"; "Nine days is the figure. It varies with Stage" (wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:52-53). "On the ninth day ... what remains is meat" (:54). The Stage variance "has never been characterised" (:137). The Goblinoid ninth-day rendering is lawful because by then the body is "material and nothing else" (wiki/The War Cycle/The Rites.md:56). Class IV must be rendered fast, and "a body that has been argued over is a body worth nothing" (The Crossing.md:73). After the window, the body keeps only an inert physical record of its Traits (wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:107).
findings.why_it_matters: If a high-Stage corpse stayed active for years, rendering houses could harvest old graves of powerful practitioners, and the Goblinoid ninth-day rite would become an interception for those bodies. It would also contradict the nine-day law the whole Class IV trade is built on.
findings.question: The Necrocursica says a powerful practitioner's body stays metaphysically active for years or even decades; canon says nine days and then 'meat'. Which holds?

options.label: Conform to nine days
options.consequence: Stage stretches or shrinks the window by days, not years, which canon's Stage variance allows (The Crossing.md:53). After the window, the bones are an inert Trait record that a reader can study and nothing more. The Tria Prima 'Salt' still works as the anchor during the window, and the Class IV trade and the Rites stay intact.

options.label: Keep years and decades as the author's own heterodox claim
options.consequence: The Necrocursica claims to measure the variance that canon calls unmeasured. If that is true in-world, old high-Stage graves become Class IV stock and a grave-robbing economy appears, and the Standing Index, the Bench and the Rites would all need amending.

options.label: Keep it as an in-world error flagged by a later annotator
options.consequence: The text stays nearly as it is, but it needs a gloss so readers do not take it as mechanics.

findings.recommendation: Conform to nine days. Recast "still doing something decades after death" as the Trait record left in the bone (Core Vocabulary:107). That keeps the same eerie effect without any active Essence.
findings.correction: The conflict is real, but canon is not one-sided, and option 1's claim that bones are 'inert ... and nothing more' is contradicted by the material ledger. Canon grades a Crystal-bearer's remains as Class IV long after burial: Gravetide Ink is 'Class III, IV on practitioner grave-dirt' (Alchemical Index:68), and Granite-Bone Binding Mortar is 'IV on a donor who bore a Crystal' (:63). The Standing Index grades anything that 'carried a Soul Crystal' as identity-shaped carry (:29). Trait tissue is 'laid down in flesh: mineral into bone' (Core Vocabulary:107), and 'a Trait is precisely what survives a melt' (Alchemical Index:111). So recast the recommendation: the Temperance Residue is gone by day nine (Crossing:54), but Trait tissue in the bone keeps Class IV carry indefinitely. On that basis, 'still doing something decades after death' can stay as passive Trait-tissue carry, not active Essence. That is not inert. Also, the Rites citation is :57, not :56. This canon-internal tension (Crossing 'meat' against Class IV grave-dirt) should also be recorded as a CONFLICTS row.
findings.verify_evidence: wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:52-54, :73, :137; wiki/The War Cycle/The Rites.md:57 ('material and nothing else'); wiki/The Master Material Ledger/The Alchemical Index.md:63, :68, :111; wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Standing Index.md:29; wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:107; Necrocursica :97, :133

findings.topic: What the Volitional Trace is in Soul Crystal terms, and where it lives
findings.doc_claim: Codex II (docx extract:261): "Not unfulfilled desire, which leaves only the Sympathetic Bond Trace. Unfulfilled decision." Codex III (docx extract:114): "the record of the commitment that was never completed", held in the Anamnesis Wellspring. Corrant Papers:251: Anamnesis "holds the harmonic record of experience". Necrocursica:109 says the Trace is "the only one that retains agency"; Necrocursica:357 says an unpursued Trace "sits in the Anamnetic fabric".
findings.canon:
No canon category has this name. The closest is the Heresiology's Anamnesis row: "preserves not mere memory but charged records of lived commitment" and "A trace may complete a decision" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:171). The Temperance Residue returns to "the Wellspring" (wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:32, :52), which gives a route into Anamnesis. The Plane of Fate "Records ... bonds, oaths, grudges" (wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:29), and a vow becomes a standing law in the Essence Core (Heresiology:238).

Obsession Force is the living's inversion of Attraction: it forms when a practitioner "cannot release judgment, lineage, memory" (Core Vocabulary:48) and shows as "Locking onto one target with impossible persistence" (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/V. Wellsprings, Attraction and Obsession, Magic Integration (Parts Thirteen–Fifteen).md:157). The Trace's single-minded pursuit looks like that, but Obsession belongs to a living Crystal, not to the dead.

Adjacent canon: the Verdance Reclamation Draught carries a donor's "unfinished obsessions" across as Traits (wiki/The Master Material Ledger/The Alchemical Index.md:111), and the Ketsumyōgan's Grief Trace reads "their last thought's resonance" (wiki/The Disciplines/The Ketsumyōgan — The Binding Fate Eye.md:92).
findings.why_it_matters: The Trace drives all three Codex volumes, the Necrocursica's Category III and the Corrant Papers. Without a home in the Crystal layers and the Crossing, the central mechanism of all five documents stays disconnected from the magic system.
findings.question: Where does an unfinished decision go when the person who made it dies? Choose the Trace's home in canon terms.

options.label: An Attraction Layer commitment that rides the Temperance Residue into the Wellspring and lodges in Anamnesis
options.consequence: This matches the Heresiology's Anamnesis row, Codex III's 260-year-old Genesio Trace and the Corrant letter. The nine-day window becomes the moment a Trace is laid down: Mortalis governs the passage, and Anamnesis holds the record. No canon page has to change.

options.label: A fourth product of the Crossing
options.consequence: The Codex's 'fourth residue' becomes literally a fourth thing that parts at death, one the Research Division's three-product Crossing does not know about. That is strong in-world drama, but it leaves the Crossing page incomplete unless the idea is framed as a disputed thesis.

options.label: Obsession Force on the side of the dead
options.consequence: This is the simplest reuse of existing canon, but it erases the Codex's distinction between desire and decision and makes every Trace predatory (FoW V:157). The Codex's benign completion, with the Genesio hollow going quiet and 'finished', contradicts that.

findings.recommendation: The Attraction Layer commitment lodged in Anamnesis. Keep the 'fourth product' idea as the Codex authors' in-world argument, while the Accord files the Trace under Anamnesis. Also describe the Necrocursica's First and Seventh Corruptions (a practitioner's Attraction Layer taken over by a dead person's aim) as Obsession Force, which is the Attraction Layer's canon failure state (Core Vocabulary:60).
findings.correction: The status (absent_from_canon) and the question are right. Option 1 has a gap: the Temperance Residue returns to 'the Wellspring concerned' (Crossing.md:53), meaning the Wellsprings the person was repaying, not Anamnesis generally. 'Rides the Residue into the Wellspring and lodges in Anamnesis' therefore works only if the deceased harmonised Anamnesis, or died within reach of an Anamnesis node (the Genesio hollow is one, Codex III docx:194-206), or canon gains a line routing all Traces to Anamnesis. State that condition in the option. The Plane of Fate recording 'oaths' (Core Vocabulary:29) supports an Attraction Layer home; a vow held as standing law in the Essence Core (Heresiology:238) is a competing Core home that could be offered as a further option. Minor: Codex III puts Anamnesis holding Traces at docx:116, not :114, and adds that they 'attenuate over time'.
findings.verify_evidence: wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:32, :52-53; wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:171, :238; wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:29, :48, :60; scratchpad Codex III docx:112-116, :194-210, :248; Corrant Papers:251; Necrocursica:357

findings.topic: The Necrocursica names a 'Volitional Layer' that is not a Soul Crystal layer
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:201: the Trace "uses the nearest available directed-intent architecture — which is the practitioner's own Volitional Layer — as a template".
findings.canon: The Soul Crystal has three layers: Essence Core, Aether Shell and Attraction Layer (wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:56-60; wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/V. Wellsprings, Attraction and Obsession, Magic Integration (Parts Thirteen–Fifteen).md:22). The same Necrocursica sentence opens by naming the practitioner's "Attraction Layer". The text elsewhere routes completion through "the practitioner's Attraction Layer as a resonance guide" (Necrocursica:173) and has the Seventh Corruption co-opt the "Attraction Layer" (:357).
findings.why_it_matters: It invents a fourth Crystal layer at the point where the text explains its most important failure mode.
findings.mechanical_fix: Necrocursica:201: replace "the practitioner's own Volitional Layer" with "the practitioner's own Attraction Layer". The phrase "volitional architecture" at :205 and :357 can stay, because it describes something rather than naming a layer.
findings.verify_evidence: Necrocursica:201 opens with 'differentiated their Attraction Layer from the Trace' and then says 'the practitioner's own Volitional Layer'. The phrase occurs only there. :173 says 'Attraction Layer as a resonance guide'; :205 and :357 say 'volitional architecture'. The three canon layers are at wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:56-60 and FoW V:22.

findings.topic: The Codex says the Soul Crystal 'moves toward its next station' at death
findings.doc_claim: Codex II (docx extract:31) and wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:30: "the slow metaphysical withdrawal of Essence from the Soul Crystal as it moves toward its next station".
findings.canon: "The Crystal does not depart. It comes apart — into three products with three destinations" (wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:22), and death means "the three products have parted and are now the property of three different laws" (:36). The rest of the Codex passage agrees with canon: Mortalis treats death as a process (wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vitalia — Biochemistry.md:49), and Mortalis "does not preserve the dead in storage. It governs passage" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:170).
findings.why_it_matters: This is the Codex's only direct statement about what death does to the Crystal, and it describes a single travelling soul where canon describes one that comes apart.
findings.mechanical_fix: In both the docx-derived text and the wiki condensation, replace "as it moves toward its next station" with "as its lattice comes apart and each part goes to its own law". Keep the rest of the sentence and the river-not-reservoir line, which are consistent with canon.
findings.verify_evidence: Codex II docx:31 and wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:30 read 'as it moves toward its next station'. wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:22, :36 say 'does not depart. It comes apart'. The Vitalia — Biochemistry.md:49 and Heresiology:170 citations are accurate.

findings.topic: Which canon system can build an impression-body, and how canon already uses the dead as material
findings.doc_claim: Codex II (docx extract:101): the method is to "gather the echo from the ambient Aether, call the resonance-thread back through the sympathetic bond" and reweave the Parunic Echo. Necrocursica:173: Category III must "create a material substrate capable of holding the impression", sealed with Mortalis (:177). Paracelsus built it at his bench, and it "lasted eleven days" (Corrant Papers:133; Codex III docx:276).
findings.canon:
"Impression-body" is already a canon word (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:66, :170), but no page says how one is built. Necromancy "does not summon them, which is a different discipline governed elsewhere" (wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:87).

The Spirit Summoning Arts (wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Summoning Arts.md):
- Summoning is "a three-plane crossing": a vessel built from Aether, identity supplied by a Core, and existence recognised through Attraction (:13).
- Vocatia contacts an existing presence such as "an ancestral resonance" (:32).
- Arts builds the vessel from "alchemical constructs" (:47).
- Binding Arts fix "how long it may persist, and under what conditions it must dissolve" (:48), which is the Necrocursica's Sealing.
- Tier III summons (Vocatia, Animatria and Arts, Stage IX–XI) last "Minutes to hours" (:65), Tier V lasts indefinitely (:67), and material anchors extend duration (:70).

The Soul Plane archive keeps significant souls' patterns "held permanently, without loss" (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Crossing and the Making of the God Hand.md:77).

The dead as material:
- Class IV Crystal Draw, where "Carry is identity-shaped", has three lawful sources (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Standing Index.md:29, :51-59), plus unlawful draw from extraction and engine work (:63-65).
- Class IV is "the interception of that repayment" to the Wellspring inside the nine days (The Crossing.md:66-73).
- At Heavy carry, "the origin governs" the working (Standing Index:48).
- Threshold products seed a Crystal's melt with a donor's law (:91-95).
- The Refraction Draught: "The donor's own way of seeing comes with it" (:141).
- Gravemark Ink's donor carry "behaves as though it has an opinion about who is buried" (:127).
- Corpus Marrow Salts use ground Soul Crystal shavings, and the housing "takes the donor's set" (wiki/The Master Material Ledger/The Alchemical Index.md:90).
- The Verdance Reclamation Draught transfers a donor's Traits (:111).
- Gravetide Ink: "a contract with the dead is a working whose remaining term outlives the signer" (:68).
- Echo-Bloom Incense reads a site's Residue and destroys it in the reading (:32); Stillgate Ash grounds "A body's residual field after death" (:46).
- The Bench's Attribution "names the class. It does not name the source" (wiki/Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/The Bench of Attribution.md:68).
- In the Heresiology's Conjunction section, Class IV cost falls on "the donor, who is by definition dead" (Heresiology:107), and "Every Threshold product above T5 answers the third question with an absent, powerless, dead and unnamed party" (:109).
findings.why_it_matters: The impression-body is the central event of Codex II and III and of the Corrant Papers. Converting it needs a named canon system, a Stage gate and a duration; otherwise the alchemy stays disconnected from the magic system Isaac wants it tied to.
findings.question: Which part of canon actually builds an impression-body?

options.label: A Vocatia summons on an alchemical vessel, sealed with a Binding
options.consequence: Every part is already canon. The mourner's bond is the Vocatia channel, the place-imprint is the Mnemata substrate, Paracelsus's bench builds the Arts vessel, and the Mortalis Sealing is a Binding Arts chain. It needs Stage IX or above for an independent Spirit Forge body (Spirit Summoning Arts:49), and either a material anchor or Tier V to reach eleven days.

options.label: An alchemical Draft made from high-carry Class IV remains of the deceased
options.consequence: Canon's carry already transfers identity into material, so this works mechanically. But it only works inside the nine days, and the Codex commission came two years after the death (Codex II docx:27). The Bench also cannot certify whose remains are used, so impression-bodies become a Class IV black-market product.

options.label: A cast working (Glyphica and Mnemata) with no vessel
options.consequence: The cheapest option, but it produces a reading or an apparition, not a body that walks rooms and finds documents, so the Corrant plot breaks.

options.label: Both: summoning as the method, Class IV as optional vessel material
options.consequence: This touches the most canon, and the Heresiology's three Conjunction questions then apply directly to every commission.

findings.recommendation: The Vocatia summons on an alchemical vessel. Reserve the Class IV vessel from the combined option for Vaughaus Thom's regional scaling, which fits the Heresiology's Conjunction and Fermentation cases. The texts should also acknowledge that the Soul Plane archive does keep significant patterns (God Hand:77), so the Codex's 'impression, not retrieval' is a claim about Mortalis and the ordinary dead, not about the archive.
findings.correction: The inventory is accurate, but two consequences are wrong. (1) Option 1's Stage gate: an alchemical vessel is a material anchor, and the Spirit Summoning Arts page gates 'material-anchored constructs' at Stage VII (Refraction), keeping Stage IX for independent Spirit Forge bodies (SSA:49). Give both gates and let Isaac pick which kind of body it is. The 'material anchors extend duration' line is in the Tier II context (SSA:70); Forge vessels being 'more durable' (SSA:47) is the better support for eleven days. (2) Option 2 does not work 'only inside the nine days'. Canon grades a Crystal-bearer's bone-ash and grave-dirt as Class IV with no nine-day limit (Alchemical Index:63, :68), and R54-42 makes blood from a living Crystal-bearer Class IV, so a mourner's own blood is lawful Class IV material. The Heresiology's 'donor, who is by definition dead' (:107) is partly overtaken by R54-42. Minor: for Vaughaus Thom's regional scaling, the closer canon hook is the Anamnesis row's 'regional saturation through repeated retrieval' (Heresiology:171). The recommendation stands.
