findings.topic: Impression-body lifespan and timing: eleven days or fourteen
findings.doc_claim: Corrant Papers:133: "It lasted eleven days." Corrant Papers:139: "On the fourteenth day, the entity ... asked to be taken to a room". Codex III (docx extract:276): "the impression-body would have eleven days of sufficient coherence". Corrant Papers:171 says Madeleine Ault completed her decision "eleven days after she died", but Codex II (docx extract:27) says the wife "died of the lung-sickness two years ago".
findings.canon: Canon is silent on impression-body duration. The timing matters for canon, though: work inside the nine days touches the Temperance Residue and Class IV law (wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:52-54, :66-73), and work two years later cannot.
findings.why_it_matters: The fourteenth-day line contradicts two statements of eleven days, and 'eleven days after she died' would put the commission inside the Crossing's window, which changes which residues and which laws apply.
findings.mechanical_fix: Corrant Papers:139: change "On the fourteenth day" to "On the eleventh day". Corrant Papers:171: change "eleven days after she died" to "eleven days after the commission", matching Codex II docx:27.
findings.correction: The internal conflict is real, but the fix misses a line. Corrant Papers:135 reads 'On the eleventh day, it began to change', and :139 has the entity asking for the room on the fourteenth. Changing only :139 to 'eleventh' packs the change, the request, the room and the ending into one day and leaves an awkward duplicate. Minimal consistent fix: :139 'On the fourteenth day' becomes 'Before the eleventh day was out'. That keeps 'It lasted eleven days' (:133) and Codex III docx:276 ('eleven days of sufficient coherence to locate and direct him') unchanged. :171 'eleven days after she died' becomes 'eleven days after the commission', matching Codex II docx:27 ('died of the lung-sickness two years ago'). It stays mechanical.
findings.verify_evidence: scratchpad Corrant Papers:133, :135, :139, :147, :171; Codex III docx:276; Codex II docx:27

findings.topic: Full resurrection (Category IV), the rule that death is permanent, and a lich as the author
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:181: "Full resurrection is Category Four. Category Four is not authorized." Necrocursica:497: "Do not file a Category IV application. They will not approve it". The Codex Vol I Aphorism (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:85): "to raise the dead required a diminishment of the living". Necrocursica:5: the author's hand wound "has not yet fully healed", which implies a living body. Necrocursica:305: "if I describe the echoes of the dead as more interesting than the people in the room, treat this document as a confession".
findings.canon:
R60-04 (live): "Death is almost always permanent; the only exceptions are liches, the undead and their kind" (rules/doc-combat-society-politics-law-2026-09-26.yaml:77-85). Necromancy "does not raise the dead, which is not a thing that can be done" (wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:87); it "holds the three products together" (:88). Liches and the other undead are "holes in the Crossing" (wiki/The Bestiary/The Undying and the Constructs.md:14). The Heresiology treats resurrection claims as heresy markers: "Counterfeit resurrection claims" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:170) and "Counterfeit resurrections assembled from grief, trace, and desire" (:98).

Malphas:
- "The founder is a lich" (wiki/Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/The Mother.md:23).
- He "did not die in the conventional sense and did not seek out a lichdom" (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Malphas · Ferment of Stars.md:26).
- His Essence Core is "Split-housed", with the remainder in the Golden Remnant (:42, :97).
- His Crystal is "Overgrown, held there permanently rather than resolving" (:44).
- Mortalis became "Co-primary as of the Becoming" (:54).
- The Remnant is explicitly not a phylactery-style win condition (:99), unlike the Lich page's "immortal unless the phylactery itself is destroyed" (wiki/Aberrations/Lich.md:21).
- The Mother cult seeks "Malphas's path to undeath" (rules/doc-combat-society-politics-law-2026-09-26.yaml:519).

In Crossing terms, Malphas is a standing hole in the Crossing: his Core never went to the Soul Plane and his Temperance is not diffusing, so the Wellsprings he owes are never repaid (The Crossing.md:92, :97). The Heresiology's Case II, "The Compelled Author and the Necromantic Manuscript" (Heresiology:209), describes the Necrocursica under its previous author.
findings.why_it_matters: The author of the text that forbids resurrection is himself the setting's main exception to permanent death. How the text frames Category IV decides whether resurrection is a live plot device, whether the Mother reads the book as scripture, and whether Malphas is honest in it.
findings.question: How should Malphas's Necrocursica treat full resurrection, and was he still alive when he wrote it?

options.label: Impossible, not just forbidden; written while he was alive
options.consequence: This matches the Crossing (:87) and R60-04: the crossed do not come back, and only those who never crossed stay. Category IV survives as the Accord's category for refusing fraudulent applications. The healing-hand detail and the Fifth Corruption confession stay, and they read as a self-diagnosis he later fulfilled at the Becoming. The text describes lichdom as refusing to cross, not as coming back.

options.label: Impossible; written after the Becoming
options.consequence: The author writes from inside the exception. The hand-wound line has to go, because a lich's hand does not heal. The book becomes a lich's account of why he is not resurrected: sharper, but less of a warning.

options.label: Keep 'possible but unauthorised'
options.consequence: This contradicts the Crossing (:87). Resurrection becomes a live mechanic the table can pursue, with R60-04's 'almost always' as the only cover, and the Heresiology's doctrine against counterfeit resurrection loses force.

options.label: Deliberately misleading: forbidden on paper, but his own path in fact
options.consequence: This fits the Mother as a cult of his undeath (R60-24). It makes the Necrocursica unreliable in-world, so every mechanic in it needs a canon check before use.

findings.recommendation:
Impossible, not just forbidden, and written while he was alive. It is the only framing consistent with both R60-04 and the Crossing, it keeps the text a warning, and it turns his later lichdom into dramatic irony rather than hypocrisy.

In the same pass:
- Necrocursica:181 says "Category Four is the subject of every case study in Chapter the Third", which is untrue of its own Chapter Three: all seven cases are Category I–III failures. Reword it to say those cases were heading toward Category IV.
- Recast the Vol I Aphorism's "power of revivification" as holding the three products together at the Wellspring's expense (The Crossing.md:97).
- The Heresiology's 'Compelled Author' case needs re-reading with Malphas as the author; the compulsion could be whatever answered him at Invocation (Malphas card:21-22). That question belongs to the attribution seam.
findings.correction: The canon cited is accurate and the question is Isaac's, but four things need correcting. (1) 'Counterfeit resurrections assembled from grief, trace, and desire' is Heresiology:97 (Conjunction Perverted), not :98. (2) 'Malphas is a lich because his Crossing never finished' is an inference, not canon. The card says he 'did not die in the ordinary sense' and his Core 'had a second home built for it' (Malphas card:26, :136), so his Crossing may never have begun. Bestiary:14 lists liches among holes in the Crossing, but the unrepaid-Wellspring consequences (Crossing:92, :97) are written for necromantic constructs. Label this as derived. (3) The recommendation says option 1 is 'the only framing consistent with both R60-04 and the Crossing'. That is false: option 2 (impossible, written after the Becoming) is equally consistent. The reason to prefer option 1 is dramatic (a warning, irony instead of hypocrisy), not a matter of canon. Option 1 must also meet a timing constraint: the Necrocursica cites Codex I-III and the Corrant Papers (:109, :497), so a living Malphas must write after Kwon Mu-jin's trilogy; this seam did not check that against Malphas's timeline. (4) On re-reading the Heresiology: canon already places Malphas under Fermentation Perverted ('describes him without naming him', Malphas card:45, :142). Case II's 'talented writer, pulled by access and manipulated through need' (Heresiology:209) describes Noxinus's circumstances (Codex II docx:85). Refer both to the attribution seam. The 'every case study in Chapter the Third' error is confirmed: Chapter Three contains no Category IV case.

findings.topic: The Necrocursica's revenant against canon's undead and hauntings
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:141: when the residues interact "with an active Aetheric Shell ... the result is what the older literature calls a revenant", and :141 adds "This is not a supernatural phenomenon". Necrocursica:145: "The revenant does not think. It is not the deceased." The Tria Prima of the dead: Trace as Sulphur, Corporeal Residue as Salt, Nospheric Echo as Mercury (:129-137).
findings.canon:
Canon's walking dead are bodies whose three products "have been prevented from parting" (wiki/The Bestiary/The Undying and the Constructs.md:14). Necromancy does this deliberately (wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:88), but undead can also arise from "corrupted Wellspring energies ... or abyssal taint" (Undying:24) or wander "as restless spirits seeking vengeance or purpose" (:49). A held construct "may retain skill and preference" and is not a person (The Crossing.md:92-93), which agrees with the Necrocursica's "does not think".

Hauntings: "A haunting is a charge with no path" (wiki/The Master Material Ledger/The Alchemical Index.md:46). A body "denied the nine days at a site the Wellspring cannot reach" produces "a lawful Echo with nowhere to go" (wiki/The War Cycle/The Rites.md:86). On battlefields, residue that cannot diffuse "pools" into Echo Beasts and the Hollow (The Crossing.md:126).

The Tria Prima is not canon anywhere except the Codex itself (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:68, :158).
findings.why_it_matters: The Necrocursica adds a natural undead mechanism (residues plus an active Shell) that sits beside canon's stalled-Crossing account without using it. Scenes with ghosts or revenants need a single rule.
findings.question: Can a revenant happen on its own, without a necromancer, and if so, by what canon mechanism?

options.label: A Crossing that stalls on its own
options.consequence: A revenant is what happens when a body spends its nine days at a site the Wellspring cannot reach (Rites:86) or on a saturated battlefield (The Crossing.md:126). It is the same state necromancy keeps up on purpose, except that nobody maintains it, and it fades when the residue finally diffuses. The Necrocursica's 'not supernatural' line becomes literally the Crossing's account, and the Tria Prima stays as the author's alchemical gloss.

options.label: Only through necromancy
options.consequence: This is the strictest reading of the Crossing (:88). The Necrocursica's natural revenant is cut, and the Bestiary's taint-born undead need a different explanation.

options.label: Keep the Necrocursica's mechanism as written
options.consequence: That creates a third undead mechanism alongside necromancy and taint, resting on an 'active Aetheric Shell' that canon never defines.

findings.recommendation: A Crossing that stalls on its own. The Tria Prima of the dead depends on the choice in ws-01 and on the alchemy seam's ruling on whether the Tria Prima is canon.
findings.verify_evidence: Necrocursica:129-145. wiki/The Bestiary/The Undying and the Constructs.md:14, :24, :49; wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:88, :92-93, :126; wiki/The War Cycle/The Rites.md:86; wiki/The Master Material Ledger/The Alchemical Index.md:46. The Tria Prima appears only in the Codex and its meta page (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:68, :158; wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:42).

findings.topic: Two different lists of 'Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions' (flagged for the Heresiology seam)
findings.doc_claim: The Necrocursica's seven are all Mortalis failures: Mirror Trace, Nospheric Resonance Lock, Incomplete Sealing, Aetheric Bleed, Inversion, Nomenclature and Completion (Necrocursica:199-339). The Codex uses the Heresiology's list instead: "The Separation Perverted" (Codex II docx:239). The Necrocursica's Sixth tells readers to treat residues as "data sources" (:329), and :413 says "The residues of the dead are data."
findings.canon: Canon's Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions are the inverted stages of the Great Work (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:23, :57-139). Canon warns against conflating seven-item lists: "Two documents, two sevens, no relation beyond the number" (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Crossing and the Making of the God Hand.md:71). The Heresiology's Distillation Perverted names "Reduction of persons to residue classes without accompanying ethical commentary" and "Necromantic manuals whose warnings survive only as footnotes" (Heresiology:126-127). Canon's Mortalis failure, "Equilibration", in which practitioners "cool toward it without noticing" (wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vitalia — Biochemistry.md:51), corresponds to the Necrocursica's Aetheric Bleed and Inversion. Mirror Trace corresponds to Dissolution Perverted, dissolving "into another will" (Heresiology:73).
findings.why_it_matters: The Necrocursica's catalogue of what dealing with the dead does to practitioners carries the Heresiology's exact title for a different list, which is the confusion canon already calls the standard error. With Malphas as author, the Heresiology's Distillation warning also reads as a diagnosis of a text that calls the dead 'data'.
findings.question: The Necrocursica uses the Heresiology's exact name for a different list of seven. Should it be renamed, or mapped onto the Heresiology's list?

options.label: Rename the Necrocursica's seven (for example 'the Seven Mortalis Injuries') and have each cite its Heresiology parent
options.consequence: This removes the clash canon already warns about, and each injury gains a canon parent: for example, Mirror Trace under Dissolution Perverted, and Inversion under Mortalis Equilibration.

options.label: Keep the name and make the Necrocursica the Mortalis chapter of the Heresiology's seven
options.consequence: This needs a one-to-one mapping that does not exist, because seven Mortalis failures do not line up with seven Great Work stages, and it creates the very conflation canon warns against.

options.label: Keep as is
options.consequence: Two canon-facing lists of seven share one title.

findings.recommendation: Rename the Necrocursica's seven and have each cite its Heresiology parent. Hand the full mapping to the alchemy and Heresiology seam, since this seam only touches it where the corruptions concern the dead.
findings.verify_evidence: Necrocursica:3, :199-339; Codex II docx:239, :284; wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:23, :57, :73, :126-127; wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Crossing and the Making of the God Hand.md:71; wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vitalia — Biochemistry.md:51

missed.topic: Canon disagrees with itself on whether a practitioner's remains stay live after nine days
missed.detail: The Crossing says that on the ninth day 'what remains is meat' and that Class IV must be rendered fast. The material ledger, though, grades practitioner grave-dirt and a Crystal-bearer's bone-ash as Class IV with no time limit, and Trait tissue survives in bone. This is a canon-internal tension, and per CLAUDE.md it should be a CONFLICTS row. It decides whether the Necrocursica's 'bones ... decades after death' can stand, and whether an impression-body can be built from old remains.
missed.evidence: wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:54, :73; wiki/The War Cycle/The Rites.md:57; wiki/The Master Material Ledger/The Alchemical Index.md:63, :68, :111; wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:107; wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Standing Index.md:29
missed.question: After nine days, does a powerful practitioner's body still hold anything usable? Options: (a) Only Trait tissue (traits laid into bone), which is still Class IV 'carry', meaning identity-shaped material, but carries no active residue. The ledger stays as it is, the Crossing's 'meat' is read as 'no Temperance', and the Necrocursica's decades-old bones survive as passive carry. (b) Nothing: the ledger's grave-dirt and bone-ash Class IV entries must be restricted to the nine-day window. That is a bigger change and breaks Gravetide Ink and Granite-Bone Mortar. Recommend (a).

missed.topic: The Necrocursica we have postdates the Codex trilogy it is supposed to precede
missed.detail: In Codex II, Vis reads the Necrocursica and De Raits says the fourth residue is 'Not described by Noxinus'. The extant Necrocursica, however, lists the Volitional Trace as 'now formalized' by De Raits, Thom and Trismegistus, and cross-references Codex I-III and the Corrant Papers. So the Codex quotes a Necrocursica that cites the Codex. With Malphas as the new author, which edition he wrote, and when, also decides ws-09 ('written while alive').
missed.evidence: scratchpad Codex II docx:89-99, :187; Necrocursica:93, :109, :463 (Appendix II on its relationship to the trilogy), :497
missed.question: Is the Necrocursica one book or two editions? Options: (a) Two editions: an early one (three residues, the one quoted in the Codex) and a later formalised one (four residues, cites the trilogy). Both lists survive and the chronology is repaired, but Malphas must be placed at both dates. (b) One book, written after the trilogy: the Codex's citations of it must be rewritten. (c) One book, written before: strip its references to the trilogy and the Corrant Papers and its four-list credit. Recommend (a); it pairs with ws-01 option 1.

missed.topic: The texts call impression-body work 'necromancy', but canon defines necromancy narrowly
missed.detail: The Crossing defines necromancy as holding the three products together, and says summoning the dead is 'a different discipline governed elsewhere'. The Codex and the meta page call the impression 'what the necromantic tradition calls retrieval', and the Necrocursica is a 'Treatise on Cadaverous Alchemy'. A commission made two years after a death cannot be necromancy in the Crossing's sense. The Heresiology itself uses 'Necromantic Manuscript' and 'Necromantic manuals' loosely, so canon's own usage is mixed.
missed.evidence: wiki/The War Cycle/The Crossing.md:87-88; scratchpad Codex II docx:31; wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:57; Necrocursica:3; wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:127, :209
missed.question: Should the converted texts keep calling impression-body work 'necromantic'? Options: (a) Keep it as the in-world scholars' loose term, with a line in the Necrocursica noting that the Accord's legal sense is narrower. This matches the Heresiology's own loose usage. (b) Replace it with 'Mortalis' or summoning vocabulary throughout, which is the strictest canon fit but loses period flavour. Recommend (a).

seams.title: Great Work, Tria Prima, the three sevens
seams.summary: Most of this seam has never been connected rather than being contradicted. Canon has the Heresiology's seven stages and seven inversions, Alchemetrica's Four Operations, Twelve Turnings and four colour readings, and the sixteen Temperance Stages, but nothing links any of them to another. The Codex's claim that the Great Work "is" the Temperance path goes further than canon allows, because pure alchemists do the Great Work and cannot temper. Some things are plainly broken: "Sovereignty" is not a Stage, "Volitional Layer" is not a Crystal layer, the Necrocursica gives its seven Mortalis failures the Heresiology's exact name for a different seven, and "the Third Corruption" means three different things across the Codex and the Necrocursica. The new authors create two sharp problems. Kwon Mu-jin's card flaw is the opposite of the Non-Commitment the Codex author admits to in himself, and Malphas takes over canon's standing example of Submission while his card files him under Fermentation. The Tria Prima exists only inside the Codex; the strongest link on offer is the Crystal's three layers, through Alchemetrica's line that the crucible is a Soul Crystal analogue. Noticed outside this seam: Calcination and Distillation are named as Wellsprings but are not among the Sixty (gw-05), and wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:88-92 repeats lines 82-86 word for word.

findings.topic: Is the Great Work the Temperance path? (Vol I appendix, Vol II ch. 7)
findings.doc_claim: Codex Vol I appendix (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:159): "It describes the Temperance path itself, rendered in the language of material transformation." Vol II docx extract:149 sends the stages "Toward the Temperance Stages"; docx:273 calls the Work a "spiral... where each stage is revisited from a higher vantage."
findings.canon: Canon is silent on any match between a Great Work stage and a Temperance Stage. Temperance has sixteen Stages, described as structural reorganizations rather than achievements (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VI. The Sixteen Temperance Stages (Part Sixteen).md:14-15), in two seven-Stage phases: Inner Refinement I-VII (:17) and Outer Influence VIII-XIV (:47). "All true alchemy participates in the Sevenfold Great Work" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:23), and its stages are "disciplines imposed upon both matter and maker" (:45), "a method and a judgment" (:47). Alchemy needs no Soul Crystal (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:54). A pure alchemist is Class Ø and "does not temper and cannot"; he goes through the Weathering instead (Alchemetrica.md:80-82).
findings.why_it_matters: Read literally, the Vol I claim plus Heresiology:23 puts pure alchemists on a Temperance path that Alchemetrica:82 says they cannot walk. The same answer also decides where each corruption strikes in a practitioner's life, and gw-04 and gw-12 depend on it.
findings.question: Should the Great Work's seven stages (the old alchemical sequence from Calcination to Coagulation) correspond to the sixteen Temperance Stages (the ladder of the soul's growth), and if so, how?

options.label: A. Parallel, not identical
options.consequence: The Vol I line and the Vol II Stage sentence are rewritten so the Work is a discipline that runs alongside Temperance. This agrees with the Heresiology and leaves pure alchemists untouched. No new mechanics, and the weakest link to the system.

options.label: B. The double seven (the Codex's spiral)
options.consequence: The seven stages run once across Stages I-VII and again across VIII-XIV. The pairs line up at the crisis points: Splintering V with Fermentation; Dissonance XI with Conjunction, which puts Alchemetrica's 'most dangerous operation' (Alchemetrica.md:104) on the Temperance page's most dangerous Stage (VI:63); Invocation IX with Dissolution; Zenith XIV with Coagulation, read as the refusal to call anything final (VI:76). This is new canon, so it needs a ruling and a line on the Temperance page. The matter side stays open to pure alchemists; the maker side is Temperance.

options.label: C. In-world thesis only
options.consequence: Mu-jin argues it as his school's reading, following the rule that theories surface through characters who hold and argue them (rules/doc-writing-law-2026-09-26.yaml:563). No rule is needed, and the page may show him wrong. The link to the system stays rhetorical.

findings.recommendation: B. It is the only option that ties the Work to a named mechanism. It uses the Temperance page's own two seven-Stage phases and the Codex's own 'spiral', and the Heresiology's split between matter and maker (:45) keeps pure alchemists lawful. If Isaac wants no new mechanics, fall back to C.
findings.correction: The canon citations hold (VI:14-15, :17, :47, :63; Heresiology:23, :45, :47; Alchemetrica:54, :80-82, :104). Two things need fixing. (1) Option C cites rules/doc-writing-law-2026-09-26.yaml:563 as a general rule that theories surface through characters. Line 563 is R48-24-4_THEORIES, whose verbatim (:572) covers only 'The Four Theories'. Option C should rest on R48-22-LENS_NAMES (:518) plus the Codex's in-world voice, not on R48-24. (2) Recommendation B says the split between matter and maker 'keeps pure alchemists lawful'. It does not. Heresiology:45 imposes the discipline on the maker of all true alchemy (:23), and Alchemetrica:82 says a Class Ø maker has no Temperance and undergoes the Weathering instead. Under B, a pure alchemist's maker-side stages would have no ladder to sit on. B has to carry an explicit clause: for Class Ø, the maker side of each stage is read on the Weathering (grain), not on a Temperance Stage. Otherwise B creates the exact contradiction this finding describes. The status and the question stay; B can stay the recommendation only with that clause.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-read wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:159; Vol II docx extract :149, :273; VI. The Sixteen Temperance Stages:14-15, :17, :37, :47, :63, :76; The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:23, :45, :47; Alchemetrica.md:54, :80-82, :104; rules/doc-writing-law-2026-09-26.yaml:518-527 (R48-22), :563-572 (R48-24, 'The Four Theories surface in scenes...').

findings.topic: 'Glory, Sovereignty, Zenith' named as Temperance Stages
findings.doc_claim: Vol II docx extract:149: "Toward the Temperance Stages that the Monastery describes as Glory, Sovereignty, Zenith." The wiki condensation drops this sentence (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:113).
findings.canon: Glory is Stage VI (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VI. The Sixteen Temperance Stages (Part Sixteen).md:39) and Zenith is Stage XIV (:73). No Stage is called Sovereignty; the full list is at :19-85. 'Sovereign' is a Soul Crystal developmental Tier covering Temperance IX-XII (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VIII. Traits, Soul Crystal Tiers, Domains (Parts Twenty–Twenty-Two).md:74), and Sovereignty is a Dominion Sub-Stat (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/IV. The Eight Primaries and the Sixty-Four Sub-Stats (Part Twelve).md:116).
findings.why_it_matters: The name blurs a Stage, a Crystal Tier and a Sub-Stat, which are three different ladders.
findings.mechanical_fix: If the sentence survives gw-01, replace 'Sovereignty' with a real Stage. The closest in sense is Principality, Stage XIII, whose entry says "They are legislating" (VI:71), giving 'Glory, Principality, Zenith' (VI, XIII, XIV). Do not add the sentence back to the wiki version with Sovereignty in it.
findings.correction: The core claim is right: there is no Stage called Sovereignty. Glory is VI (:39) and Zenith is XIV (:73). But 'Sovereign' names three canon ladders, not two. Besides the Soul Crystal Tier (VIII:74, Temperance IX-XII) and the Dominion Sub-Stat (IV:116), it is also Band III, Levels 201-300 (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/I. Levels, Experience and Stat Points (Parts One–Three).md:24). Mu-jin's own card lists 'Sovereign Crystal' as his Tier (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:45), so under the new author the slip reads as a Tier being confused with a Stage. The mechanical part is removing 'Sovereignty'. Choosing Principality as the replacement is an editorial pick and not the only one canon allows. The fix that stays neutral to canon is 'Glory and Zenith' (or 'Glory, Principality, Zenith' if a third name is wanted).
findings.verify_evidence: Vol II docx:149 confirmed; wiki Volume the Second.md:113 drops the sentence (confirmed). VI:39, :71, :73; VIII. Traits...md:74 ('Sovereign ... Temperance IX–XII'); IV. Eight Primaries...md:116; I. Levels...md:24 ('Band III — Sovereign, Levels 201 through 300'); Kwon Mu-jin.md:45.

findings.topic: Stage-word collisions in Codex Vol II (three minor items merged)
findings.doc_claim: Vol II docx:151 and wiki Volume the Second.md:118: "When the Hermetic Stage becomes a method rather than a path." docx:237 and wiki:183: "a Conviction Corrupted in the First stage". docx:67: a life "moved through the fourteen Temperance stages".
findings.canon: The Heresiology calls the lawful Work "a method and a judgment" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:47) and writes 'stages' in lower case (:23). Capitalised 'Stage' is the Temperance term (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VI. The Sixteen Temperance Stages (Part Sixteen).md:14), and Stage I is Murmuring (:19). A Stage is reached under pressure, not passed through by every life (:14). Fourteen Stages are canonical mortal progression, sixteen in all (:15).
findings.why_it_matters: As written, readers will take 'the First stage' as Temperance Stage I. They will also read as the corruption something the Heresiology treats as half of the lawful definition ('a method').
findings.mechanical_fix: (1) Change 'a method rather than a path' to 'a method without a judgment', to agree with Heresiology:47. (2) Change 'in the First stage' to 'in the first stage of the Work'. (3) Change 'moved through the fourteen Temperance stages' to 'moved through the Temperance Stages it reached'. Throughout the conversion, write lower-case 'stage' for the Great Work and keep capitalised 'Stage' for Temperance.
findings.verify_evidence: Vol II docx:151 ('a method rather than a path') and wiki Volume the Second.md:118; docx:237 and wiki:183 ('Conviction Corrupted in the First stage'); docx:67 ('moved through the fourteen Temperance stages'). Heresiology:47 ('a method and a judgment'), :44; VI:14-15 (Stages are reorganizations under pressure, 'not sequential achievements'; fourteen canonical mortal). The three wording fixes are editorial and do not need a ruling. Folding in 'Hermetic Stage' to lower-case 'stage' at docx:151 / wiki:118 is covered by the stated convention.

findings.topic: The Great Work's seven against Alchemetrica's Four Operations, Twelve Turnings and colour readings
findings.doc_claim: All three Codex volumes and the Necrocursica use only the Heresiology's order: "Calcination, Dissolution, Separation, Conjunction, Fermentation, Distillation, Coagulation" (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:113), and "The Monastery teaches Calcination first" (:141). None of them mentions Turnings or colours.
findings.canon: Canon has three schemes, each claiming to cover all alchemy, and nothing linking them. (1) The seven stages (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:23, :44). (2) The Four Operations, Coagulation, Distillation, Sublimation and Conjunction: "Every Draft ever entered in the Standing Index is one of four operations" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:98-104). (3) The Twelve Turnings (Alchemetrica.md:110-124). The orders clash: the Turnings put the Rot (putrefaction, 5) before the Wedding (conjunction, 6) (:116-117), and "A working that never blacks has not rotted and will not conjoin" (:149), while the Heresiology puts Conjunction before Fermentation (:44). No Turning is Distillation, and Sublimation is an Operation but not a stage. The colours are Blacking (putrefaction), Whitening (separation complete), Yellowing and Reddening (:147-154), yet the Parting Turning (:115) comes before the Rot. Coagulation, not Calcination, is the first operation an apprentice may run alone (:101). Canon never matches stages to Turnings, colours or Temperance.
findings.why_it_matters: The conversion is supposed to bring Codex alchemy into line with Alchemetrica. With no concordance, a writer has to pick an order without saying so, and the two canon pages will seem to contradict each other on the page.
findings.question: How should the seven stages relate to the workshop's Twelve Turnings and colour readings, given that the two disagree on whether rotting comes before or after joining?

options.label: A. Three registers with a concordance
options.consequence: The seven are the doctrinal order for matter and maker; the Four Operations are verb classes; the Turnings are the bench order. One table sets Burning beside Calcination, Taking beside Dissolution, Parting beside Separation, Rot beside Fermentation, Wedding beside Conjunction, menstruum and Rising beside Distillation, and Setting beside Coagulation. It pins the colours to Turnings and states that the bench rots before it weds while the doctrine joins before it ferments. No page is reordered, and the Monastery's 'Calcination first' and the bench's 'Coagulation first' both stand.

options.label: B. Reorder the seven to match the bench
options.consequence: Fermentation moves before Conjunction. This breaks the Heresiology's order, its diagnostic table (:267-275) and the Codex's numbering.

options.label: C. Reorder the Turnings to match the seven
options.consequence: This breaks Alchemetrica's colour logic ('never blacks... will not conjoin') and the six-to-nine-week Rot.

options.label: D. Leave them unconnected
options.consequence: No edits. The conversion cannot make the Codex's alchemy line up with the workshop, and readers meet two orders with no explanation.

findings.recommendation: A. It is the smallest change that makes both canon pages true at once. The stage/Turning difference also becomes a point of doctrine instead of an error, and it fits gw-01 B's split between matter and maker.
findings.correction: The claim that 'canon never matches stages to Turnings' is wrong. Alchemetrica's flowchart already glosses six Turnings with alchemical stage names: Burning = calcination, Taking = dissolution, Parting = separation, Rot = putrefaction, Wedding = conjunction, Rising = sublimation, Setting = congelation (Alchemetrica.md:113-120). Calcination, Dissolution, Separation, Conjunction and Coagulation (as congelation) therefore already have bench Turnings in canon. Only Fermentation and Distillation lack one. The summary's 'nothing links any of them' is also overstated: Alchemetrica's 'Heresy at the Bench' (:323-330) takes Fermentation, Distillation and Coagulation 'gone wrong' from the Heresiology onto the workbench. The order clash depends on reading the Rot as the Fermentation stage. Heresiology:113 calls lawful fermentation 'rot in service to transformation', which supports that reading, but canon never states it. Option A's concordance has two errors. (a) The 'menstruum' belongs to the Taking, i.e. dissolution (:114). (b) canon glosses the Rising as sublimation, which Alchemetrica keeps as its own Operation apart from Distillation (:102-103). Distillation has no bench Turning at all. Revised question for Isaac: is the Rot the Fermentation stage (if so, the bench rots before it weds while the doctrine weds before it ferments, and that has to be stated), and where does Distillation sit at the bench? Recommendation A still stands with those corrections.
findings.verify_evidence: Alchemetrica.md:98-104 (Four Operations; :101 Coagulation first an apprentice may run alone), :110-124 (Turnings, with stage glosses at :113-120), :149-154 (colours), :323-330 ('Heresy at the Bench'); Heresiology:44, :113, :267-275.

findings.topic: Calcination and Distillation are named as Wellsprings but are not among the Sixty
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica docx:81 treats them as Wellsprings: "Calcination burns away false structure. Dissolution unravels cohesion into base frequencies. Sublimatio elevates without intermediate states."
findings.canon: Alchemetrica lists eight Wellsprings that are also operations, Calcination and Distillation among them (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:23-33). The live rule R18-5-ALCHEMY_DOCTRINE_BINDING repeats this (rules/pack-18-eighteen.yaml:262-280). Cards list 'Calcination · Caloria' (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Ignatius Sanctus Sanctorum Arsenal · The Archpaladin.md:50) and Mu-jin's 'Distillatio' (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:48). But the register of sixty (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/V. Wellsprings, Attraction and Obsession, Magic Integration (Parts Thirteen–Fifteen).md:29-128) and the Caloria page (wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Caloria — Thermodynamics.md:19-82) have no Calcination or Distillation. There, Sublimare's analogue is fractional distillation (wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vectoria — Mechanics.md:47-52), while Alchemetrica.md:30 gives Sublimare the definition of sublimation. CONFLICTS.md has no row for this.
findings.why_it_matters: Alchemetrica anchors four of the seven stages to Wellsprings, and two of those anchors are not on the list of sixty. Any stage-to-Wellspring or stage-to-Stage link (gw-01) would rest on currents that do not exist there. Recorded here so it is not lost; it belongs to the Wellspring seam.
findings.question: Are Calcination and Distillation Wellsprings (currents a soul harmonises with) or only operations (things done to matter)?

options.label: A. Operations only
options.consequence: Alchemetrica:23-33 and the cards are corrected. R18-5 needs a new ruling, because its verbatim cannot change. Mu-jin loses two harmonisations.

options.label: B. Alchemical names for Wellsprings already in the register
options.consequence: Distillation becomes the trade name for Sublimare (fractional distillation), and Calcination names a Caloria entry still to be chosen. Alchemetrica gets an alias column, and its Sublimare row moves to Sublimatio. The count of sixty, R18-5 and the cards' wording all stand.

options.label: C. Add both to the register
options.consequence: Breaks 'the Sixty' everywhere it appears.

findings.recommendation: Settle this in the Wellspring seam. Lean B: it keeps the count, the ratified rule and the cards, and the Vectoria page already describes Sublimare as distillation.
findings.correction: The substance is right. The Sixty have no Calcination and no Distillation or Distillatio (V. Wellsprings...md:29-128; only Sublimatio :62, Sublimare :63, Coagulatio :82, Dissolution :123 and similar are present). Alchemetrica:26, :29 and R18-5's verbatim name them as Wellsprings. CONFLICTS.md and RULINGS.md have no row. But the doc_claim quote at Necrocursica docx:81 names Calcination, Dissolution and Sublimatio, not Distillation. The Necrocursica uses Distillation as a Wellspring-alignment at docx:213 ('Distillation-aligned separation'). Mu-jin's card lists Coagulatio, Distillatio, 'Fixation' and Calcination (Kwon Mu-jin.md:48), and 'Fixation' is not the register's Fixatio (V:81) either. Docx:81's 'Sublimatio elevates without intermediate states' actually agrees with Vectoria ('Where Sublimatio skips a phase', Vectoria — Mechanics.md:50). The page off the register is Alchemetrica, which gives that definition to Sublimare (:30, :103). Option B leaves out a consequence: making Distillation the trade name for Sublimare folds two of Alchemetrica's Four Operations, Distillation mirrors Distillatio (:102) and Sublimation mirrors Sublimare (:103), onto one Wellspring. This belongs to the Wellspring seam, as the auditor says.
findings.verify_evidence: Necrocursica docx:81, :213; Alchemetrica.md:23-33, :102-103; rules/pack-18-eighteen.yaml:262-280 (R18-5, status live in out/rules.resolved.json); V. Wellsprings...md:62-63, :81-83, :123; Vectoria — Mechanics.md:47-52; Kwon Mu-jin.md:48; Ignatius...md:50; grep of CONFLICTS.md and RULINGS.md for Calcination/Distillati returns nothing.

findings.topic: Tria Prima (Sulphur, Salt, Mercury) and Spagyria
findings.doc_claim: Codex Vol I: Spagyria separates compounds into "Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury, the triadic grammar of material refinement" (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:68), and the appendix says it "Requires formal documentation" (:158). Necrocursica docx:129-137 maps Sulphur to the Volitional Trace ("the active principle"), Salt to the Corporeal Residue and Mercury to the Nospheric Echo, and leaves its fourth residue, the Aetheric Shell (docx:101), outside the triad.
findings.canon: Absent outside the Codex. The Tria Prima appears only in the Codex and its meta page (wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:42). Spagyria survives only as a profession, 'licensed spagyrists' (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:14). No page maps the triad to anything in the system. Canon does contain triads it could map to. (1) The Crystal's three layers: Essence Core on the Soul Plane, Aether Shell on the Material Plane, Attraction Layer on the Fate Plane (wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:55-60); the Core decides how the soul burns and the Layer how people and memory bind (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/V. Wellsprings, Attraction and Obsession, Magic Integration (Parts Thirteen–Fifteen).md:22). (2) The doctrine line: reagents are the nouns, the Wellspring the verb, Glyphica the grammar (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:15; rules/pack-18-eighteen.yaml:262-280). Alchemetrica also says "The crucible is a Soul Crystal analogue" (Alchemetrica.md:36). Real-world names may appear as lenses (rules/doc-writing-law-2026-09-26.yaml:518).
findings.why_it_matters: This is the most direct way to make Codex alchemy speak the Crystal's language. The Necrocursica already commits to one mapping, which may not survive whichever choice is made.
findings.question: Should Sulphur, Salt and Mercury (Paracelsus's three principles: the active, the fixed and the mediating) correspond to something in the magic system?

options.label: A. Crystal layers, matched by plane
options.consequence: Sulphur is the Essence Core, Salt the Aether Shell, Mercury the Attraction Layer. Spagyria becomes medicine that works layer by layer, and the crucible-as-Crystal line becomes the bridge. The Necrocursica's Sulphur = Volitional Trace becomes awkward, because the Necrocursica itself ties the Trace to the Attraction Layer (docx:201, 213, 357). Its triad either stays its author's 'modified' reading or is remapped.

options.label: B. Crystal layers, matched by behaviour
options.consequence: Sulphur is the Core (burns), Mercury the Shell (moves through and around the body), Salt the Attraction Layer (binds), following V:22's wording. The plane pattern breaks, since Salt ends up on the Fate Plane.

options.label: C. The doctrine line
options.consequence: Salt is the reagent, Sulphur the Wellspring, Mercury Glyphica. This ties Spagyria to Draft-craft and the Standing Index but says nothing about the Crystal. The Necrocursica's triad stays an analogy.

options.label: D. Lens only
options.consequence: The Tria Prima stays Furveus's pharmacological grammar and the Necrocursica author's analogy. No new canon, and no link to the system at this point.

findings.recommendation: A. Keep the Necrocursica's residue triad as an openly 'modified' in-world reading, using the text's own word (docx:125), and name the Aetheric Shell residue as Salt's companion. Alchemetrica:36 already makes the vessel a Crystal analogue, and the Emerald Principle (Volume the First.md:157) is about correspondence between scales, so a triad that holds at both scales is the cheapest strong link. Matching by plane keeps it teachable.
findings.verify_evidence: The Tria Prima is absent outside the Codex, its meta page (wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:42) and 'licensed spagyrists' (Heresiology:14), confirmed by grep across wiki/. Codex Vol I:68, :158; Necrocursica docx:97 (Corporeal Residue = Salt), :101 (Aetheric Shell residue = 'the Aether Shell of the Soul Crystal system'), :125 ('a modified Tria Prima'), :129, :133, :137, :201, :213, :357. Core Vocabulary.md:55-60; V:22; Alchemetrica:15, :36; Volume the First.md:157. One note on option A: matched by plane, the Necrocursica's own Aetheric Shell residue (docx:101) lands on Salt next to the Corporeal Residue, which strengthens the recommendation. See the missed item on residue names.

findings.topic: 'Volitional Layer' in the Necrocursica's First Corruption
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica docx:201: the Trace uses "the practitioner's own Volitional Layer — as a template for completion rather than as a guide."
findings.canon: The Crystal has three layers, Essence Core, Aether Shell and Attraction Layer (wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:55-60); there is no Volitional Layer. The same case's resolution separates "the practitioner's Attraction Layer" (Necrocursica docx:213). Obsession Force, which is fixation, is the Attraction Layer's failure state (Core Vocabulary.md:60).
findings.why_it_matters: A fourth Crystal layer would enter canon through a corruption case study.
findings.mechanical_fix: At Necrocursica docx:201, change 'Volitional Layer' to 'Attraction Layer'.
findings.verify_evidence: Necrocursica docx:201 ('the practitioner's own Volitional Layer'); the same sentence and docx:213 use 'Attraction Layer'. Core Vocabulary.md:55-60 lists three layers only. grep of wiki/ finds 'Volitional Layer' nowhere. Docx:357's lower-case 'volitional architecture' is not a layer name and can stay.

findings.topic: Three sevens: the Heresiology's, the Necrocursica's and the Hataraki's
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica title (docx:3): "the Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions Arising from the Misapplication of Mortalis Law". Chapter 3 numbers the Mirror Trace, Nospheric Resonance Lock, Incomplete Sealing, Aetheric Bleed, Inversion, Nomenclature and Completion (docx:199-357). Codex Vol II coins the same name for the Heresiology's seven, "in the language I am beginning to develop for this volume" (docx:153).
findings.canon: The Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions are the seven Great Work inversions, Conviction through Tyrannous Finality (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:57-143, :267-275). The meta page calls the Heresiology "the finished version of a book this man left open" (wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:64). A tribunal grade is built on them: Grade III, "One or more of the Seven Corruptions is visibly active" (Heresiology:184). The Crossing page already sets apart another seven, the corruptions of the Seven Works of Hataraki: "Two documents, two sevens, no relation beyond the number" (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Crossing and the Making of the God Hand.md:71-73). Canon says nothing of the Necrocursica's seven. The chronology is also tangled: in the Codex the Necrocursica is already written before Vis coins the term (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:86, :165), yet the surviving Necrocursica cites all three Codex volumes (docx:109, 465).
findings.why_it_matters: Same name, same count, different contents. A Grade III charge cannot say which seven it means, the Crossing page's 'two sevens' becomes false, and it cannot be settled who coined the name (Mu-jin or Malphas under the new attribution).
findings.question: The Necrocursica's seven Mortalis failures carry the exact name of the Heresiology's seven moral inversions. Which list keeps the name 'Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions'?

options.label: A. Rename the Necrocursica's seven
options.consequence: The name belongs only to the Heresiology and Codex seven. The Necrocursica's title, its chapter 3 heading and Appendix II's cross-reference are rewritten. Grade III and the Crossing note stay true.

options.label: B. Nest them
options.consequence: Each Mortalis failure is recast as the Mortalis form of one Great Work inversion, for example Mirror Trace under Instrumental Union and Nomenclature under Conviction. That leaves a single seven, but it is a heavy rewrite, and the pairs are forced for the failures the Necrocursica itself calls mechanical.

options.label: C. Same name, collision made part of the world
options.consequence: Both lists keep the name, and an archivist's note like the one at Crossing:73 explains the mix-up. Grade III must then specify 'the Seven of the Heresiology', and the Crossing note must say three sevens.

findings.recommendation: A. One candidate name is 'the Seven Unmoorings', from the text's own verb (docx:425). Each failure can optionally name the Heresiology inversion that usually drives it. This is the smallest edit and keeps Grade III and the Crossing note true. The Necrocursica itself says the first four are mechanical failures rather than inversions (docx:285), so a one-to-one nesting (B) would bend them.
findings.correction: The collision is real and correctly laid out, but the chronology evidence is misread. Vol II docx:153 ('in the language I am beginning to develop for this volume') coins the names 'Calcination Perverted / the Corruption of Conviction', not 'Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions'. That term already appears in Codex Vol I:165 ('the subject of the forthcoming volume'), and Vol II docx:147 says 'I have referred previously to the Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions'. The real tangle: the Codex's author uses the term in Vol I while saying of the Necrocursica 'I have not read it' (Vol I:162). The Necrocursica, already written by Vol I:86, carries the same term in its title (docx:3) and chapter 3 heading (docx:187), yet cites all three Codex volumes (docx:109, :465). Who coined the name stays open under the new attribution. The question, options and recommendation A stand.
findings.verify_evidence: Necrocursica docx:3, :187, :199-357 (headings at :199, :219, :239, :263, :283, :311, :339), :285, :425, :465; Vol II docx:145-153; Volume the First.md:86, :162, :165; Heresiology:57-143, :184, :267-275; Crossing and the Making of the God Hand.md:71-73; Alftian Codex meta:64.

findings.topic: 'The Third Corruption' means three different things
findings.doc_claim: Vol II, Separation Perverted: "Clarity without commitment is not the completion of the stage. It is the stage's inversion." (docx:265). Vol III: "as I described it in the second volume, is the inversion of the scholar's purpose" (docx:382), and "the inversion that insists on understanding everything except itself" (docx:30). Necrocursica Appendix II: "The Third Corruption as described in the Codex is the Cacodaemon of Nomenclature, partially" (docx:469). The Necrocursica's own Third is the Incomplete Sealing (docx:239).
findings.canon: Separation Perverted, the Corruption of Non-Commitment, is "Perfect diagnosis, absent intervention", with the practitioner retreating into analysis (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:84-85). It is third in order (:44, :271). Nomenclature has no canon entry. Tat "Asks the question that produces the Third Corruption's definition" (wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:48).
findings.why_it_matters: Vol III claims to follow Vol II while shifting the meaning from 'will not act' to 'cannot see himself'. The Necrocursica then reassigns it to a corruption from a different list. A reader of 'the Third' gets a different thing in each document.
findings.question: What is the Third Corruption, and should the texts refer to corruptions by number at all?

options.label: A. The Heresiology's definition, cited by name
options.consequence: Non-Commitment everywhere. Vol III's lines are reworded as what Non-Commitment feels like from inside (the safe distance of analysis). Appendix II's Nomenclature claim is cut or kept as its author's disputed reading. Names replace ordinals. Small edits, consistent result.

options.label: B. Vol III's self-blindness is a separate corruption outside the seven
options.consequence: Appendix II's 'general scholarly Corruption' becomes canon as an eighth. This breaks the seven and adds new doctrine.

options.label: C. Keep the drift as character
options.consequence: The author's definition changes as he does, and Appendix II is Malphas needling him. This adds texture but needs an editorial note, and readers get two definitions.

findings.recommendation: A. The Heresiology is canon's finished version (meta:64), and naming corruptions instead of numbering them also clears the collision with the Necrocursica's numbering in gw-08.
findings.correction: The auditor overstates the drift inside the Codex. Vol III's 'scholar who describes error as though from safety' (Vol III docx:30, :234, :382) falls within the Heresiology's own Non-Commitment: 'exempts themselves from consequence by retreating into analysis' (Heresiology:84), 'The investigator who documents a coming catastrophe more carefully than they obstruct it' (:86), and the false promise 'Innocence through distance' (:271). Vol II and Vol III do not define two different corruptions. Vol III adds the self-blindness as the inside view, and naming it Non-Commitment across the Codex is mechanical. The live conflicts are (a) Necrocursica Appendix II's reassignment to Nomenclature plus an unlisted 'general scholarly Corruption' (docx:469), and (b) the Necrocursica's own ordinal Third, the Incomplete Sealing (docx:239). So the question for Isaac narrows to: does Appendix II's reading stay as its author's disputed claim, or is it cut? Replacing ordinals with names remains the right move (gw-08).
findings.verify_evidence: Vol II docx:265; Vol III docx:28-30, :234, :382, :384 (byte-identical to THE ALFTIAN CODEX.md, checked with cmp); Corrant Papers docx:273; Necrocursica docx:239, :469; Heresiology:84-86, :271; Alftian Codex meta:48.

findings.topic: The author's own corruption does not fit Kwon Mu-jin's card
findings.doc_claim: Vol II: "The Separation Perverted, in my experience of it, was something I recognised in the mirror" (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:184), in "the letter I did not answer" (:186). The meta page calls the Codex "A single unanswered letter" running through all three volumes (wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:33).
findings.canon: Non-Commitment is "Perfect diagnosis, absent intervention" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:85). Mu-jin's card gives the opposite. Flaw: "Cannot let an error sit uncorrected, even when correcting it costs him the room" (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:118). Stress Default: "Names the problem aloud whether anyone wants to hear it or not" (:124). His Catalyst is "seeing a truth no one else could see, and being right" (:43). His Crystal is Refined, with the Splintering fracture integrated (:46), and he is self-bound to a teaching vow (:27).
findings.why_it_matters: With Mu-jin as author, the Codex's backbone becomes a man recognising in himself the one corruption his card says he is least capable of.
findings.question: Which corruption does Mu-jin find in himself over the course of the Codex?

options.label: A. Keep Non-Commitment, as a single lapse
options.consequence: The unanswered letter is the one error he let sit. The card gains a Lore line explaining why. The arc stands, and his Flaw becomes the thing he once broke.

options.label: B. Conviction (Calcination Perverted)
options.consequence: This fits his Catalyst and Flaw. Vol III already frames the turn this way: "I began this project with the conviction that the Great Work was a system of alignment" and "I had the direction reversed" (docx:390). The letter goes unanswered from certainty, not avoidance, and the corruption he first diagnosed in the king (Volume the First.md:167) turns out to be his own. The 'Third Corruption' lines in Vol III, the Corrant Papers P.S. (docx:273) and Necrocursica Appendix II change.

options.label: C. Submission (Dissolution Perverted)
options.consequence: This fits the Ledger-Prince, the child the court made into a symbol (Kwon Mu-jin.md:24, :30). But it doubles up the corruption canon gives the Necrocursica's author (gw-11).

findings.recommendation: B. It is the only option that agrees with his card without a special exception, and Vol III's own thesis sentence is already a certainty being overturned.
findings.verify_evidence: wiki Volume the Second.md:184, :186, :188 ('I had simply decided not to be responsible for it'); Alftian Codex meta:33; Heresiology:85; Kwon Mu-jin.md:27 (self-bound teaching vow), :43, :46, :118, :120 (Loop: 'states it plainly'), :121 (Foil: 'honesty without patience'), :124; Volume the First.md:167; Vol III docx:390; Heresiology Case I :208 (the king as Calcination Perverted) supports option B. Added weight for B: Heresiology:86 lists 'The teacher who recognizes drift in a student and says nothing' as Non-Commitment. Under option A, a man bound to a teaching vow would be committing a vow-level lapse, which reads as a Shear Break (Heresiology:239), and his Refined Crystal (:46) records nothing like it.

findings.topic: The Second Corruption's canon example is the compelled Necrocursica author
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica docx:5: "Authored under compulsion by Noxinus Ren ... during his confinement at the Genesio Monastery". Codex Vol II: Dissolution Perverted "is the stage that produces Noxinus writing the Necrocursica" (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:134).
findings.canon: Heresiology Case II, 'The Compelled Author and the Necromantic Manuscript': "A talented writer, pulled by access and manipulated through need" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:209). Under Submission: "The gifted assistant writing what the master wished written" (:75). Malphas's card: "Expelled from the Pyraeon Forge Academy and declared a metaphysical threat. Unbound in life" (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Malphas · Ferment of Stars.md:20). "The Heresiology named him without naming him" as Fermentation Perverted (:45-47), with an Overgrown Crystal held permanently (:44).
findings.why_it_matters: Replacing Noxinus with Malphas moves canon's standing example of Submission onto a character canon already files under Fermentation.
findings.question: Did Malphas write the Necrocursica under compulsion, which keeps him as canon's example of Submission, or of his own free will?

options.label: A. Compelled
options.consequence: He is confined after being declared a metaphysical threat. Malphas descends from Submission to Fermentation, which echoes "The Monastery teaches Calcination first" (Volume the Second.md:141). Case II and Vol II:134 keep their shape with the name changed, and the card's Lore gains the confinement.

options.label: B. Willing
options.consequence: He writes as Fermentation's 'crisis becomes laboratory' (Heresiology:114). Case II and Vol II chapter 7 need a new example of Submission or a rewrite, and the header loses 'under compulsion'.

options.label: C. Split
options.consequence: Malphas is the theorist and a compelled scribe writes it down, which fits Heresiology:75 word for word. But it keeps a Noxinus-like figure that Isaac meant to replace.

findings.recommendation: A. The header's confinement suits a man 'declared a metaphysical threat'. It keeps two canon passages intact and gives Malphas an arc along the corruption ladder instead of a second label.
findings.correction: The citations hold, but the finding misses two canon anchors that bear on the choice. (1) The footnote. Canon's compelled author 'Puts the warning in the footnote' (Alftian Codex meta:43). Case II's instruction turns on it: 'The warning survived as a footnote' (Heresiology:209). Vol II calls the footnote 'the one thing that separates the text from its most dangerous possible form' (wiki Volume the Second.md:137). Distillation Perverted cites 'Necromantic manuals whose warnings survive only as footnotes' (Heresiology:127). So the Necrocursica is canon's example for Sanitized Truth as well as Submission. Isaac must also decide whether Malphas writes the conscience-footnote. (2) Malphas's own card supports option A's 'descent': at Stage IX he 'stopped working alone' and handed responsibility to something that 'did not sign anything' (Malphas · Ferment of Stars.md:21-23), which is Submission-shaped (Heresiology:73, dissolving 'into another will'). His primary Wellspring is Dissolution (:53). Recommendation A stands and is stronger for these points. Add the footnote as a sub-question.
findings.verify_evidence: Necrocursica docx:5; wiki Volume the Second.md:134, :137; Heresiology:73, :75, :114, :127, :209; Alftian Codex meta:43; Malphas · Ferment of Stars.md:20-23, :44-47, :53.

findings.topic: Can corruption be read on the sheet? Crystal State, Shear Break, Coherence and the Vows
findings.doc_claim: The Codex and the Necrocursica describe corruption only through behaviour. Necrocursica docx:349 says Completion feels "indistinguishable, from the inside, from the most profound form of Temperance alignment". No text names a Crystal State or Sub-Stat for any corruption.
findings.canon: General hooks exist. The Vows are Votia: Tempering Coherence "measures the alignment between a practitioner's stated law and their lived behaviour", and "a vow broken is a Shear Break" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:238-239; wiki/The Magic System/The Magical Categories — Unified Taxonom.md:265-267). Investigators are told to read the Coherence before the interview (Heresiology:243). Coherence is a Tempering Sub-Stat, "The Crystal's internal honesty meter" (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/IV. The Eight Primaries and the Sixty-Four Sub-Stats (Part Twelve).md:105). Corrupted techniques "are sustained by refusal", which shows as Harmonics Attunement falling away from Tempering Coherence (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/V. Wellsprings, Attraction and Obsession, Magic Integration (Parts Thirteen–Fifteen).md:198-199), and the bench says the same (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:330). Obsession Force degrades Coherence catastrophically (V:156). Soul signs include a split between declared belief and pulse-pattern, and 'hollow over-coherence' (Heresiology:152). Crystal State is not a marker. Malphas pairs Fermentation Perverted with a permanently Overgrown Crystal (Malphas · Ferment of Stars.md:44-47). Sinclair Mercer's working, sustained by refusal, sits on a Fractured Crystal (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Sinclair Mercer · The Soul Devourer.md:46, :208), and Ignatius's on a Refined one (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Ignatius Sanctus Sanctorum Arsenal · The Archpaladin.md:41, :116). Pure alchemists do not temper, and "No instrument in the Accord reads grain" (Alchemetrica:82-86). Canon gives no signature for any single corruption.
findings.why_it_matters: Canon already wires corruption to one number (Coherence) and one failure (Shear Break), but not corruption by corruption. My reading of the seven Vows (Heresiology:225-231), which is not canon: 'resemblance/identity' and 'contradiction before power' guard Conviction, 'join' and 'the voiceless' guard Conjunction, and no vow guards Non-Commitment, the Codex author's own corruption.
findings.question: Should each of the seven corruptions leave a readable signature on a character's sheet, and through what?

options.label: A. Existing instruments only
options.consequence: The conversion cites Coherence, Attunement against Coherence, and Shear Break in general terms. No table is added, and pure alchemists stay unreadable.

options.label: B. A stat table per corruption
options.consequence: Each corruption gets the Sub-Stats it moves, the Crystal State it drifts toward, and the Stages where it strikes (linked to gw-01 B). This is new canon, needs ratification, and needs a clause for Class Ø practitioners.

options.label: C. The Vows as the hook
options.consequence: The seven Vows are reworked so each guards one corruption, with a vow for Non-Commitment such as acting on what one has separated. A kept vow then buys Coherence against its corruption, and a broken one is that corruption's Shear Break. Only one canon list changes.

findings.recommendation: C. It uses the mechanism canon already built: the Heresiology says "the vow is what the soul is failing at" (:241). It costs one list edit and lets investigators and character sheets read a named corruption as a named broken vow. B can follow later if Isaac wants numbers.
findings.correction: The general hooks are cited correctly, but the auditor's non-canon reading of the Vows undersells what canon already implies. The seven Vows (Heresiology:225-231) track the corruption entries almost word for word. 'I will not make crisis my preferred laboratory' matches Fermentation Perverted's 'Crisis becomes laboratory' (:114). 'I will not cleanse my notes of blood...' matches Distillation's corrective on cost removed from the page (:132). 'I will not call what is provisional final' matches Coagulation's 'mistakes interim form for absolute completion' (:136). 'join' and 'the voiceless' match Conjunction's three questions (:99-105). 'resemblance identity' matches Conviction's Mortalis expression (:66) and Case III (:210). 'contradiction before ... power' matches the Conviction corrective (:68) and Submission's dissolving into a patron or monarch (:73). Canon never states the mapping, so the status stays absent_from_canon. But option C costs less than described: only Non-Commitment clearly lacks a vow, and Submission shares one. Also, Alchemetrica's 'Heresy at the Bench' ties three named corruptions (Fermentation, Distillation, Coagulation gone wrong) to the refusal tell (Alchemetrica.md:323-330), and V:198-199 reads that tell as Attunement against Coherence. So canon already reads three corruptions on the sheet, collectively rather than one by one. Treat V:198's 'corrupted techniques' (Obsession-sustained) as the same mechanism as the Heresiology's Seven only for those three. Recommendation C stands.

missed.topic: Two cards quote a 'Heresiology' line that is not in the Heresiology
missed.detail: Sinclair Mercer's and Ignatius's cards credit the phrase 'a corrupted operation sustained by refusal' to the Heresiology. The Heresiology page has no such phrase. It comes from Alchemetrica's 'Heresy at the Bench' (which opens 'The Heresiology treats corruption doctrinally. What follows is...') and from Fracture of Worlds V. This matters to item 5 of the seam, because the cards merge Obsession-sustained workings into the Seven Corruptions by attribution. Mechanical fix: in both cards, change 'The Heresiology names the condition' to cite Alchemetrica's Heresy at the Bench, or reword it without naming a source.
missed.evidence: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Sinclair Mercer · The Soul Devourer.md:208; wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Ignatius Sanctus Sanctorum Arsenal · The Archpaladin.md:116; grep for 'refusal' in wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md finds only :85 ('refusal of moral burden'); wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:325, :330; wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/V. Wellsprings...md:198.

missed.topic: The Necrocursica's residue names disagree with what canon says the Necrocursica names
missed.detail: The Necrocursica's Tria Prima maps onto its own residues: Corporeal Residue, Aetheric Shell, Nospheric Echo, plus the Volitional Trace. The meta page and the wiki Vol II condensation say the Necrocursica's three residue categories are the Harmonic Imprint, the Sympathetic Bond Trace and the Parunic Echo. Any Tria Prima mapping (gw-06) rests on residue names canon does not recognise. This probably belongs to the residue/Mortalis seam, but it decides what gw-06 can map.
missed.evidence: Necrocursica docx:97, :101, :105, :109, :129-137; wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:58; wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:82.
missed.question: Which residue names does the converted Necrocursica use: its own (Corporeal Residue, Aetheric Shell, Nospheric Echo) or the ones canon credits to it (Harmonic Imprint, Sympathetic Bond Trace, Parunic Echo)? Option A: keep the Necrocursica's names and correct the meta page and Vol II table. The Tria Prima mapping survives as written. Option B: rename to canon's three. The Necrocursica's Sulphur/Salt/Mercury assignments must be redone, and Salt loses the 'Corporeal Residue = Salt' line (docx:97). Recommendation: A, because the docx is the fuller source and its triad is the only worked mapping.

missed.topic: The footnote that canon's Case II turns on is missing from the Necrocursica
missed.detail: Canon makes a footnote the conscience of the compelled author. Case II: 'The warning survived as a footnote'. Distillation Perverted: manuals 'whose warnings survive only as footnotes'. The meta page says he 'Puts the warning in the footnote', and Vol II says the footnote separates the text from its most dangerous form. The Necrocursica docx has no footnote; its warnings are archive stamps. Under Malphas's authorship this feeds gw-11: someone has to write the footnote, and whoever does is canon's example of both Submission and Sanitized Truth.
missed.evidence: grep -i footnote in THE NECROCURSICA.md returns nothing; stamps at docx:13, :449, :505; wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:127, :209; wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:43; wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:137.
missed.question: Does the converted Necrocursica carry a warning footnote, and whose hand is it? Option A: Malphas writes it himself. This keeps Case II, but a man canon files under Fermentation is showing conscience. Option B: a later hand adds it, such as an archivist or the Corrant Papers' new author. Case II's 'the author put the warning in' becomes 'the warning was added'. Option C: no footnote. Case II and Vol II:137 need rewriting. Recommendation: A, if gw-11 goes to option A, since a compelled Malphas leaving a trace of dissent fits the descent from Submission.

seams.title: Glyphica and Mechanica
seams.summary: The Necrocursica's glyph work is closer to current canon than it first looks. Authorization, Boundary, Direction and Sealing are canon's Four Glyph Roles. The Category One chain Ie-Ur-Flx is exactly Alchemetrica's Distillation triple, which canon calls "the forensic operation". The Third Corruption's open-seal mechanics match the Spirit Rune Arts' unsealed-rune doctrine almost word for word. The hard breaks are these. Ie is Perception, not Sight, a mechanical fix under the live rule R18-4. "Fixatio" and "Mortalis itself" are Wellsprings used as glyphs; canon only allows that through a distinct attested form, as [AnMa] Anamnesis shows, and none exists for either. The Aetheric Bleed calls lawful work "Mechanica", which canon defines as unauthorized, drawn from a donor, Grade V and permanent on the ground. The Parunic Echo, Jabir's amulet and De Raits's wax-seal glyph each claim something canon does not support as written, so each needs Isaac's choice. Canon also has an unrecorded split between the Spirit Rune Arts phoneme table (which Mu-jin's Book of Summons follows) and the Master Glyph Index. That split decides which glyph vocabulary Mu-jin writes in. His Fixation Anchor Sense makes him the natural detector of an Incomplete Sealing. But he holds no Mortalis harmonization, so he can diagnose Category Three work and cannot lawfully authorize it.

findings.topic: Glyph names in the Category One chain and in Alchemetrica's operations table
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica, Chapter the Second: "begins with Ie (Sight) as the Authorization Glyph" and "uses Ur (Balance) as the Direction Glyph", then "Flx (Flux) to Fixatio". Alchemetrica's table lists the codes Ur Ma Th / Ie Ur Flx / Xr Vael Ora and gives no names.
findings.canon: The Master Codex workbook (the source build/codex.py:7 reads) has row [Ie] = Perception: Root, Iesara, Luminalis, Fulguria. wiki/The Fourteen Archons/Pair IV — Insight Against Dream.md:24 lists "[Ie] Perception". None of the 136 forms is named Sight. [Ur] Balance (Root, Urion) is confirmed at wiki/The Magic System/The Master Glyph Index — 136 Attested Forms.md:118. [Flx] Flux (Derivative — Synonym, Wyther, primary Transmutatio/Spatium, attested at Fixatio) is in the workbook and at scenes/20_aurelian_no_signature.md:194. R18-4 requires a glyph in an inscription to be "quoted exactly as the Index gives it" (rules/pack-18-eighteen.yaml:193-195), and it is live in out/rules.resolved.json. All nine Alchemetrica codes are valid forms: Ur Balance, Ma Recall, Th Foundation (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:101); Ie Perception, Ur Balance, Flx Flux (:102); Xr Excision, Vael Renewal, Ora Truth (:103; Ora is unclassified, Master Glyph Index page:100). Only Ora is attested at its mirror Wellspring, Sublimare. Alchemetrica:102 calls Distillation "the forensic operation", so the Necrocursica's Distillation-aligned Category One chain matches canon.
findings.why_it_matters: The Necrocursica presents this chain as "the formula. Do not improvise it." Naming Ie as Sight breaks R18-4, and Check 38 fails it in bracketed form.
findings.mechanical_fix: Change "Ie (Sight)" to "Ie (Perception)", or the house form "[Ie] Perception". Keep "Ur (Balance)" and "Flx (Flux)" unchanged. Where a converted text names Alchemetrica's operation glyphs, use Ur Balance, Ma Recall and Th Foundation; Ie Perception, Ur Balance and Flx Flux; Xr Excision, Vael Renewal and Ora Truth. Keep the Ie-Ur-Flx triple itself, because it is Alchemetrica's Distillation chain. A minor point merged here: Ie authorizes a Luminalis perception, not a Mortalis process, which is correct for a reading that must not touch the residue.
findings.correction: The Sight-to-Perception fix is right and is mechanical under R18-4. One claim is wrong: Check 38 would not fail "[Ie] Sight". Check 38 only checks that a bracketed token such as [Ie] exists in the Index, and [Ie] does, so the check passes. The name drift is caught only by R18-4, applied by hand. Everything else stands. All nine Alchemetrica codes match the workbook rows. Only Ora is attested at its mirror Wellspring, Sublimare, and part of the reason is that Distillatio is not among the sixty Wellsprings in the Lists sheet. Alchemetrica.md:101 also supports Ur as the Direction glyph: "A Distillation without a Direction glyph separates every signature present".
findings.verify_evidence: Workbook Master Glyph Index rows (via build/codex.py sheets()): [Ie] Perception, Root, Iesara, Luminalis, Fulguria; [Ur] Balance; [Flx] Flux, Synonym, Wyther, Transmutatio, attested at Fixatio; no form is named Sight. rules/pack-18-eighteen.yaml:187-195 (R18-4-GLYPH_QUOTED_EXACTLY, live in out/rules.resolved.json). rules/pack-18-eighteen.yaml:394-395 and build/codex.py:107-115: Check 38 tests only whether the token is known. wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:100-102. Source: THE NECROCURSICA.md:165.

findings.topic: Two glyph vocabularies in canon, and which one Mu-jin writes in
findings.doc_claim: The Necrocursica glosses Ie as "Sight". The conversion makes Mu-jin the author of the Codex, so every glyph he names will be in his voice.
findings.canon: The Spirit Rune Arts phoneme table (wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Rune Arts.md:95-107) gives Ie Insight, Ma Memory, Wy Truth, Ra Transcendence, Sa Silence, El Illusion, Ir Endurance, plus Ci Order/Honor, Zo Echo, No Negation, Tar Weight and Ky Structure. The Master Glyph Index gives different names for the same codes: [Ie] Perception; [Ma] Recall (wiki/Summoned and Bound/Vaelmorn · The Standing Grave.md:131); [Wy] Motion (wiki/The Magic System/The Descent of Parun — The Fourteen Hands.md:32); [Sa] Illumination and [Ir] Continuum (Master Glyph Index page:96, :80); [Ra] Flame and [El] Life (workbook). It has no Ci, Zo, No, Tar or Ky at all. Mu-jin's Book of Summons follows the phoneme table: `Ie` Insight, `Ma` Memory, `Ci` Order, `No` Negation (wiki/The Disciplines/The Open Crucible — Kwon Mu-jin's Book of Summons.md:44, 57, 125). It also has `Th` Structure (:57), which matches neither list. In-world precedent for drift: a Sealing glyph "that had drifted in meaning since entry" (wiki/Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/The Bench of Attribution.md:120). R18-4 makes the Index the authority. CONFLICTS.md has no row for this split.
findings.why_it_matters: Mu-jin's own canon page uses the older names. A Codex in his voice will either contradict his book of summons or break R18-4 and Check 38.
findings.question: When Mu-jin and Malphas name a glyph (a written Parun form), should they use the Master Glyph Index names, or the older phoneme-table names from the Spirit Rune Arts page and Mu-jin's Book of Summons?

options.label: Index names only; log the Spirit Rune Arts table and the Book of Summons as a conflict to fix later
options.consequence: Passes R18-4 and Check 38. Mu-jin's summons page reads inconsistently with his Codex until it is brought in line.

options.label: Treat the older phoneme names as a real in-world teaching register, where meanings drift
options.consequence: Keeps Mu-jin's voice continuous with his book. Every such gloss breaks R18-4 unless a ruling makes an exception.

options.label: Index names in the chain, with Mu-jin's old teaching gloss in parentheses when he explains ("Ie, Perception; my teachers said Insight")
options.consequence: Passes R18-4 and turns the split into character texture, at the cost of a clause each time.

findings.recommendation: Option 3 for Mu-jin's Codex, option 1 for Malphas's Necrocursica, and log the Spirit Rune Arts / Book of Summons split in CONFLICTS.md either way. The Index is the live authority, and Mu-jin is a teacher who explains old terms.
findings.correction: The split is real and CONFLICTS.md has no row for it. Five details need fixing. (1) The phoneme table is at The Spirit Rune Arts.md:100-105, with its sample chain at :107. (2) The drift is wider than the finding lists: Ka (Cycle, Index Dream), Va (Moment, Index Law), Se (Fire, Index Song), and Ae appears twice, as Sound and Era, where the Index has Ae Vastness and AeV Era. Si, Zu and Fi are also missing from the Index. The table does agree with the Index on Ur Balance, Th Foundation, En Lattice, Al Edge and Cal Craft. (3) Check 38 catches only the codes that do not exist in the Index (Ci, Zo, No, Tar, Ky, Si, Zu, Fi) when they are bracketed. It does not catch a wrong name on a valid code. (4) Canon already answers the question for any chain, inscription or chant: R18-4 is live and requires the Index names. Option 2 (old names inside a chain) would need Isaac to overturn a live rule. Say so, rather than offering it as an equal option. (5) The decision left for Isaac is only whether Mu-jin mentions his old teaching names in explanatory prose, and whether the Spirit Rune Arts table and the Book of Summons get logged and brought into line. The recommendation (option 3 for Mu-jin, option 1 for Malphas, and a CONFLICTS row either way) stands.
findings.verify_evidence: wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Rune Arts.md:100-107. Workbook rows: [Ka] Dream, [Va] Law, [Se] Song, [En] Lattice, [Cro] Cycle, [Len] Line; no [Ci], [Zo], [No], [Tar], [Ky], [Si]. wiki/The Disciplines/The Open Crucible — Kwon Mu-jin's Book of Summons.md:44, :57, :125. wiki/Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/The Bench of Attribution.md:120. grep of CONFLICTS.md and RULINGS.md for phoneme, Spirit Rune, Open Crucible and Insight: no hits. rules/pack-18-eighteen.yaml:394-395.

findings.topic: Authorization, Boundary, Direction and Sealing as glyph roles
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica: "Ie (Sight) as the Authorization Glyph, establishes Boundary Glyphs at a standard five-metre perimeter", with Ur as "the Direction Glyph" and a "Sealing Glyph chain".
