findings.canon: Glyphica "Governs the Four Glyph Roles: Authorization, Boundary, Direction, Sealing" (wiki/The Magic System/The Magical Categories — Unified Taxonom.md:94). Each role is defined at wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Rune Arts.md:31-51. They run as "a sequence rather than a checklist" (wiki/The Magic System/Mechanica Extraction Without Recognition.md:34; Alchemetrica.md:279). The Draft-circle carries "the Authorization, Boundary, Direction and Sealing chains" (Alchemetrica.md:166). The summon template has the fields Authorization / Boundary / Direction / Sealing Glyph (wiki/The Called · Summon Register/Summon Entry · Blank Template.md:63-67). These are roles, not classes; the classes are Root, Extension, Compound, Synonym and Counter (Master Glyph Index page:40-46). The spoken counterpart is Warrant, Ground, Vector, Seal (wiki/The Descent of Parun — The Fourteen Hands/The Counted Speech — A Speaker's Grammar of Parun.md:101-108). Boundary sets "spatial and temporal limits" (Spirit Rune Arts:40), including "how long it may persist" (Alchemetrica:260).
findings.why_it_matters: The roles are the strongest bridge between the Necrocursica and current canon and should survive the conversion unchanged.
findings.mechanical_fix: Keep the four role names and their order. Add a duration beside the five-metre perimeter, because canon defines Boundary as both place and time; the value is the writer's choice.
findings.correction: The finding is right that these are canon's four Glyph Roles and not classes. It should cite the live rule that says so directly: R18-4-ROLE_VS_CLASS_AXES (rules/pack-18-eighteen.yaml:206) calls role and class "orthogonal axes". Soften one claim: that Warrant, Ground, Vector and Seal are the spoken counterpart of the four roles is an inference. The parallel is real (Descent:58 lists who, ground, which way, how it ends), but no canon line maps the slots onto the roles. The mechanical fix, adding a duration to the Boundary, stands: Alchemetrica:260 defines Boundary as including "how long it may persist".
findings.verify_evidence: wiki/The Magic System/The Magical Categories — Unified Taxonom.md:94. wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Rune Arts.md:33-51 (Boundary at :40). wiki/The Magic System/Mechanica Extraction Without Recognition.md:34. wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:166, :260, :279. wiki/The Called · Summon Register/Summon Entry · Blank Template.md:63-67. Master Glyph Index page:40-46. Counted Speech:101-108. grep across wiki and rules for Warrant beside Authorization: no mapping found. rules/pack-18-eighteen.yaml:206 (R18-4-ROLE_VS_CLASS_AXES, live).

findings.topic: The Category One seal ends on a Wellspring ("Flx to Fixatio")
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica: "The Sealing Glyph chain is Flx (Flux) to Fixatio, locking the observation field so that it attenuates cleanly".
findings.canon: Fixatio is one of the sixty Wellsprings in the Codex Lists sheet (read by build/codex.py:39-43), not a glyph. A glyph is "a boundary condition imposed on that law" (Master Glyph Index page:20). Sealing "Draws heavily on Fixatio chains" (Spirit Rune Arts:50), and "Fixatio chains close the Draft" (Alchemetrica:121). [Flx] Flux is attested at Fixatio (workbook). [Tp] Topology is the only form whose primary Wellspring is Fixatio: "Freezes a local outcome grid for a brief window" (workbook). The archive already has "[Flx] Flux frozen by [Tp] Topology (Thalen / Fixatio / Materia)" (scenes/20_aurelian_no_signature.md:194). One form does carry a Wellspring's name, [AnMa] Anamnesis (workbook), so a Wellspring-named glyph needs its own attested form, and none exists for Fixatio.
findings.why_it_matters: Read literally, the chain treats a law as a glyph. Read charitably, it names the Wellspring the seal runs under. The text must pick one reading.
findings.question: The Category One seal ends "to Fixatio", which is a Wellspring, not a glyph. How should the last step of the chain read?

options.label: "Flx (Flux), closed on a Fixatio chain": Fixatio is named as the law the seal runs under
options.consequence: Smallest change and matches the Spirit Rune Arts wording. The seal names only one glyph.

options.label: "Flx (Flux) to Tp (Topology)": Topology is the Index's Fixatio glyph
options.consequence: A fully named, checkable chain with an archived precedent. Topology's "brief window" suits a field meant to fade.

options.label: Replace Flux with a sealing-sense glyph such as Lk (Lock)
options.consequence: Reads more obviously as a seal, but breaks the Ie-Ur-Flx Distillation triple that ties the chain to Alchemetrica.

findings.recommendation: Option 2. It keeps the author's chain and its link to Alchemetrica, names a real Fixatio glyph, and matches how Flux has already been sealed in the archive.
findings.correction: The facts check out: Fixatio is a Wellspring; Tp is the only form whose primary Wellspring is Fixatio; AnMa is the only form named after a Wellspring; Flx is attested at Fixatio. But the finding misses canon's own habit of labelling a role by its Wellspring. The Spirit Rune Arts' example compound rune combines "a Benediction Authorization, an Anima Spirare Direction, and a Fixatio Seal" (Spirit Rune Arts:84), and Alchemetrica:121 says "Fixatio chains close the Draft". So option 1 ("Flx, closed on a Fixatio chain" or "a Fixatio Seal") is canon's own wording, not merely the smallest change. It remains Isaac's decision. The recommendation should either lean to option 1, or offer option 1 with Tp named as the Fixatio glyph ("Flx sealed by Tp on a Fixatio chain"). Either way, name the idiom at Spirit Rune Arts:84 when giving the reason.
findings.verify_evidence: Lists sheet: Fixatio is one of the sixty. Workbook: [Tp] Topology is the only row whose primary Wellspring is Fixatio; [AnMa] is the only name that is a Wellspring; [Flx] is attested at Fixatio. wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Rune Arts.md:50, :84. wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:121. scenes/20_aurelian_no_signature.md:194. Master Glyph Index page:20. Source: THE NECROCURSICA.md:165.

findings.topic: "Mortalis itself" as the last Sealing glyph for Category Three
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica: "The Sealing Glyph chain for Category Three ends with Mortalis itself — the Wellspring inscribed as the final boundary" and "This is the glyph that makes the impression-body temporary."
findings.canon: A glyph "creates nothing and carries no power"; it is a boundary condition on a law (Master Glyph Index page:20; Descent:37). None of the 136 forms is named Mortalis; the only Wellspring-named form is [AnMa] Anamnesis (workbook). Forms attested at Mortalis are: [Vor] Return, Root, Auren, "Recycles Essence; prevents restless dead" (workbook; wiki/Summoned and Bound/Obrenkael · The Mule.md:68); [Rt] Return, its unclassified Synonym (Master Glyph Index page:104); [Ob] Obol, "Guided, lawful soul-crossing with minimal bleed"; [Au] Death, "ends unrest; calms echoes"; and also [SoulDr], [Sv], [Blt], [Bd] and [Wy]. The Standing Note says to pitch a new entry only "If no combination fits" (Master Glyph Index page:128). A spoken Seal names "the condition on which it ends" (Counted Speech:108). The Warrant "ena" means "by the dead, in the mouth of the living" (Counted Speech:165), canon's only Parun hook for speaking for the dead. Malphas has Mortalis as co-primary and "is standing in his own" (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Malphas · Ferment of Stars.md:54).
findings.why_it_matters: This seal is what keeps impression-bodies temporary, and its failure is the Third Corruption. The whole necromancy framework rests on a step that canon says cannot exist as written.
findings.question: What is the last glyph of the Category Three seal, the step that keeps an impression-body (the animated echo built from a dead person's residue) temporary?

options.label: Vor (Return), the Mortalis-attested glyph that "prevents restless dead"
options.consequence: Lawful, checkable and exact in meaning. The text says "the Mortalis seal" instead of "Mortalis itself".

options.label: Rt (Return), the same meaning as an unclassified synonym
options.consequence: Adds an eerie beat: the glyph that makes the dead temporary is one the Continuum cannot classify. Unclassified forms carry weight in canon (the Moto Long Reading), so this spends some of it.

options.label: Keep "Mortalis itself" as Malphas's own heterodox claim, with a marked in-world dissent
options.consequence: A strong voice beat from a writer who stands in Mortalis. The text then asserts something canon calls impossible, so an annotator has to say so.

options.label: Pitch a new Mortalis-named form, the way [AnMa] carries Anamnesis
options.consequence: Makes the claim literally true, but adds a 137th form against the Standing Note when Vor already fits.

findings.recommendation: Option 1, written as a closing condition: the Seal ends when the Trace's decision is delivered. If the chain is spelled out further, open it with the Warrant "ena". This uses existing canon from end to end, and it explains why the Corrant Papers' echo ended "in one breath" after eleven days.
findings.verify_evidence: Workbook: the forms attested at Mortalis are exactly [Au], [Wy], [Vor], [Bd], [Ob], [SoulDr], [Blt], [Sv] and [Rt]. [Vor] reads "Recycles Essence; prevents restless dead". [Ob] reads "Guided, lawful soul-crossing with minimal bleed". No form is named Mortalis. Master Glyph Index page:20, :104, :128. Descent:37. Counted Speech:108, :165. wiki/Summoned and Bound/Obrenkael · The Mule.md:68. wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Malphas · Ferment of Stars.md:54. THE CORRANT PAPERS.md:147 ("In one breath"). Source: THE NECROCURSICA.md:177. "The Mortalis seal" in option 1 also follows the role-by-Wellspring idiom at Spirit Rune Arts:84.

findings.topic: How the Third Corruption's seal fails, measured against canon's failure rules
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica, Third Corruption: the practitioner "does not properly execute the final Mortalis Sealing Glyph", and the body accumulates Essence "through the structural vacancy created by the absent Sealing Glyph".
findings.canon: For inscribed work: "An unsealed rune is an open wound in the local Aether field. Environmental Essence bleeds into it", and the Continuum may complete it (Spirit Rune Arts:51). That nearly matches the Third Corruption. For spoken work there are two rules. "Under the sum · Nothing sealed it. The working runs and does not stop" (Counted Speech:143). But "Slot skipped · No seal, no working, no cost" (Counted Speech:145). A working with no Authorization "cannot lawfully Seal and therefore does not end" (Alchemetrica:279); that is Mechanica and does not apply here. The Draft-circle carries the Sealing chain (Alchemetrica:166).
findings.why_it_matters: If Category Three is spoken, a missing Seal means no impression-body at all, and the Corruption cannot happen as written. The answer decides which canon rule the Third Corruption depends on.
findings.question: Is the Category Three operation inscribed on a Draft-circle or spoken, and does its seal fail by being missing or by being short?

options.label: Inscribed on a Draft-circle; the Seal chain is left unfinished or broken
options.consequence: Matches the Spirit Rune Arts' "open wound" doctrine almost word for word. "Absent" becomes "unfinished or broken".

options.label: Spoken; the Seal comes in under the sum
options.consequence: Matches "the working runs and does not stop". The text's "underestimation of the Trace's charge density" already reads as a counting error.

options.label: Both: the circle is scribed and the seal is spoken last, and either failure produces the Corruption
options.consequence: The most complete version, but it needs both rules explained on the page.

findings.recommendation: Option 1. Category Three already needs "a material substrate", which is Draft-circle work, and the unsealed-rune passage describes the Third Corruption's accumulation exactly. Keep haste, underestimation and failure of nerve as the causes.
findings.verify_evidence: wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Rune Arts.md:51. Counted Speech:143, :145. Alchemetrica.md:166, :279. Sources: THE NECROCURSICA.md:173 ("create a material substrate"), :241 ("does not properly execute"), :245 ("absent Sealing Glyph"). The text says both "improperly executed" and "absent", so the finding is right that it must choose. The delayed seal that succeeded (Necrocursica:249-251) fits canon: a warranted working can still be closed (Mechanica page:34, :37).

findings.topic: "The Third Corruption" means two different things in the two books
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica: "The Third Corruption: The Incomplete Sealing". Codex Vol II: "The Third Corruption ... the Separation Perverted or the Corruption of Non-Commitment". Codex Vol III: "the inversion of the scholar's purpose".
findings.canon: Heresiology Grade III cites "the Seven Corruptions" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:184). The Heresiology's corruptions follow the operation-perverted pattern, for example "Conjunction Perverted" (:93). That matches the Codex's list, not the Necrocursica's. Canon is silent on the Necrocursica's seven names.
findings.why_it_matters: Mu-jin's Codex and Malphas's Necrocursica will cross-reference each other. Right now "the Third Corruption" is a sealing failure in one book and a scholar's self-deception in the other. The Corruptions seam probably owns the full list; it is recorded here because audit item 6 depends on it.
findings.question: The two books number seven Corruptions differently. Which list owns the numbers, so that "the Third Corruption" means one thing?

options.label: The Codex/Heresiology list owns the numbers; the Necrocursica's failures become named case types without numbers ("the Incomplete Sealing")
options.consequence: Aligns with the Heresiology. The Necrocursica loses its "seven" framing.

options.label: Both lists stand as two authors' rival schemes, always cited with the author's name
options.consequence: Both books stay intact. Readers must track which list is meant.

options.label: Merge them into one list of seven
options.consequence: Cleanest canon, largest rewrite.

findings.recommendation: Option 1. The Heresiology already uses the operation-perverted scheme, so Malphas's case studies read naturally as failure modes beneath it, and the Incomplete Sealing keeps its name.
findings.correction: Three corrections, and the decision stays Isaac's. (1) The Heresiology's section is titled "The Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions" (Heresiology:57), the exact title the Necrocursica uses for its own list (Necrocursica:3, :187). The clash is a title collision with canon, not only a numbering difference. (2) In the Heresiology's order, Separation Perverted, the Corruption of Non-Commitment, is third (:59, :70, :81), which matches Vol II exactly. So canon already sides with the Codex's numbering. "Conjunction Perverted" is at :92; line :93 is blank. (3) The Necrocursica itself says the two schemes differ. It reads the Codex's Third Corruption as "partially" its own Cacodaemon of Nomenclature, and as a general scholarly corruption that "does not appear in the Seven Corruptions because it is not a Mortalis Corruption" (Necrocursica:469). Recommendation stays option 1. Rename Malphas's set so it does not reuse the canon title, for example "the seven Mortalis failures" or named case types, and keep :469 as his in-world cross-reference.

findings.topic: Mechanica in the Aetheric Bleed and in the Category One seal
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica, Fourth Corruption: "performing legitimate work ... but doing so through sustained Mechanica rather than lawful Glyphic syntax", cured by months of Wellspring Communion. Category One seals so as to avoid "leaving a Mechanica impression in the local Aether".
findings.canon: Mechanica works without Authorization and takes finished output: "Mechanica always has a donor" (wiki/The Magic System/Mechanica Extraction Without Recognition.md:19). In Extraction the donor "may be captive, purchased, dead, or unaware" (:23). The category is "Forbidden constructs bypassing Soul Crystals, Wellsprings, or Glyphic Syntax" (Magical Categories:131). Heresiology Grade V says "Grades I through IV describe workings that ran lawfully and ended ... A Mechanica working cannot end" (Heresiology:186), and the Seven Corruptions sit at Grade III (:184). Statute XXVI: nothing closes an unsealed boundary (Mechanica page:37). The operator's delayed bill is Shell clouding, falling Coherence and flickering Traits (:44). Canon agrees with the Bleed on two points: "structural debt in the local Aether field" (Alchemetrica:277), and the debt turning from the field onto the practitioner (Mechanica page:46). Authorization needs harmonization, and "A forged authorization is Mechanica by definition" (Spirit Rune Arts:36).
findings.why_it_matters: Canon makes Mechanica unlawful by definition, Grade V, and permanent on the ground. The Bleed calls it legitimate, files it as a Grade III Corruption, and cures it.
findings.question: Is the Aetheric Bleed caused by real Mechanica (forbidden work with no lawful warrant, drawing on the dead as a donor and scarring the ground for good), or by lawful work done badly?

options.label: Real Mechanica: residue work without Mortalis harmonization is Extraction from a dead donor. Drop "legitimate"; the practitioner can be treated, but the worked ground never heals; the case is Grade V
options.consequence: The strongest tie to current canon, and apt for Malphas, a Rot Host lord, writing about Mechanica from the inside. This Corruption becomes the one that crosses into Grade V.

options.label: Lawful but under-harmonised: remove the word Mechanica; the Bleed comes from repeated over-warranting, the cost the Counted Speech takes from the speaker
options.consequence: Keeps the cure and Grade III. Loses the Mechanica link Isaac asked for.

options.label: Keep the text and add an in-world note that Malphas uses "Mechanica" loosely
options.consequence: The least rewriting. The misuse stays in text that faces canon.

findings.recommendation: Option 1. In Category One, replace "a Mechanica impression" with "an open boundary", because that operation is authorized. This uses canon's own donor and debt mechanics. The months-long cure can stand for the practitioner, because canon never says how an operator is treated.
findings.verify_evidence: wiki/The Magic System/Mechanica Extraction Without Recognition.md:17-19, :23, :34, :37, :44, :46, :50. Magical Categories:131. Heresiology:184, :186 (Grade V: "A Mechanica working cannot end ... leaves ground that cannot be"). Alchemetrica.md:277, :279. Spirit Rune Arts:36. Source: THE NECROCURSICA.md:265, :277. Note: the Bleed's own premise, "without adequate Wellspring harmonization", makes "Mechanica" correct by canon's definition (Spirit Rune Arts:36). The words that break canon are "legitimate", the Grade III filing, and the cure for the ground. Option 1 fixes all three.

findings.topic: The Parunic Echo as a glyph-trace every practitioner leaves
findings.doc_claim: Codex Vol II: the Parunic Echo is "the glyph-trace inscribed in the fabric of the world by any Temperance-active practitioner of sufficient stage". Corrant Papers: "her Parunic trace".
findings.canon: Aetheric Residue is "A permanent, if often subtle, change to the location where the working occurred" (wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:40). Every working leaves it, whatever the Stage. At Stage X, residue holds the practitioner's colour so that "a Mancer arriving a week later can still say who was here" (wiki/The Magic System/The Color of Essence.md:41). In inscription, the reading of the Engraver's Attraction Layer "becomes part of the rune's permanent structure" (Spirit Rune Arts:36). But in ordinary casting, Glyphica is "grammar spoken aloud and then forgotten by the air" (Spirit Rune Arts:23), and Mirror-Sign leaves no signature because "nothing was ever inscribed" (Descent:88). So canon has no lasting glyph-shaped trace from casting. The Codex also credits these residues to the Necrocursica, whose own four categories are Corporeal Residue, Aetheric Shell, Nospheric Echo and Volitional Trace. That is an internal conflict, probably owned by the residue seam.
findings.why_it_matters: The Parunic Echo is one of the three things the reconstruction method weaves back together. As written, it contradicts the rule that casting's syntax leaves nothing behind.
findings.question: What is the "Parunic Echo" in current canon terms? (Aetheric Residue is canon's name for the permanent trace any working leaves on a place.)

options.label: Rename it Aetheric Residue, drop "glyph-trace", and keep the Stage condition as how legible the trace is
options.consequence: Pure canon, but the Codex's coined term is lost.

options.label: Keep "Parunic Echo", defined as the signature each Authorization stamps into a practitioner's Residue, legible once they reach a high enough Stage
options.consequence: Keeps the term three texts use and grounds it in Spirit Rune Arts:36 and Color of Essence:41. A small canon extension that needs logging.

options.label: Keep it as written: a lasting glyph-trace
options.consequence: A new canon claim that contradicts "forgotten by the air".

findings.recommendation: Option 2. It keeps the word the Codex and the Corrant Papers already rely on, and it rests that word on two existing canon rules rather than on a trace canon says ordinary casting does not leave.
findings.correction: The finding misses canon's own term for a trace unique to one practitioner. "Essence Signature" is "The unique trace a practitioner's Essence leaves, readable through Gnosis-based perception. You cannot forge one" (Core Vocabulary:46). Its legibility depends on Stage: "the Signature is readable at distance" from Stage IV (Color of Essence:35; Sixteen Stages:87-92), and the residue holds the practitioner's colour for days at Stage X (Color of Essence:41). That matches "any Temperance-active practitioner of sufficient stage" far better than an Authorization stamp. Option 2 as written is also weak: a spoken working "carries nothing at all", while a cut ward carries the cutter's hand (Accord Latin:84-85; The Gate:59). An Authorization stamp therefore exists only for inscribed or poured work, not for every practitioner. Two further points. Core Vocabulary:40 calls Residue permanent, but the Mechanica page says ordinary residue "thins on a schedule" (Mechanica page:50); this canon tension should be noted. Also, "every working leaves it, whatever the Stage" is an inference; the line says only "Traces left behind by an Essence working". Revised recommendation: keep the name "Parunic Echo" and define it as the practitioner's Essence Signature left in the Aetheric Residue, legible from Stage IV. Drop "glyph-trace". Log it as a small canon extension, the naming only.

Mechanica page:50. Spirit Rune Arts:23, :36. Sources: wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:84; THE ALFTIAN CODEX — VOLUME THE SECOND.md:99; THE CORRANT PAPERS.md:171.

findings.topic: Jabir's copper amulet: which hand, and can Parun hold a quotation?
findings.doc_claim: Codex Vol I: "an amulet of worked copper bearing the quote in a Parunic dialect older than anything catalogued in the Genesio Archivum". Meta page: "in a script no Genesio archive could decipher".
findings.canon: "There is one script. There have always been fourteen ways to be wrong about that." (Descent:15). Every hand traces one lattice (:22), and root Parun is read by "Trained practitioners of every people" (:184). Canon calls the varieties hands, not dialects. Parun has "no register below the legal one" (Descent:57; Counted Speech:23), so a Parun sentence is a working, not a quotation. Gravetongue is ruled out: it is "never written" and transcriptions are "inert" (Descent:112-113; Counted Speech:299), and it is an Ironblood war-chant about the First Asteroid impact (wiki/Races & Peoples/The Goblinoid Peoples.md:163-166). No hand is tied to the dead; the only dead-linked Parun is the Warrant "ena" (Counted Speech:165). The candidates are: Mirror-Sign, read by Deepkin only and invisible to wards (Descent:85-91, 187); the thirty unclassified forms, which "the Continuum cannot classify" and which the Long Reading links to the Moto seat (Master Glyph Index page:71-75); and Old High Runic, four thousand years old but read by any Parunist (Descent:71-74). The "Wellspring resonance" Vol I describes (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:97) fits the amulet being a working.
findings.why_it_matters: As written, the amulet claims an undecipherable Parun text carrying prose. Canon rules out both halves, and Mu-jin, who reads glyph chains for a living, now receives it.
findings.question: What is written on Jabir's amulet, given that canon says every Parun hand can be read by a trained scholar, Gravetongue cannot be written, and Parun cannot carry a plain quotation?

options.label: Very old Old High Runic: change "no archive could decipher" to "no archive could date", and treat Jabir's recited words as his gloss of the working cut into the copper
options.consequence: The smallest canon footprint. The undecipherable mystery is lost.

options.label: Mirror-Sign: the copper is worked around a path that was never cut, so no archive can read it and no ward can detect it
options.consequence: Keeps "undecipherable" and the felt resonance. Tying a Shaneni astrologer to Deepkin lore needs a reason.

options.label: Written in unclassified forms: archives can read the glyphs but cannot classify them
options.consequence: A strong canonical mystery, but it touches the Moto Long Reading, which canon keeps deliberately blank.

options.label: A fifteenth, uncatalogued hand
options.consequence: Keeps the text as written. Contradicts "fourteen ways" and needs a canon extension.

findings.recommendation: Option 1, and replace "dialect" with "hand" whichever option is chosen. It keeps the scene and its resonance with the least new canon. Option 3 is the bolder choice if Isaac wants the amulet to matter later.
findings.correction: (1) Volume I itself does not call the text undecipherable. It says only "in a Parunic dialect older than anything catalogued in the Genesio Archivum" (Volume the First.md:96). "a script no Genesio archive could decipher" appears only on the meta page (Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:47). Option 1 therefore needs almost no change to Vol I ("dialect" becomes "hand"); the drift to fix is on the meta page. (2) Canon has a precedent for a principle cut in Parun: "The Temple of Inscription runs seventy years on a single theorem cut in this hand" (Descent:72, Old High Runic). So "Parun cannot carry a quotation" overstates canon. Canon says rather that any Parun sentence is also a working (Descent:57-58; Accord Latin:108), which fits the resonance described at Vol I:97. (3) "Dialect" is canon's word for spoken varieties (Counted Speech:245), so the change to "hand" is right for writing on copper. The recommendation (option 1, with option 3 as the bolder choice) stands.

findings.topic: The glyph associated with Gillus De Raits on a wax seal
findings.doc_claim: Corrant Papers, Entry the Third: "It was a specific glyph I had seen once before" and "It is the glyph associated with Gillus De Raits."
findings.canon: The 136 forms are attested and filed by Archon (Master Glyph Index page:40-65); none is a person's mark. But "A glyph name reduces letter by letter to lattice cells", so any name already has a written form (Descent:206-208), and a proper noun can be a glyph, as with the Moto seat (Master Glyph Index page:75). Check 38 fails unknown bracketed tokens (rules/pack-18-eighteen.yaml:394-395). The Warrant "oyeth" means "by a thing I made with my hands" (Counted Speech:173). An Entry petition needs "a named author who will stand behind it" (Alchemetrica:296).
findings.why_it_matters: The seal is the clue that ties Madeleine Ault's echo to De Raits. What kind of mark it is decides whether it is checkable, and whether it is unique to him.
findings.question: What is "the glyph associated with Gillus De Raits"?

options.label: His name traced as a Parun path (canon's Method gives every name a written form), written unbracketed
options.consequence: Canon-consistent, unique to him, passes Check 38, and leaves the Index untouched.

options.label: One of the 136 used as his personal mark, such as Lei (Binding) or Ma (Recall) to fit his Mortalis/Anamnesis
options.consequence: Checkable and meaningful, but a glyph others also use is weak proof of identity.

options.label: A house sigil, not Parun at all
options.consequence: The simplest option. "Glyph" becomes "sigil", and the link to Genesio's sealed stacks stays.

findings.recommendation: Option 1. It is how canon says any name is written, it stays unique to him, and it needs no change to the Index.
findings.correction: The status (absent_from_canon) and the need for a decision are right, but the finding misses canon that bears on the options. (a) "a Draft that was poured carries a maker's mark", read by trace examiners as evidence (The Gate:59; Accord Latin:85). This supports another option: De Raits's registered maker's mark as an alchemist, which also fits the fact that it was seen on a sealed Genesio document. (b) Gravemark Ink "Inscribes a name the Continuum registers" and is used for grave-seals (Standing Index:127). That is canon's precedent for a name written into a seal. (c) Option 1 has a cost the finding does not state. Accord Latin:108 holds that an instrument doing Aetheric work "is not a contract but a working", so a letter sealed with a Parun-traced name becomes a working in itself. Also, Descent:206-208 speaks of spell names; extending it to a person's name is an inference, with the Moto seat (Master Glyph Index page:75) as support. Revised recommendation: option 1 or the maker's-mark option. The maker's mark is lower-risk and just as unique to him.

findings.topic: Mu-jin's techniques under Glyphica canon, and his link to the Sealing failure
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica: the Third Corruption arises when the practitioner "does not properly execute the final Mortalis Sealing Glyph". Codex Vol III: a Volitional Trace in the Anamnesis Wellspring at Genesio "completes into me".
findings.canon: His Vocatia is "Spoken Parunic invocation over an open Draft-circle" (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:98), consistent with the Draft-circle carrying the four chains (Alchemetrica:166). His Fixation Anchor Sense "feels a Draft's Sealing Glyphs the way most people feel a held breath" (card:82), consistent with Sealing drawing on Fixatio chains (Spirit Rune Arts:50). He is harmonized with Anamnesis, which "reads inherited intention and unfinished formulae" (card:48) and fits the Genesio Trace. He has no Mortalis harmonization (card:48), and Authorization needs "genuine Wellspring harmonization with whatever process they inscribe" (Spirit Rune Arts:36). His Book of Summons says spoken Latin is "the authorization phrase" on top of Parun (Open Crucible:33). That conflicts with Parun being the grammar the Continuum reads (Descent:57-58), and with the Cant, rote Parun, being what licensed practitioners speak (Counted Speech:249). Outside this seam and noted only: card:48 lists "Fixation" (the Lists sheet has Fixatio), and Distillatio and Calcination are not among the Lists sheet's sixty.
findings.why_it_matters: Mu-jin's canon traits make him the natural witness of failing seals and of Anamnesis Traces. The same canon also bars him from lawfully authorizing a Mortalis operation, so the Codex has to respect both.
findings.question: In a Codex Mu-jin writes, what is his relationship to Category Three (Mortalis) work and its failing seals?

options.label: Detector only: his Fixation Anchor Sense feels impression-bodies' seals failing; without Mortalis harmonization he diagnoses and never performs Category Three
options.consequence: Fits the card exactly and makes him the natural witness of Incomplete Sealings. The Genesio completion works through his Anamnesis. The narrator performs no necromancy himself.

options.label: Give him Mortalis harmonization so he can perform it
options.consequence: Opens up the full plot, but needs a card change and a reason in his Temperance history.

options.label: Keep his senses out of the Mortalis material
options.consequence: No risk to the card, but it wastes the strongest link between the author and his subject.

findings.recommendation: Option 1, with his invocations written as Parun (Root or Cant) and Latin as the spoken label on top. It uses his canon traits as they stand, respects the harmonization rule, and keeps Parun as the only grammar that authorizes.
findings.correction: The question and recommendation stand; the Latin evidence is incomplete. Canon's summon register already sets "The spoken line in Guild Accord liturgical Latin, with the Parunic chain sitting underneath it" (Summon Register:34). So Latin over Parun is canon's normal form for a summons. The only conflict is the Open Crucible's word "authorization phrase" (:33). Latin cannot carry a warrant: the Vox register "has no first person" and "A speaker cannot put themselves into a working" (Accord Latin:84). "The Hands write boundaries onto laws. Latin writes agreements between people" (:108). Recommended fix: describe Latin as the spoken order (Nomen, Mensura, Iussum) layered over the Parun Authorization. That is mechanical under this canon. The rest checks out: card:48 (no Mortalis harmonization; Anamnesis "reads inherited intention and unfinished formulae"), card:82, card:98, and Vol III's "completes into me" (THE ALFTIAN CODEX VOLUME THE THIRD.md:228). Side notes outside this seam, also confirmed: "Fixation" at card:48 should be Fixatio, and Distillatio and Calcination are not among the sixty Wellsprings in the Lists sheet.

Spirit Rune Arts:36, :50. Descent:57-58. Counted Speech:249. Lists sheet: Fixatio is present; Fixation, Distillatio and Calcination are absent.

findings.topic: Rimward: Mu-jin's working with no Draft and a standing he did not hold
findings.doc_claim: The Codex's thesis, which Mu-jin now voices: "Correspondence is not reflection. It is response" (meta page flowchart). The Necrocursica sets "sustained Mechanica" against "lawful Glyphic syntax".
findings.canon: At Rimward, "He asked without one, as though he held a standing he did not have"; afterwards "he would not discuss what had answered" (Kwon Mu-jin.md:178). His house law is that a summoner "who claims a standing he lacks gets nothing" (:163). An over-warrant "is deducted from the speaker at the moment the Seal closes" (Counted Speech:110), from "the hands, the hearing, the teeth or the years" (:149); eyes are not on that list. "A forged authorization is Mechanica by definition" (Spirit Rune Arts:36), and Mechanica "always has a donor" (Mechanica page:19).
findings.why_it_matters: An author who writes about warrants, seals and Mechanica carries an unexplained unwarranted working of his own. Whether the Codex touches it, and what canon calls it, changes his card.
findings.question: Does Mu-jin's Codex touch Rimward, and if it does, what does canon call what he did?

options.label: Never named: he will not discuss it, as the card says, and the Codex's "response, not reflection" thesis carries it by implication
options.consequence: Honours the card and adds no new canon.

options.label: Over-warrant: the eye was the deduction taken at the Seal
options.consequence: A clean canon mechanism, but the Ring's register of deductions needs "the eyes" added.

options.label: Mechanica: something answered because something was taken from
options.consequence: An enormous consequence: Grade V, a donor, scarred ground at Rimward. It reshapes his card.

findings.recommendation: Option 1. The card says he would not discuss it, and a teacher who writes a treatise on warrants and seals while leaving out one entry of his own is stronger than an explanation.
findings.verify_evidence: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:163, :178 ("He asked without one, as though he held a standing he did not have"; he lost his right eye). Counted Speech:110, :149 (the deduction list names hands, hearing, teeth and years, not eyes). Spirit Rune Arts:36. Mechanica page:19. There is no Rimward row in RULINGS.md or CONFLICTS.md. Also worth noting for Isaac: the house law says an over-claimed standing "gets nothing" (card:163), while the Counted Speech says an over-warrant "seals" and is deducted (:110). Rimward sides with the Counted Speech, which adds weight to option 2 if he ever chooses to name it.

missed.topic: Gravemark Ink: a canon reagent for grave-seals that write a name
missed.detail: The Standing Index lists Gravemark Ink (T4, reserved T5), which "Inscribes a name the Continuum registers" and is used for "grave-seals that must hold against the thing under them". Its donor's carry "behaves as though it has an opinion about who is buried", and lawful supply falls short of demand. This is canon's closest material for the Category Three Mortalis seal, the step that keeps an impression-body temporary. It also offers a checkable medium for how De Raits could seal his work. Neither the Necrocursica nor the auditor uses it.
missed.evidence: wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Standing Index.md:127. Sources: THE NECROCURSICA.md:177; THE CORRANT PAPERS.md:151-155.
missed.question: Should the Category Three seal be scribed in Gravemark Ink, a real Standing Index reagent whose donor residue has "an opinion about who is buried"? Options: (a) yes, which ties Malphas's formula to a priced, scarce reagent and gives the Incomplete Sealing a material cause (short or diluted ink); (b) no, and leave the medium unnamed. Recommendation (a): it is canon already, and its supply shortfall gives Malphas's case a source of illicit supply for Vaughaus Thom's scaling.

missed.topic: Canon already explains the First Corruption through Authorization
missed.detail: Canon says that when a working is authorized, the Continuum reads the Engraver's Attraction Layer "and that reading becomes part of the rune's permanent structure". The Necrocursica instead has the Category Three chain use "the practitioner's Attraction Layer as a resonance guide" for the completion vector, which is a Direction job, and names as the First Corruption the practitioner's own patterns being absorbed into the Trace. Canon puts the Attraction Layer in the Authorization role, and that is exactly how a practitioner's own will would get written into the working. Moving it from Direction to Authorization is a small wording change that gives the First Corruption a direct canon basis. It sits on the seam between glyph roles and the Corruptions, so the Corruptions seam may own it.
missed.evidence: wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Rune Arts.md:36. Source: THE NECROCURSICA.md:173.

missed.topic: Spoken workings leave no author; cut or poured ones do
missed.detail: Canon says "A spoken working has no author in its own grammar ... A ward that was cut carries the cutter's hand. A Draft that was poured carries a maker's mark". The Bench of Attribution has spent 400 years trying to place a speaker at a scene. This matters for three findings. It weakens gcm-09's option 2 (an Authorization stamp from every practitioner). It supports gcm-06's option 1: the Category Three operation is inscribed, so it is attributable, and the Corrant investigation can therefore trace De Raits. And it affects how the Necrocursica's forensic Category One reads a scene.

seams.title: Craft economy: Index, tiers, costs, stats
seams.summary: Canon already has a full alchemy economy: 61 formulas in the Alchemical Index (T2 to T7), the Standing Index's T1 to T9 rank gates and Provenance, Fidelity and Carry marks, the Drafts ladder's EU-per-dose rungs, Alchemetrica's doctrine and the Heresiology's case law. It says almost nothing about the dead, though. There are only two Mortalis formulas (both T4 or below), no Dissolution formula, no table of Mortalis operations, no alchemy Sub-Stat profile and no Temperance Min column for alchemy. The five texts price nothing: they use a clearance scheme ("Accord Level III/IV/V") whose word "Level" collides with canon's character Level. Canon also contradicts itself in three places that decide how the Codex's alchemy should read. First, the live rule R2-6 says no Draft refills a reserve, while the Drafts ladder banks EU. Second, Alchemetrica ranks pure alchemists who have no Crystal on the Tiered Path, which defines every Tier as a Crystal transformation. Third, the texts disagree on how many residue categories there are. The Real Alchemy, which R18-5 makes a required source, is not in the repo, the vault or Notion, so Paracelsus's arsenic and mercury can only be checked against Alchemetrica's material sections.

findings.topic: Formulas touching the dead, memory, grief, residues (inventory)
findings.doc_claim: Corrant Papers:53 describes the Castlefall circle as drawn "in an ink that catches the light differently from ordinary ink" (a Mortalis ink, unnamed). None of the five texts names an Index formula.
findings.canon: Read from wiki/The Master Material Ledger/The Alchemical Index.md (the Notion sync from 09-26, newer than imports/alchemy/The Alchemical Index.merged.md). Each line gives tier, Wellspring, Family, Class and mechanism. Echo-Bloom Incense: T2, Oneirion/Verdantia, Limina, III. Thermoluminescence: the smoke empties a site's trapped Residue as light, and reading destroys the record (:32). Lantern Resin: T3, Anamnesis/Oneirion, Limina, II. Remanent magnetisation: it cures around one scene's field (:44). Stillgate Ash: T3, Mortalis, Vitalia, III. Grounding: the dead's residual field gets a path to earth, and living Essence bleeds the same way (:46). Gravetide Ink: T4, Mortalis/Abyntheus, Vitalia, III (IV on practitioner grave-dirt). The Boundary role made material for contracts with the dead (:68). Granite-Bone Mortar (T4, :63) and Will-Break Fumigant (T4, :76) use the dead as stock (bone-ash, grave-tallow) and become IV if the donor bore a Crystal. Obsidian Epoch Resin: T5, Nihiloth/Terranova, Limina, II. The glass transition traps a configuration as a record (:85). Dreamstone Shard Flask: T5, Oneirion/Exuroth, Limina, IV. A condensed grief-echo rendered from a person (:87). Corpus Marrow Salts: T5, Materia Primordia, Materia, IV. Soul Crystal shavings seed the donor's set (:90). Ethereal Current Oil: T5, Somnalis, Fluxia, III. Boundary-layer drag carries the departing field into the current, and an unlawful killing leaves the killer's Signature in it as a tracer (:92). Hollow-Watch Incense: T5, Tenebra, Limina, III. Stimulated emission releases one suppressed record (:93). Sever-Bond Twine: T5, Catharsis/Anamnesis, Caloria, II. A series circuit: it cuts pact, oath and summon loops whole (:100). Anamnesis Draught: T6, Anamnesis/Eidolyn, Limina, V. It drops the retrieval threshold to zero, and a Weave-Keeper is required (:109). Verdance Reclamation Draught: T6, Rebirthine, Vitalia, IV. It seeds the donor's Traits, grief included, into a successor across a Temperance transition (:111). Pyric Refinement Ash: T6, Exuroth, Caloria, III. Genuine regret sets the burn threshold (:114). Fossil Ring Dust: T6, Lethegraal, Limina, VI. 'Dead seconds' shorten a stalled era's constant (:115). Null-Essence Draught: T7, Nihiloth, Limina, VI. A name willingly forgotten is the antiphase, and it takes small records from everyone present (:124). The Codex Alchemical Index ($WOTR_TRUE_CANON/The Master Codex.xlsx) has no row whose Wellspring is Dissolution and only two Mortalis rows (#16 and #27). Adjacent Standing Index entries: Gravemark Ink, T4, IV/B/44, reserved T5 (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Standing Index.md:127). Cinder Bead Compound, T5, IV (:131). Namekeeper's Thread, T6 (:142). Mnemonis Solution, an Anamnesis Draft on the Draught rung, not entered (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/X. The Tier Ladders (Part Twenty-Four).md:216).
findings.why_it_matters: These are the only lawful building blocks a converted Codex can name without inventing a formula (R18-2, R18-5). The unnamed Mortalis ink at Castlefall has a ready canon identity in Gravetide Ink.
findings.mechanical_fix: Cite classes from the wiki page, not the import. Echo-Bloom Incense is Class III, not II (RULINGS.md:816, WAR-148: living hair is Class III). By WAR-148's rule that the highest-class ingredient sets Class (RULINGS.md:815), Stillgate Ash's bone-ash reads 'Class III, IV on a donor who bore a Crystal', like Granite-Bone and Deep Grid Mortar (Alchemical Index.md:63, :94). On the page itself (not part of the conversion), lines 19 to 22 repeat the stale intro ('Four entries') against the current count at :18 ('Twelve entries'). The unnamed ink at Corrant Papers:53 can be named Gravetide Ink (T4, Mortalis) with no new formula.
findings.correction: The inventory is accurate: every tier, Wellspring, Family, Class and line number checks out against the wiki Index. Two parts of mechanical_fix need changing. (1) Calling the Castlefall ink 'Gravetide Ink' is a creative choice, not a mechanical fix. Corrant:53 only says the ink is 'associated with Mortalis-adjacent practice'. Gravetide Ink's canon use is scripting 'contracts with the dead' (Codex #27). The only canon circle-drawn Mortalis material is Stillgate Ash, and it is a powder, not an ink. Move the naming into a decision (Gravetide Ink, Stillgate Ash, or leave it unnamed) or into ae-11's substrate question. (2) Giving Stillgate Ash 'IV on a donor who bore a Crystal' extends WAR-148 by analogy. WAR-148 named only Deep Grid and Granite-Bone. The extension is sound because the Codex ingredients include 'Bone-ash' and Standing Index:29 makes Crystal Draw Class IV, but it should be labelled as an extension, not presented as an existing ruling. The rest stands: Echo-Bloom is Class III per WAR-148 (RULINGS.md:816, wiki :32 against import :28), and the stale intro is at :22 against :18.
findings.verify_evidence: wiki/The Master Material Ledger/The Alchemical Index.md:18,22,26,32,36,44,46,56,63,68,76,81,85,87,90,92,93,94,100,105,109,111,114,115,120,124; imports/alchemy/The Alchemical Index.merged.md:28 (Echo-Bloom Class II); RULINGS.md:815-816; Codex Alchemical Index #16 Stillgate Ash ingredients 'Bone-ash, river-silt, cooled funeral-flame soot', #27 Gravetide Ink effect 'script contracts with the dead'; only two Mortalis rows and no Dissolution row among 61; Standing Index.md:29,127,131,142; X. The Tier Ladders:216

findings.topic: Alchemical Tiers T1 to T9 and their Temperance minimums
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:97 says the corporeal residue lasts in proportion to the Stage of the deceased, "ranging from hours in Stage I practitioners to years in Stage VII and above." The texts give no formula Tiers.
findings.canon: The Codex Alchemical Index has no Temperance Min column (headers: #, Name, Type, Glyphs, Wellsprings, Family, Physics Domain, Titan, Ingredients, Process, Effect, Tier, Risk, Mechanism, Notes). The Spell Index does have one ($WOTR_TRUE_CANON/The Master Codex.xlsx). The Codex Lists sheet's AlchTier column runs T1 to T8 only (Lists rows 2 to 9). The Standing Index keeps T9 and says the Codex vocabulary 'stops at T8' (The Standing Index.md:85). Standing Index rank gates: T1 none, then T2 Apprentice through T9 Paragon (:73-83). Tier of Standing maps to Stage (wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:64-79). The derived minimums are: T1 none; T2 Welling (II); T3 Ascension (III); T4 Flourishing (IV); T5 Splintering (V); T6 Transcendence (VIII); T7 Dissonance (XI); T8 Principality (XIII); T9 Revelation (XV). The FoW X Placement table uses the Alchemical Index T as the same 'Index rank' (X. The Tier Ladders:208-213). The texts' Roman-numeral Stages match canon: Stage VII is Refraction (II:72).
findings.why_it_matters: When a conversion says who may run a formula or operation, canon supplies the floor only through this chain, not through a column. Caveat: pure alchemists break the chain (see ae-05).
findings.mechanical_fix: State an alchemical minimum as the formula's Tier read through the Tier of Standing, for example 'Stillgate Ash, T3: a Journeyman, Ascension'. Never write 'Temperance Min' for an alchemical row as if the Codex listed one. Keep the texts' Stage numerals (I to XVI) as written.
findings.correction: There is a wrong line number: Stage VII Refraction is at II. Grades:70, not :72. There is also a substantive problem. The fix attaches a Stage floor to each alchemical Tier (T3 read as Ascension, and so on). Canon names the rank gates (Standing Index:75-83), and the gate names match the Tier of Standing names (II:64-79). But Alchemetrica:75 says only 'advancement gate[s] above Tier Five consult Temperance', and Alchemetrica:77 places Crystal-less alchemists at Tier Four. So a Stage floor for T1 to T5 alchemy is an inference that canon itself contradicts for pure alchemists. Mechanical fix: state an alchemical minimum as the Standing Index rank gate by name (for example 'Stillgate Ash, T3, Journeyman gate'). Add the Stage equivalent only for T6 and above, or only for Crystal-bearers. Never write 'Temperance Min' for an alchemical row.

Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:64-79 (VII Refraction at :70), :84; Alchemetrica.md:75,77; Necrocursica:97

findings.topic: What pays for a Draft: EU, vein depletion, stock
findings.doc_claim: None of the five texts puts a figure on anything. Vol II:223 says Mortalis "had been opened — not widely, not at scale, but opened in the specific, careful manner" for one commission.
findings.canon: A vein is 'the channel that feeds' a site (X. The Tier Ladders:443). A site drawn on steadily falls a rung, and one worked past what it can give 'gives out' (:482). Class I Vein Draw is 'Taken straight off a Wellspring vein by array' (The Standing Index.md:26). The alchemist channels a Wellspring 'through a material medium rather than through their own resonance' (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:35). A harmonised alchemist runs Drafts at 'roughly a quarter of the vein depletion' (:61), and the work is 'hurrying a thing along and then paying for the hurry' (:48). Mechanica 'depletes veins without reciprocal replenishment' (:277-279). A Draft is placed by 'the EU one dose holds' (X. The Tier Ladders:147). A pure alchemist has no Crystal and still makes Drafts (Alchemetrica:66). Canon is silent on how much vein depletion a batch causes, whether the maker spends any of their own EU, and what 'reciprocal replenishment' is.
findings.why_it_matters: Kwon's volumes must say what an operation costs, or they will reach for a word canon has not defined. 'Vein depletion' is the only cost term canon offers, and it has no number.
findings.question: When a converted text shows an alchemist at work, what pays for it?

options.label: Stock and the vein, not the maker's reserve
options.consequence: The Essence comes from the Provenance of the stock (Class I to VI) plus a draw on a vein. The maker pays in time, precision and body (crucible palsy), not EU. This fits pure alchemists, the Drafts ladder and Alchemetrica:35. No new numbers are needed.

options.label: The maker's EU pays a share, plus stock
options.consequence: Gives bench work an EU line. It breaks pure alchemists, who have no reserve, and it contradicts 'rather than through their own resonance'.

options.label: Vein draw counted on the sites ladder
options.consequence: A big working (Category III, the Genesio activation) visibly lowers a site's rung, which gives Vol III a measurable cost. It needs a draw-per-batch figure that canon does not have, and inventing one is forbidden until Isaac rules.

findings.recommendation: The first option, with the sites-ladder Draw used qualitatively and no figures. Canon already says the medium carries the working and pure alchemists work with no reserve, so the maker's EU cannot be what pays.
findings.correction: The Draft-specific silence is real, and the vein citations are right. But 'the maker's EU cannot be what pays' is too strong. Canon already charges makers from their reserve for standing workings: 'costs its maker a tenth of their reserve once', a quarter for proofed armour, and a hundredth per enhanced round (X. The Tier Ladders:560). This covers work 'enchanted, glyphed or worked beforehand' (X:509). So option 2 has a canon precedent, and its only real obstacle is pure alchemists, who have no reserve. The recommendation should read: stock plus vein draw for Drafts, with the arms-ladder reserve fraction noted as the existing precedent Isaac could extend to Crystal-bearing makers. Alchemetrica:35 ('through a material medium rather than through their own resonance') argues for option 1 but does not rule out option 2.
findings.verify_evidence: X. The Tier Ladders (Part Twenty-Four).md:147,443,482,509,560; Alchemetrica.md:35,48,61,66,277; Standing Index.md:26; rules/doc-essence-ledger-rulings-2026-09-25.yaml (R44-1..6, nothing on veins or Draft cost)

findings.topic: Can a Draft refill a practitioner? R2-6 against the Drafts ladder
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:277 heals a thinned Aether Shell through "Extended Wellspring Communion with Ascensio, Fixatio, or Benediction ... This takes months." Vol II:267 gives Tat 'pharmacological Essence-work'.
findings.canon: R2-6-REPLENISHMENT_RULE is live (rules/pack-02-two.yaml:222-237): 'no consumable restores a practitioner's magazine. Any technique, item or draft proposed to do so is refused at design.' The same line is restated in wiki/The War Cycle/The Long March.md:37 and wiki/War/The War Cycle.md:41. Against it, X. The Tier Ladders:148 says whatever a dose delivers 'is banked there' in the Crystal and 'A dose can overfill'. IX. The Essence Ledger:298 lists 'alchemical treatment' as Active Recovery. Neither CONFLICTS.md nor RULINGS.md records the clash.
findings.why_it_matters: Paracelsus is the Codex's physician-alchemist. Whether his medicines can put Essence back into a practitioner decides what his iatrochemistry and Category Two stabilisation can do on the page.
findings.question: Can a drinkable Draft put Essence back into a practitioner's reserve?

options.label: R2-6 governs: no Draft refills
options.consequence: Paracelsus's medicines heal bodies and steady Shells, and a Shell is rebuilt only by Wellspring communion, as the Necrocursica already says. The 'banked' sentence on the Drafts ladder goes to correction.

options.label: The Drafts ladder governs: doses bank EU
options.consequence: Philters and Elixirs refuel and can overfill. R2-6 and The Long March must be narrowed to 'raw Essence cannot be shipped'. Accord logistics changes.

options.label: Split: Drafts raise a reserve only as Threshold support, outside combat
options.consequence: Both pages need new wording, and it needs a ruling on what counts as Threshold support.

findings.recommendation: Log this in CONFLICTS.md for the docket. Meanwhile, write the conversion so that no Draft refuels a working reserve on the page. That text stands under any ruling, and the Necrocursica's months of communion already follows R2-6.
findings.verify_evidence: rules/pack-02-two.yaml:222-237 (R2-6-REPLENISHMENT_RULE, live in out/rules.resolved.json, verbatim matches); wiki/The War Cycle/The Long March.md:37; wiki/War/The War Cycle.md:41; X. The Tier Ladders:148 ('is banked there', 'A dose can overfill'); also X:212 Metering Tonic and :216 Mnemonis Solution 'sized to a Stage V reserve'; IX. The Essence Ledger:298; no entry in CONFLICTS.md or RULINGS.md (grep overfill/refill/R2-6 finds only unrelated technique rulings at RULINGS.md:841,862,868). CLAUDE.md forbids settling this as 'later beats earlier', so it is correctly a decision.

findings.topic: Crystal-bearer and pure alchemist, grain, the Weathering, and the Tiered Path
findings.doc_claim: Corrant Papers:49: "pharmacologists who work with Essence-adjacent materials for years develop a sensitivity to residual Aetheric impressions that they cannot name or systematise." Corrant Papers:59 names "the Soul Crystal of Paracelsus Furveus".
findings.canon: Alchemetrica:75: 'The Accord certifies both and ranks them on the same Tiered Path'. It places pure alchemists 'at Tier Four' (:77) and describes them as Class Ø, Dormant, undergoing the Weathering and acquiring grain that 'No instrument in the Accord reads' (:80-86). Against this, wiki/The Guild Accord/The Tiered Path.md:15 says each Tier is 'a measurable transformation of the Soul Crystal', and II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds:84 says 'Hollow and F confer no rank'. R45-3-ENHANCEMENT_CEILING (rules/doc-shot-and-enhanced-weapons.yaml:63) caps anything 'alchemically worked beforehand' at the maker's Grade, and canon never gives a Class Ø maker a Grade. Canon also has a separate workshop ladder, from Cinderhand to Master of the Circle to Alchemarch (Alchemetrica:306-316). One more defect in that page: Alchemetrica:80-86 and :88-92 are the same paragraph printed twice.
findings.why_it_matters: The conversion has to rank the Codex's alchemists and cap what they make. The Corrant pharmacologist is a ready-made case of grain, but canon cannot say where she ranks.
findings.question: In the converted texts, how is a Crystal-less alchemist ranked, and what caps what they make?

options.label: Alchemetrica governs for alchemists
options.consequence: Pure alchemists hold Tiers 1 to 5 by bench certification, and Temperance gates start only above Tier Five. The Tiered Path and R45-3 each need a carve-out.

options.label: The Tiered Path governs; rank alchemists on the workshop ladder
options.consequence: Pure alchemists hold no Tier of Standing and rank as Hand, Drafter or Master of the Circle. The sentence at Alchemetrica:75-77 needs rewording. The conversion stays clean.

options.label: Keep pure alchemists out of the five texts
options.consequence: The conflict never surfaces, and the grain beat in the Corrant Papers is lost.

findings.recommendation: For the conversion, rank alchemists on Alchemetrica's workshop ladder. It is canon and contradicts nothing. Write the Corrant pharmacologist as a pure alchemist whose sensitivity is grain, and keep Paracelsus a Crystal-bearer as Corrant Papers:59 says. File the Tiered Path, Alchemetrica and R45-3 tension for the docket.
findings.correction: The conflict is real, but one citation is wrong and better ones exist. R45-3-ENHANCEMENT_CEILING is scoped to enhanced weapons ('An enhanced weapon performs no higher than the Grade...'). It does not cap everything alchemically worked. Stronger evidence: VIII. Traits, Soul Crystal Tiers, Domains:69 lists 'Dormant ... Class Ø, pre-Initiate', which puts a Class Ø alchemist below Tier 1. X. The Tier Ladders:515 says 'An item Tier is the lower of what its material can hold and the Tier of Standing its maker stood at'. That is the real product cap, and it gives a maker with no Tier of Standing nothing to stand on. The duplicated passage is :82-86 reprinted at :88-92 (:80 is not repeated). Alchemetrica also contradicts itself: 'No Soul Crystal' at :66 against 'a Dormant Crystal' at :80. The recommendation says the workshop ladder 'contradicts nothing'. That dodges the question: the workshop ladder (Alchemetrica:308-316) is a rank inside a house, gives no Accord Tier, and so cannot answer what caps a pure alchemist's product under X:515. The question stays Isaac's.

Traits, Soul Crystal Tiers, Domains (Parts Twenty–Twenty-Two).md:69; VII. Aether Class:29; X. The Tier Ladders:509,515; rules/doc-shot-and-enhanced-weapons.yaml:63-73

findings.topic: Which stats and Sub-Stats govern alchemy
findings.doc_claim: The texts name no stats. Necrocursica:173 has Category Three "establish the completion vector using the practitioner's Attraction Layer as a resonance guide."
findings.canon: Several names have been retired. Diagnosis is absorbed into Gnosis Analysis (IV. The Eight Primaries and the Sixty-Four Sub-Stats:55). Inscription is absorbed into Ardency Density (:44). Parunic chain precision is Gnosis Fluency (:53). Tempering Coherence is 'The structural prerequisite for Threshold eligibility' (:105), and Clarity governs Essence waste (:102). Harmonics Attunement 'Reduces draw cost' (:76), and Vitality Filtration resists 'alchemical corrosives' (:29). Retired names are read as the entry that absorbed them (:18). Part Fifteen gives stat profiles for Sage Arts, Summoning, Spirit Rune Arts and Hataraki, and none for Draftcraft (V. Wellsprings, Attraction and Obsession, Magic Integration:160-195). Attraction against Obsession is tracked through Attunement against Tempering Coherence (:199). Mortalis strengthens Resilience Persistence and Gnosis Cognition (:98). Anamnesis strengthens Gnosis Retention, Gnosis Analysis and Resilience Anchoring (:122). The Families register still prints the retired 'Gnosis Diagnosis' and 'Resilience Coherence' (wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md:65). R18-5 names sources, not stats. Standing Index products already move Sub-Stats: Hillcarry Salts raises Clarity and Yield (:111), and Quiet-Hour Incense dulls Attunement (:109).
findings.why_it_matters: Converted cards and author notes need a stat line for Paracelsus, Malphas and Kwon's alchemy. Canon has no alchemy profile, and the retired names in the task brief would fail a terminology check (R14-5, rules/pack-14-fourteen.yaml:204).
findings.mechanical_fix: Use the senior names: Gnosis Analysis (not Diagnosis), Ardency Density (not Inscription), Resilience Anchoring (not Resilience Coherence). Tempering Coherence remains a live, separate Sub-Stat.
findings.question: Which Sub-Stats govern making a Draft and running a Mortalis operation?

options.label: Borrow the Spirit Rune Arts profile, plus Harmonics Attunement
options.consequence: No new rule. The profile is Gnosis Fluency; Ardency Density, Compression and Depth; Dexterity Finesse; Tempering Clarity; with Attunement for draw cost. It is the closest precedent: Parunic writing that persists without the maker.

options.label: Propose a Draftcraft profile
options.consequence: Map Alchemetrica's three layers. The Core seeding the material maps to Tempering Coherence and Maturity, Shell precision to Tempering Clarity, the Attraction Layer to Harmonics Attunement. Add Gnosis Analysis and Fluency for the Reading and the chain, and Vitality Filtration for exposure. It needs ratification.

options.label: Keep stats out of the texts and the notes
options.consequence: Fastest. Nothing mechanical explains why Paracelsus's precision matters.

findings.recommendation: Use the first option now in author notes, and file the second through propose_rule. It maps Alchemetrica:57-61 one-to-one onto existing Sub-Stats and invents nothing. The in-world prose names no Sub-Stats either way.
findings.correction: The retired-name mapping and absorptions are right (IV:18,29,44,53,55,76,92,102,105; Limina:65 still prints 'Gnosis Diagnosis' and 'Resilience Coherence'). Option 1 misstates the Spirit Rune Arts profile, which is at V:181-183, not :160-195 in general. The profile also includes Resilience (Ward, Hardening) as a primary and Dominion Gravity as a secondary, so the borrowed profile must carry them or say it drops them. Also worth citing: V:163 names 'inscribes a Parunic Draft' among the systems that pass through the stat framework, yet no Draftcraft profile follows. That confirms the gap. The question remains Isaac's.

findings.topic: The Real Alchemy, a required source, is missing
findings.doc_claim: Vol I (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:161): "His use of Arsenic and Mercury was reckless but not incorrect in principle." Checking this claim is exactly the job R18-5 gives The Real Alchemy.
findings.canon: R18-5-ALCHEMY_SOURCE_ORDER (rules/pack-18-eighteen.yaml:234-258): 'Three sources, consulted in this order, and none of them optional.' The Real Alchemy is described in sources/WOTR_Companion_Guide_Amendments_Pack_Eighteen.md:75. No page of that name exists in wiki/ (the 381-page mirror), in ~/wotr-vault/true-canon, or in Notion search (2026-09-28). CONFLICTS.md C-058 logged the missing Provenance Doctrine but not this page. The Bench of Attribution is present.
findings.why_it_matters: Every invented process in the conversion (Spagyria, the stabilisation protocol, Paracelsus's metals) is meant to be checked against this page before it reaches the page.
findings.question: The Real Alchemy page does not exist anywhere we can read. How should the alchemy conversion proceed?

options.label: Isaac points to or supplies the page
options.consequence: The alchemy passes wait until it is in the corpus.

options.label: Proceed without it and log the gap
options.consequence: Check process claims against Alchemetrica's material sections (Vessels, Heat, Lute, Menstrua, the bodily costs) plus real-history research through wotr-phenomenon. Add a CONFLICTS.md row like C-058. Some risk of divergence if the page turns up.

options.label: Write The Real Alchemy first
options.consequence: A new canon document for Isaac to ratify, which delays the conversion.

findings.recommendation: Proceed without it and log the gap. Alchemetrica already carries most of the real-world substrate the page was meant to hold (four-day calcinations, dung-bed Rot, luting, the four menstrua).
