seams.title: Setting, timeline, institutions
seams.summary: Canon puts the Voyager Era at 000–070 IC, the first era of the Imperial Age. The Four Ceilings says those decades "built nothing": iron could not be melted until 260–310 IC, and rail came later still, running on the Essence mains. So the texts' railways, platform coffee and carriages don't fit the Voyager Era. Mu-jin and Malphas both live in the Withering Era, the story's present (Year 715), so the authorship change already forces the era question. Almost all of the texts' geography and institutions are missing from canon: Castlefall, Urbis, the Trans-Alftian region, the Shaneni empire, the Heralds, Enforcer-Archivists, the clearance Levels and "Naln". Genesio and Tempus exist only as case names in the Heresiology. The texts also contradict each other on where the Archivum and Monastery stand, on the Castlefall–Genesio distance, and on the six-year versus twelve-year timeline. Three fixes are mechanical: the division name, the "current Epoch's reckoning" wording, and the coal smoke. That last one also turned up a conflict inside canon that nobody has logged. Outside this seam: Codex Vol II docx line 67 says "the fourteen Temperance stages", but canon has sixteen.

findings.topic: Which era the texts are written in, and whether rail is an anachronism
findings.doc_claim: Every text carries the era stamp. Vol I (wiki Volume the First.md:14): "Transcribed from the Archivum of the Heralds, Urbis — Era of Voyagers". Corrant Papers:286: "Era of Voyagers, Urbis". The same texts ride trains. Vol II docx:213: "Neros and I took the railway to Urbis". Vol III docx:40: "Castlefall — the railway platform".
findings.canon: The Voyager Era runs 000–070 IC. It is the first of three eras inside the Imperial Age (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Concordance of Ages.md:44, :108, :110, :157). Its technology: "The first decades of the Imperial Age built nothing" (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Four Ceilings.md:155). Iron first melted 260–310 IC (Four Ceilings.md:192-194). A railway is "the main, laid on its side" (Four Ceilings.md:241; wiki/Geography & the Four Quarters/The Bearing and the Holding.md:49). Rail arrived "in the first generation of the mains" (Four Ceilings.md:275), and the mains' founding instruments are about 400 years old (wiki/The Magic System/Mechanica Extraction Without Recognition.md:65). The story present is Year 715, Withering Era (Concordance:14, :130), and the Accord's communion is forming now (rules/doc-combat-society-politics-law-2026-09-26.yaml:186 R60-09; RULINGS.md:2087 C-084). R53-01 (rules/doc-world-texture-law-2026-09-26.yaml:19) says 1800s–1950s technology "exists across" the Imperial Age, and R59-04 (rules/doc-era-apparatus-law-2026-09-26.yaml:83) allows "railways where they run". Read literally, R53-01 would allow rail at 0–70 IC, but the Concordance's sequence of ceilings rules it out. This tension is not in CONFLICTS.md. Both new authors live in the present: Mu-jin is 24 (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:26) and 38 in the Academy arc (wiki/The Table — Running Pieces/State of Play — Kwon Mu-jin Aetherion Academy.md:13). Malphas's cell works a coldhouse "on a main capped four years" (wiki/Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/The Mother.md:58). "Era of Voyagers" is also not the canon form of the name, which is "the Voyager Era".
findings.why_it_matters: The era decides two things: whether the rail, platform stalls and carriages are anachronisms, and whether Mu-jin and Malphas can be the authors at all. The Voyager Era closed roughly 645 years before their lifetimes.
findings.question: In which era of the Imperial Age are the Codex, the Necrocursica and the Papers written? The age has three eras: the Voyager Era (years 0–70), the Long Reckoning (70–645) and the Withering Era (645 to now, the story's present).

options.label: A. Withering Era, the story's present
options.consequence: Rail, trams and coffee stalls are already canon there, and Mu-jin and Malphas can be the authors. Every "Era of Voyagers" stamp is replaced (Vol I:14, Vol II docx:5 and :281, Vol III docx:354 and :406, Corrant:107, :125, :286, and the wiki meta pages Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:14 and Lore & History.md). Lines about the Accord have to read as the Accord still forming, circle by circle.

options.label: B. Keep the Voyager Era, spelled the canon way
options.consequence: All rail, carriages, platform coffee and coal must go. Mu-jin and Malphas cannot be the authors, because they live more than 600 years later. Nothing on Malphas's card supports a seven-century lichdom.

options.label: C. The late Long Reckoning (after the mains, about 400–645 IC)
options.consequence: Rail becomes possible and the texts become historical documents recovered in the present. The authorship change still fails.

findings.recommendation: A. Both new authors are present-day characters, and every piece of the texts' texture (rail, the platform stall, the red-brick lowland cities) is already canon in the Withering Era. It also keeps these texts out of the R53-01 versus Concordance question.
findings.correction: The core claim holds: Voyager Era 000–070 IC, iron not melted until 260–310, rail in 'the first generation of the mains', Year 715 is the present, and R53-01, R59-04 and R59-01 are all live. Three fixes. (1) The stamp list is wrong. wiki/Lore & History/Lore & History.md carries no 'Era of Voyagers'. The missing places are wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the Second.md:14 and Volume the Third.md:235, alongside Vol I:14, Vol II docx:5 and :281, Vol III docx:354 and :406, Corrant:107, :125 and :286, and Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:14. (2) The auditor missed that canon already comments on these codices. Errata:39 says the Guild examined 'the Alftian codices' and 'finds that not one of them cites an Age'. Every era stamp therefore contradicts canon on its face, so add option D: strip the era stamps entirely and let the texts' texture date them. D fits Errata:39 exactly and combines with A. (3) Option C's floor is off. Mechanica:65 says the mains' founding instruments are 'four hundred years old', so the mains, and rail with them, go back to about 315 IC, not 400. Recommendation: A combined with D (present-day texture, no era stamp).
findings.verify_evidence: Concordance of Ages.md:110, :112 (Divisions and Tiered Path date to the Voyager window), :117, :130; Four Ceilings.md:155, :192-194, :241, :275; Mechanica Extraction Without Recognition.md:65; rules/doc-world-texture-law-2026-09-26.yaml:19; doc-era-apparatus-law:83; out/rules.resolved.json (R53-01, R59-04 live); Errata to the Received Registers.md:39; grep of wiki for 'Era of Voyagers' (hits only Volume the First.md:14, Volume the Second.md:14, Volume the Third.md:235, Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:14); source docx lines checked.

findings.topic: Coal smoke in the railway carriage
findings.doc_claim: Corrant Papers:185: "a railway carriage that smells of damp wool and coal smoke".
findings.canon: R59-01 is live: "Draw-fed engines replace coal and steam outright" (rules/doc-era-apparatus-law-2026-09-26.yaml:18). The Bearing and the Holding.md:49 says the same: "Nothing burns and nothing boils, and there is no steam engine anywhere in the four quarters, on rails or off them". Four Ceilings.md:243 agrees. But the same two pages also carry a stray paragraph describing a coal boiler: Bearing and the Holding.md:55, "It burns coal, it carries its own water", and Four Ceilings.md:247-249. That paragraph contradicts the live ruling, and CONFLICTS.md has no row for it.
findings.why_it_matters: Coal smoke on a train implies a steam engine, and Isaac's live ruling rules steam out. The stray canon paragraph could mislead the conversion if nobody logs it.
findings.mechanical_fix: Corrant:185: replace "damp wool and coal smoke" with a smell from the Essence-driven line, e.g. "damp wool and warm brass" (the engine rides the conduit and nothing burns). The steam from coffee cups (Vol III docx:44) can stay. Separately, the coal-boiler paragraph at Bearing and the Holding.md:55-57 and Four Ceilings.md:247-251 should get its own CONFLICTS.md row against R59-01. It is not ruled here.
findings.verify_evidence: Corrant:185 'smells of damp wool and coal smoke'; rules/doc-era-apparatus-law-2026-09-26.yaml:18 R59-01 (live); Bearing and the Holding.md:49 (no steam), :55 ('It burns coal'), :57 (coal arriving to heat); Four Ceilings.md:243, :247-249 (the coal-boiler paragraph; :250-251 is the costing paragraph, not coal). CONFLICTS.md has no boiler or coal row, and RULINGS.md:1972 is R59-01's source.

findings.topic: "The current Epoch's reckoning" used as a date
findings.doc_claim: Vol I (wiki Volume the First.md:40): "older than the Heralds — possibly older than the current Epoch's reckoning". Vol II docx:149: "older than the Herald tradition, older than the current Epoch's reckoning".
findings.canon: Epochs have no count. wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/Errata to the Received Registers.md:34: "No calendar existed. No observer stood outside the Epoch to mark its passage." Errata :38: an Epoch figure "is not to be placed on the Age count". The only count is the Concordance's, from −1,400 to the present (Concordance of Ages.md:22-24).
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase treats an Epoch as a calendar, which the Errata forbids by name. The fix is small.
findings.mechanical_fix: Replace "the current Epoch's reckoning" with "the count" ("possibly older than the count itself") at Vol I:40 and Vol II docx:149, and in the wiki condensation of Vol II if it carries the phrase. Vol III docx:5, "the year of the Accord's current reckoning", can stay: it names the single Imperial count (Concordance:22).
findings.correction: The Errata does not forbid the phrase 'by name'. Its rule (Errata:38) bars placing an Epoch figure on the Age count, and the texts give no figure. Errata:35 lets a register tie an origin to an Epoch, and Errata:39 explicitly clears 'the Alftian codices' as 'never in conflict with the count'. The only friction is that 'reckoning' implies an Epoch calendar, which Errata:34 says never existed. Downgrade the status from conflict to minor wording. The replacement ('older than the count itself', or 'older than the Epoch's turning') is optional polish, not a canon-required fix.
findings.verify_evidence: Errata to the Received Registers.md:31-39; Volume the First.md:40; Vol II docx:149.

findings.topic: Name of the Guild Accord division
findings.doc_claim: Corrant Papers:3: "Enforcer-Archivist, Guild Accord — Research Archives Division". The same form appears at Corrant:17, 43, 71, 231, 241 and 281, Vol III docx:404, Necrocursica:497, and wiki Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:83.
findings.canon: The canon name is "Research and Archives" (wiki/The Guild Accord/The Guild Accord in the Modern Era — Divisions, Companies, Academies and Offices.md:53; wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemetrica.md:14; Concordance of Ages.md:14; wiki/Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/The Bench of Attribution.md:14). The short form "the Research Division" is also canon (Concordance:75, :133), so Vol III docx:314 can stay.
findings.why_it_matters: The division's name is misspelled in every cross-reference line.
findings.mechanical_fix: Change "Research Archives Division" to "Research and Archives Division" at every occurrence.
findings.verify_evidence: Modern Era — Divisions…md:53 'Research and Archives'; Alchemetrica.md:14; Concordance:14; Bench of Attribution.md:14; Concordance:75 and :133 'Research Division'. Every listed occurrence was checked: Corrant:3, 17, 43, 71, 231, 241, 281; Vol III docx:404; Necrocursica:497; Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:83.

findings.topic: Where the Trans-Alftian region sits on the canon map (the terraces, Castlefall, the eastern lowlands)
findings.doc_claim: Vol I:20: "a creature of the Alftian lowlands, son of terrace-farmers who smelled of limestone and good rain". Castlefall is "A castle-city in a mountain-cut valley" (Vol I:67), about 600 m up (Corrant:185). The nobleman lives "in the eastern lowlands" (Vol II docx:27).
findings.canon: Castlefall, Trans-Alftian, the Alftian terraces and the eastern lowlands appear nowhere outside these texts (repo grep). The only other "Alftian" in canon is Errata:39, which names "the Alftian codices" as registers that cite no Age. In canon, "east" is a whole quarter, the New World (wiki/Geography/Geography & the Four Quarters.md:25). Mu-jin's canon ground is the Inner World. He was born at Sum-gol (Kwon Mu-jin.md:162). Sum-gol lies in Ketsuen, a state running "from the northeastern shield's limestone valleys ... south through Sum-gol" (wiki/The Inner World — The Northern Shield/The Sovereign Enclave of Ketsuen — The Crow's Reach.md:20). Ketsuen has river-valley farming (:68), high-altitude herbs prized by alchemists and dense natural seeps in the Uplands (:72), and a Corridor road to Nalūn (:70).
findings.why_it_matters: Mu-jin now has to walk the Codex's route himself. If the region is off his canon map, his card and the texts disagree about his life. The name "Alftian" (elvish in origin) was built for an elf narrator; renaming is for the naming seam.
findings.question: Where on the canon map does the Trans-Alftian region (terraces, Castlefall, Genesio, Urbis, the eastern lowlands) sit, now that Mu-jin is the traveller?

options.label: A. In the Inner World, between Ketsuen and the Concord heartland
options.consequence: The terraces become Ketsuen's limestone valleys, Genesio sits in the Uplands and Urbis is a heartland city. The invented names survive, including the Heresiology's Genesio case, and Mu-jin travels ground his card already covers. Needs one geography note on the Ketsuen or Inner World page.

options.label: B. Replace the invented places with canon ones (Sum-gol, the Uplands, a Nalūn or Concord city)
options.consequence: The fewest new places. Heresiology case IV and many lines get renamed, and a canon town has to get rail for the Castlefall platform scene.

options.label: C. Keep a separate invented region outside the mapped kingdoms
options.consequence: The least rewriting. It adds more unplaced geography and puts Mu-jin far from Sum-gol, Rimward and the Ashgate road.

findings.recommendation: A. Ketsuen already has limestone valleys, alchemists' high-altitude herbs, dense seeps and way-stations. The texts' region can sit there without inventing a new corner of the world or pulling Mu-jin off his map.
findings.verify_evidence: Volume the First.md:20, :67; Vol II docx:27; Corrant:185. Ketsuen page :20 (limestone valleys through Sum-gol), :68, :70, :72; Kwon Mu-jin.md:162; Errata:39 is the only other 'Alftian'. The auditor's aside that the name is 'elvish in origin' has no canon citation and should be dropped. The ws-18 correction, that Sum-gol was emptied, does not change this recommendation.

findings.topic: The Shaneni empire, where Jabir comes from
findings.doc_claim: Vol I:93: "He had come from the Shaneni empire's borders, and his knowledge was a synthesis of traditions most scholars treated as incompatible." Vol III docx:402 names him "Jabir ibn Hayyan", a real historical person; the wiki condensation already cut it to "Jabir" (Volume the Third.md:233). The real name belongs to the naming seam and is only noted here.
findings.canon: "Shaneni" appears nowhere in canon. The only lost empire in canon is the High Empire of Eresse, dated "First Eon, Great Spirit War Era" (wiki/The Elven Peoples/The High Empire of Eresse.md:14), which ended long before anyone living could come from its borders. In canon, east is the New World quarter (Geography & the Four Quarters.md:25). Mu-jin's own card calls his line "Eastern Concord-adjacent" (Kwon Mu-jin.md:25).
findings.why_it_matters: Jabir's "eastern tradition" is half of the Codex's Hermetic synthesis. Where it comes from decides whether the story adds a new polity to the map.
findings.question: Is the Shaneni empire a new living polity, or should Jabir come from a place canon already has?

options.label: A. Keep Shaneni as a new living empire east of the Alftian region
options.consequence: Adds a polity that the Powers of the Imperial Age page and the map will need.

options.label: B. Jabir comes from the New World, the eastern quarter
options.consequence: No new polity. The eastern tradition anchors to a canon quarter, which has elven old-ground and its own law.

options.label: C. Jabir comes from the Concord east, Mu-jin's own "Eastern Concord"
options.consequence: Makes the eastern Hermetic tradition part of Mu-jin's inheritance, but ties it to the unresolved origin question in ws-18.

findings.recommendation: B. It adds nothing to the map and stays clear of Mu-jin's unsettled origin.
findings.verify_evidence: Volume the First.md:93 and :160; no 'Shaneni' elsewhere in the wiki (grep); High Empire of Eresse.md:14; Geography & the Four Quarters.md:25; Kwon Mu-jin.md:25; Vol III docx:402 'Jabir ibn Hayyan'; Volume the Third.md:233 'Jabir'.

findings.topic: What and where Genesio is, and how far it is from Castlefall
findings.doc_claim: Vol I:27 has a town: "The Archivum in Genesio — squat, salt-weathered", with streets (:39) and a craft district (:44). Vol III docx:174: "Genesio mountain territory — three days' travel from Castlefall". Corrant:205: "approximately four hundred kilometres north of Castlefall". Necrocursica:365 has a platform at "a Genesio waystation". Corrant:51 mentions "the Accord facility in Genesio".
findings.canon: Genesio exists in canon only as the Heresiology's case "IV · The Genesio Activation Sequence" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:211). Travel rates: "foot about 20 miles a day, mounted 30 to 40, rail where it runs, less in snow and passes" (rules/doc-world-texture-law-2026-09-26.yaml:199, R53-08). Four hundred km is about 250 miles: 6–8 days mounted, or under a day by rail. Neither makes three days. In the provinces, "The railway reaches the county town and stops" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Works and Days — Occupations, Trades and Technology.md:259). A possible hook: Antediluvian cities were built on top of Wellsprings (Concordance:66), which suits Genesio's cyclopean hall over a dense, old Wellspring.
findings.why_it_matters: The distance and the "three days" cannot both be true under R53-08. The texts also treat Genesio as both a town and a mountain territory.
findings.question: How far is Genesio from Castlefall, and how does a traveller get there?

options.label: A. 400 km: one day by rail to a railhead, then two days mounted up the passes in midwinter
options.consequence: Both figures stay true under R53-08. The Necrocursica's Genesio platform becomes the railhead. Genesio becomes a territory whose town holds the Archivum.

options.label: B. Three days mounted, about 100–120 miles, with no rail to Genesio
options.consequence: Cut "four hundred kilometres" from Corrant:205. The Genesio platform in the Necrocursica goes.

options.label: C. Rail all the way, 400 km in under a day
options.consequence: Cut "three days' travel" from Vol III:174. Genesio becomes a rail town and loses its remote-hollow feel.

findings.recommendation: A. It keeps every figure the texts give and fits the canon rule that provincial railways stop at the county town.
findings.verify_evidence: Volume the First.md:27, :39, :44; Vol III docx:174 'three days' travel'; Corrant:205 'approximately four hundred kilometres north'; Necrocursica:365 'a Genesio waystation'; Corrant:51; Heresiology:211; rules/doc-world-texture-law-2026-09-26.yaml:199 (R53-08, live); Works and Days:259; Concordance:66.

findings.topic: Where the Herald's Archivum and Monastery are (Urbis or Genesio)
findings.doc_claim: Vol I:14: "Archivum of the Heralds, Urbis". Vol I:27: "The Archivum in Genesio". Vol II docx:5: "lower Archive of the Herald's Monastery, Urbis", but Vol II docx:282: "sealed lower stacks of the Herald's Archivum, Urbis". Corrant:69: "Genesio — The Heralds' Archivum, Lower Stacks". Necrocursica:5: "confinement at the Genesio Monastery". Vol III docx:404 and :406 name both a "Genesio Archivum" and an "Urbis Archivum".
findings.canon: Canon is silent. Neither site exists outside these texts.
findings.why_it_matters: The recovery, filing and sealing lines on all five documents depend on which house holds what.
findings.question: Are there one or two Herald Archivums, and where is the Monastery?

options.label: A. Two houses of one order
options.consequence: The Genesio Archivum is the old house with the sealed lower stacks, and the Urbis Archivum is the order's seat. One Monastery, at Urbis. Almost every line survives. Fix Vol II docx:5 ("Monastery" to "Archivum") and Necrocursica:5 ("Genesio Monastery" to "the Genesio house").

options.label: B. One Archivum, at Genesio only
options.consequence: Every "Urbis Archivum" filing and address line moves, including Gillus's letter address in Vol II docx:183.

options.label: C. One Archivum, at Urbis only
options.consequence: Vol I's Genesio reading room, Corrant's Genesio stacks and the Necrocursica's sealing all move to Urbis.

findings.recommendation: A. The fewest edits, and it reads naturally: an old outlying house plus a seat.
findings.verify_evidence: Volume the First.md:14 and :27; Vol II docx:5 and :282; Corrant:69; Necrocursica:5 and :13; Vol III docx:404 and :406. The texts are internally inconsistent as described. Corrant:71 adds that Research and Archives staff work inside the Genesio Archivum ('my first three years at the Research Archives Division'), which supports option A.

findings.topic: The Heralds as an institution (Archivum, Monastery, Medical University, the humming bridges)
findings.doc_claim: Vol I:102: "a Heraldic bridge vibrating with the low sustained hum of God-Essence channelled through Herald-crafted stone". Vol I:59: "Herald's Medical University". Corrant:151: "It was not an Accord seal. It was not a Herald's seal."
findings.canon: No Herald order exists in canon (repo grep and wiki search). In canon, heralds are individual servants: an Archon "has a seat, a court, a lineage of heralds" (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Fourteen Titans.md:20). Canon expects monasteries without naming one: "Monasteries · Teach the Great Work as discipline before technique" (Heresiology:218). The Accord's academies run from Scholar to Chair (Modern Era VI, same page as ws-04). Stone that hums with Essence matches canon's inscribed arrays (Concordance:95-98).
findings.why_it_matters: The Heralds own most of the Codex's settings. Whatever they are sets the tone of Vol I and the chain of custody for all five documents.
findings.question: What are the Heralds, the body that runs the Archivum, the Monastery, the Medical University and the humming bridges?

options.label: A. A new Hermetic teaching order, older than the Accord's communion
options.consequence: Needs a Factions page. It fills the Heresiology's unnamed "Monasteries" duty and keeps the Codex's monks, Prior and Sacred Discourse as written.

options.label: B. An Archon's lineage of heralds that grew into an institution
options.consequence: Ties the order to canon cosmology. Isaac has to pick which Archon, and Asclepius's atheism becomes open defiance.

options.label: C. Fold them into the Accord's academies and the Alchemists' Society
options.consequence: No new order. The Medical University becomes a chartered academy, but the Monastery and the God-Essence bridges need a different owner.

findings.recommendation: A. The texts are monastic at their core, and canon already expects such monasteries. It costs one page and no rewrites of the Accord.
findings.correction: Option B is stronger than the auditor presents it. Canon already has an Archon's herald who fits these texts: Vaerath Ashveil, 'Herald of Auren. Death-Speaker', and Auren is the Archon of Death. Maelor (Memory) is a second candidate, tied to the Anamnesis material. Option B should read: 'the Heralds grew out of Auren's (or Maelor's) herald-lineage'. The consequence is that it ties the Mortalis-heavy Codex straight to a live character card, Vaerath, which Isaac must accept or refuse. Recommendation A can stand, but the question should put the Auren link to Isaac. Minor fix: the academy ranks run Scholar to Chair at Modern Era:112-116, not a section 'VI'.
findings.verify_evidence: Fourteen Titans.md:20 ('a lineage of heralds'); Vaerath Ashveil · The Pale Reaping.md:24 and :136; Fourteen Archons.md:100 (Maelor, Memory) and :108 (Auren, Death); Heresiology:218; Modern Era:112-116; Volume the First.md:59, :102, :122.

findings.topic: Urbis, and where the Research and Archives Division sits
findings.doc_claim: Corrant:231: "addressed to the Research Archives Division, Guild Accord, Urbis". Vol I:130: "a city-state in the Urbis orbit". Vol II docx:249: "Urbis's Heraldic spires".
findings.canon: Urbis does not exist in canon. The Research and Archives Division's instrument is the Archives Eternal (Modern Era:53), sealed "beneath the Council Spire of the Concord Citadel" (Concordance:14). The Citadel is "a nexus suspended between planes" (wiki/The Guild Accord/The Concord Citadel.md:15). The Concord heartland is where the Accord is strong, with "the chancery schools, the conduit network at its densest" (Modern Era:41).
findings.why_it_matters: The Papers address the Division at Urbis, but canon seats it at the Citadel.
findings.question: What is Urbis: a new heartland city with a regional Research and Archives office, or the Citadel's own city?

options.label: A. A new city in the Concord heartland with a regional Research and Archives office
options.consequence: The Archives Eternal stays at the Citadel and Halveth runs a regional desk. Needs one line of geography. Rail and trams fit an Accord city (R59-05).

options.label: B. Urbis is the City Below of the Concord Citadel
options.consequence: The Papers become Citadel documents. But the Citadel is visible only to those bound to the Lattice, so a railway into it needs new invention.

options.label: C. Replace Urbis with a canon city (Stannvaard or Altherion)
options.consequence: No new city. The Heraldic spires, the Medical University and Vis's east-facing room move there.

findings.recommendation: A. The Division address and the rest of the Papers work with no new metaphysics.
findings.correction: The substance holds: Urbis is absent, and the Archives Eternal sits beneath the Council Spire of the Citadel. Fix option C: Altherion is a kingdom (a republic that houses the Grand Church of Sancta Lux), not a city, and Stannvaard is a Guild Seat. Option C should read 'replace Urbis with Stannvaard, or with a city in Altherion'.
findings.verify_evidence: Concordance:14; Modern Era:41 and :53; Concord Citadel.md:15; Sancta Lux.md:178 ('the Kingdom of Altherion'); INDEX.md:402 (The Guild Seat of Stannvaard); Sky, the Hour and the Year.md:56.

findings.topic: "Naln": the Silent Archivists and the Accord observation post
findings.doc_claim: Vol II docx:281: "Transcribed by the Silent Archivists of Naln, Era of Voyagers". Corrant:25: "independently verified by the Accord's own observation post at Naln".
findings.canon: "Naln" appears nowhere. The wiki meta page itself admits "The Archivists are not otherwise described anywhere in this wiki" (wiki/Lore & History/Lore & History.md:33). Canon has Nalūn (nah-LOON), an Inner World salt kingdom on "the southeastern margin of the northern shield" (wiki/The Inner World — The Northern Shield/The Kingdom of Nalūn — The Chain-Cities.md:22). It has Vaultmere, "the counting city" of archivists and sealed chambers (:48), and a Measurewright station at Deepvein (:50). "Naln" is "Nalūn" with the ū dropped, but canon does not say they are the same place.
findings.why_it_matters: Two orphan names could anchor to a canon kingdom that neighbours Ketsuen and is already on Mu-jin's road (Rimward).
findings.question: Is "Naln" the kingdom Nalūn with a lost diacritic, or a different place?

options.label: A. It is Nalūn
options.consequence: The Silent Archivists are Vaultmere's archivists, and the observation post is the Measurewright station at Deepvein. Two orphans tie to canon.

options.label: B. A separate new place called Naln
options.consequence: Adds a name one letter away from a canon kingdom, which readers will take for a typo.

options.label: C. Cut Naln
options.consequence: The Research and Archives Division does the transcription and the Measurewrights do the verification.

findings.recommendation: A. The names match, and Vaultmere and Deepvein already do exactly those two jobs.
findings.correction: Three fixes. (1) Rimward is placed in Nalūn by the Natsume Kurogiku card:139 ('Rimward, the eastern frontier city of Nalūn'), not by Ara Min Mahuo.md:177, which never names the kingdom. (2) The Vaultmere and Deepvein profiles the recommendation relies on are marked 'Originated and pending ratification' on the Nalūn page (:159). They are not settled canon. (3) Deepvein is the lowest city of a subterranean salt basin, and its Measurewright station measures contracts, so it is an implausible post for watching a planet drift. Revised option A: Naln is Nalūn, and the Silent Archivists are Vaultmere's archivists (pending ratification). The Tempus drift is verified by the Measurewrights' instrument chair (Bench of Attribution.md:35), not by Deepvein. This also lines up with ws-14's recommendation.
findings.verify_evidence: Kingdom of Nalūn page :22, :48, :50, :159; Natsume Kurogiku · The Knot-Shearer.md:139; Ara Min Mahuo.md:177; Lore & History.md:33; Corrant:25; Vol II docx:281.

findings.topic: The Enforcer-Archivist title, the new Papers author's office, and the "Trans-Alftian Accord"
findings.doc_claim: Corrant:3: "Oren Corrant, Enforcer-Archivist, Guild Accord". Necrocursica:5: "Alchemist-Scribe of the Trans-Alftian Accord".
findings.canon: No such title exists. Enforcement (the Sealwrights) and Research and Archives are separate Divisions in opposing voting blocs (Modern Era:51, :53, :57). Trace examiners read workings as evidence (rules/doc-combat-society-politics-law-2026-09-26.yaml:231, R60-11). The crown's Night Watch Society "investigates illegal magic" (wiki/Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/The Night Watch.md:21). The Lattice Classification Bureau classifies cases (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Edwyn Brack.md:22). There is one Accord, forming through signed circles (Modern Era:37), and no "Trans-Alftian Accord".
findings.why_it_matters: The Papers' new author needs an office that canon can hold. The combined title straddles two rival Divisions.
findings.question: What office does the new Papers author hold?

options.label: A. A field archivist of the Research and Archives Division (drop "Enforcer")
options.consequence: Halveth and the Division frame stay as written, with no cross-bloc title.

options.label: B. An Enforcement Sealwright seconded to Research and Archives
options.consequence: Keeps the enforcer edge, and the rivalry between the two Division blocs becomes texture.

options.label: C. A Night Watch Society investigator on the crown's warrant
options.consequence: Sets the Papers against Malphas's cult, which watches the Night Watch most closely (The Mother.md:104). Halveth's Research frame has to be rewritten as a crown office.

findings.recommendation: A, the least disruption. Pick C only if Isaac wants a live thread between the Papers and Malphas. Either way, restate "Trans-Alftian Accord" as "a Trans-Alftian circle of the Accord" or cut it.
findings.verify_evidence: Corrant:3, :19, :241, :285; Necrocursica:5; Modern Era:37, :51, :53, :57; rules/doc-combat-society-politics-law-2026-09-26.yaml:231 (R60-11; verbatim at :240); Night Watch.md:21; Edwyn Brack.md:22; The Mother.md:104.

findings.topic: Accord clearance Levels III–VI, and the Bench
findings.doc_claim: Corrant:5: "Level IV Clearance Required". Necrocursica:13: "Level VI Clearance". Necrocursica:161, :169 and :173 put Categories One to Three at Levels III, IV and V.
findings.canon: Canon has no numbered clearance levels. People are gated by Tier: "S-Tier clearance or higher" (wiki/The Guild Accord/The Concord Military.md:63), and the Tiered Path has ranks 1–9 (wiki/The Guild Accord/The Tiered Path.md:23-31). Texts are gated by the Heresiology's seizure classes: "preservable under ward · preservable under redaction · transmissible only by excerpt · seal-only" (Heresiology:196). The Bench of Attribution rules "who is permitted to hold the result" (Bench of Attribution.md:25).
findings.why_it_matters: The Levels would be a new access system alongside canon's Tier-based and text-class machinery. The mechanism seam depends on the same Category authorisations.
findings.question: Keep the numbered clearance Levels (III–VI), or restate access in canon's own terms?

options.label: A. Restate in canon terms
options.consequence: Documents carry Heresiology classes (the Necrocursica is seal-only; the Papers are transmissible only by excerpt). People are gated by Tier of Standing, and lawful use goes through a Bench entry. No new system. The Necrocursica's Category authorisations need Tier numbers instead.

options.label: B. Keep Levels III–VI as an internal Research and Archives access scale
options.consequence: One new scale to define and map to Tier. The texts barely change.

options.label: C. Mixed: Levels only for archive access, Tiers for operations
options.consequence: Two systems side by side, which is more to keep straight.

findings.recommendation: A. Canon already has every piece of machinery the texts need.
findings.verify_evidence: Corrant:5 and :281; Necrocursica:13, :161, :169, :173, :213, :457, :505; Concord Military.md:63; Tiered Path.md:23-31; Heresiology:196; Bench of Attribution.md:25. The auditor's list omits Necrocursica:213, :457 and :505; those Level references belong in the same sweep.

findings.topic: Tempus, the "gas giant" in the sky
findings.doc_claim: Vol II docx:213: "Tempus — our great gas-giant, that patient eye in the night sky". Vol II docx:243: it "hung in the daylight sky ... a grey suggestion of an eye". Vol III docx:310: "Tempus will return to its correct position over the next quarter-year". The inscription on the meta page: "That which burneth in Tempus burneth also in the Soul Crystal" (wiki/Lore & History/Lore & History.md:42).
findings.canon: The canon sky: "One sun. One moon. Five wanderers. A fixed field with one star that does not move." (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Sky, the Hour and the Year.md:17). The wanderers include the Weight, with a circuit of about 29 years, used for "Generational reckoning" (:29), and the Lantern, about 12 years (:30). There is no Tempus and nothing like a giant visible by day. Tempus exists in canon only as the Heresiology case "V · The Drift of Tempus" (Heresiology:212), which does not describe the body. Canon already has one sky-drift quarrel: the Sower's rising "has slipped eleven days" (Sky:129), a drift explained by calendar arithmetic (:128). The Measurewrights hold the Bench's instrument chair (Bench of Attribution.md:35).
findings.why_it_matters: A daylight gas-giant "eye" contradicts the canon sky, and the Tempus drift carries the Codex's whole argument about correspondence.
findings.question: What is Tempus in the canon sky?

options.label: A. The Hermetic name for the Weight (Omomi), the 29-year wanderer people count generations by
options.consequence: Fits "five wanderers". Tempus (time) matches the Weight's canon job, and a drift in the generation-clock is a public shock. Drop the daylight-eye image. Heresiology case V keeps its name.

options.label: B. The Hermetic name for the Lantern (Akari), the 12-year wanderer
options.consequence: Same edits as A, and closer to a real great gas giant. It loses the link between time and generations.

options.label: C. A sixth body, a gas giant visible by day
options.consequence: Keeps the image. Line 17 of the Sky page and every sky scene would need rewriting.

options.label: D. Replace it with the Sower's drift
options.consequence: Ties into an existing canon quarrel, but contradicts the arithmetic cause canon gives for that drift.

findings.recommendation: A. It fits the canon sky, and the name already means what the Weight is used for. Have the Measurewrights verify the drift instead of a free-standing observation post.
findings.verify_evidence: Vol II docx:213 ('our great gas-giant, that patient eye in the night sky') and :243; Vol III docx:310; Lore & History.md:42; Sky, the Hour and the Year.md:17, :29, :30, :128, :129; Heresiology:212; Bench of Attribution.md:35.

findings.topic: God-Essence
findings.doc_claim: Vol I:47: "The God-Essence that ran through Heraldic structures like blood through limestone veins flows also within stone, within root, within breath." Vol I:122: Asclepius thought it "an embarrassing relic of pre-Accord theology". Vol I:157: "the structural law of God-Essence correspondence".
findings.canon: Canon has no God-Essence doctrine. The only use is lower-case "residual god-essence leakage" at the Sirel ruins (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Beatrix Vaelthorn · The Root-Sworn.md:112). Canon's cosmology starts from Omnara: "To call Omnara a god would be to diminish it" (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/Omnara and the Division.md:25). The nearest canon faith is the Current, practised by people "who live near Wellsprings" and who hold that "the currents were here first" (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Faiths of the Four Quarters.md:60-61).
findings.why_it_matters: Vol I's appendix states God-Essence as structural law. If that is fact, it is new metaphysics sitting above the Wellsprings.
findings.question: Is God-Essence a real force in the world, or the Heralds' religious word for something canon already names?

options.label: A. A belief-word only
options.consequence: It is the Heralds' name for Wellspring Essence treated as divine, and Asclepius and the modern Accord find it quaint. No new metaphysics. Vol I:157 becomes the Heralds' reading, not fact.

options.label: B. Map it to a canon term (Omnara's residue, or Titanic Law)
options.consequence: Gives the Hermetic doctrine a cosmological root. Isaac has to choose which term, and it must be checked against the Epoch register.

options.label: C. A real, measurable substance, as at Sirel
options.consequence: New metaphysics. The Standing Index and Fracture of Worlds would need an entry.

findings.recommendation: A. It keeps the texts' religious flavour without adding a force to the magic system, and it sits naturally beside the Current.
findings.verify_evidence: Volume the First.md:47, :122, :133, :157; grep finds 'god-essence' only at Beatrix Vaelthorn.md:112 (and :135 context) outside the Codex; Omnara and the Division.md:25; Faiths of the Four Quarters.md:60-61.

findings.topic: "The Eressean era"
findings.doc_claim: Vol III docx:122 (and wiki Volume the Third.md:72): the Wellspring is "pre-dating the current Accord, possibly pre-dating the Eressean era".
findings.canon: Canon has no "Eressean era". The nearest match is the High Empire of Eresse, dated "First Eon, Great Spirit War Era" (High Empire of Eresse.md:14). The Great Spirit War itself has no place on the count; the derived file imports/lore/WORLD.md:41 flags this. Canon also has "Four Eons of Eressean law" (wiki/Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/The Powers of the Imperial Age.md:91). Otherwise "Eressean" refers to the New World elves (Sky:139).
findings.why_it_matters: It dates the Genesio Wellspring. The elvish reference was chosen for an elf narrator.
findings.question: What should "the Eressean era" point to?

options.label: A. The High Empire of Eresse (First Eon)
options.consequence: Gives real depth, but inherits the High Empire's unplaced "Great Spirit War Era" dating.

options.label: B. Use the count's own terms (e.g. "possibly older than the Antediluvian Calendar")
options.consequence: Dated, sealed ages with no open conflict. Fits a human narrator.

options.label: C. Cut the clause
options.consequence: Loses a line that shows the Wellspring's age.

findings.recommendation: B. The Concordance's ages are sealed and dated, and the Eresse anchor carries an open dating problem.
findings.verify_evidence: Vol III docx:122 (a long line that holds both the Thom passage and 'possibly pre-dating the Eressean era'); Volume the Third.md:72; High Empire of Eresse.md:14; imports/lore/WORLD.md:41; Powers of the Imperial Age.md:91; Sky:139; Concordance ('the collapse that closed the Antediluvian Calendar').

findings.topic: Cosmology terms that already fit canon (Archons, the Continuum, Paru's First Speech, the Veil)
findings.doc_claim: Vol I:133: "in ways the Archons do not miss". Vol II docx:31: "Scholars of the Archonic tradition". Necrocursica:81: "encoded into the Continuum since Paru's First Speech". Vol I:72: "The manipulation of the Veil between living and residual Essence."
findings.canon: The Archons are canon (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Fourteen Archons.md:17-21). "The Continuum" is used throughout Fracture of Worlds (e.g. wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VIII. Traits, Soul Crystal Tiers, Domains (Parts Twenty–Twenty-Two).md:19). "Paru's First Speech" is canon wording, used only at Alchemetrica.md:23. The Veil is canon, "the state of being between planes" (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:13), with Mortalis among its operation Wellsprings (:29).
findings.why_it_matters: These carry over unchanged. One nuance: canon's Veil is a threshold between planes, not specifically a line between living and dead. Vol I:72 and :86 ("Veil-adjacent dead") read as a practitioner's loose usage and pass.
findings.verify_evidence: Fourteen Archons.md:17-21; FoW VIII (Parts Twenty–Twenty-Two).md:19; Alchemetrica.md:23 (the only 'First Speech' outside the texts); The Veil.md:13 and :29; Necrocursica:81; Vol II docx:31; Volume the First.md:72, :86, :133.

findings.topic: Mu-jin's canon geography, and his unsettled origin
findings.doc_claim: The new attribution makes Mu-jin the Codex's narrator, but the texts' route (terraces, Genesio, Urbis, Castlefall, the Monastery) was written for Vis.
findings.canon: Mu-jin was "born into the Mahuo court line, scholar-nobility of the house at Sum-gol" (Kwon Mu-jin.md:162). Sum-gol is Ketsuen's Mahuo province in the Inner World (Ketsuen:20, :68). But his card header says "Eastern Concord-adjacent enclave" (Kwon Mu-jin.md:25), and "Eastern Concord" appears nowhere else. Hon-guk is the Soul Kingdom and has no place on the map (wiki/The Table — Running Pieces/State of Play — Kwon Mu-jin Hon-guk.md:14). No page locates the Aetherion Academy (State of Play — Kwon Mu-jin Aetherion Academy.md:13-14). The Zettari war camp is unplaced, but his arc touches Rimward in Nalūn (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Ara Min Mahuo.md:177) and the Ashgate road (Kwon Mu-jin.md:184). Canon relates none of these to any Trans-Alftian place. Three card conflicts sit open in the character-lore notes but not in CONFLICTS.md: Eastern Concord versus Sum-gol in Ketsuen; Sum-gol being emptied versus Mu-jin keeping a school there; and his age, 24 versus "forty years" (imports/lore/clusters/c09.md:254-256).
findings.why_it_matters: Vol I has to become Mu-jin's youth, so his home and whether it still stands must be settled before anyone rewrites it.
findings.question: Where is Mu-jin from, and does Sum-gol still stand in the years he writes the Codex?

options.label: A. Sum-gol in Ketsuen, still standing; strike "Eastern Concord-adjacent" from the card
options.consequence: Matches his Lore section, the Ketsuen page and his school at Sum-gol. Vol I becomes a Sum-gol court youth.

options.label: B. Sum-gol in Ketsuen, but emptied before the Codex
options.consequence: Vol I becomes a memoir of a lost home. His school scenes must come before the emptying.

options.label: C. A new Eastern Concord enclave with Sum-gol as its seat
options.consequence: Sum-gol has to move off the Ketsuen page, and a new region is added.

findings.recommendation: A. Three canon sources agree on it, and it works with ws-05 A.
findings.correction: The status should be conflict, not ambiguous. Canon disagrees with itself about when Sum-gol ended. The Primate's card says 'He was nine when Sum-gol finished emptying', and he is 58 with Sum-gol 'forty-nine years open', which puts the emptying about 49 years ago, before Mu-jin (24) was born. Ara 'was nine when Sum-gol went', which puts it about 12 years ago. Mu-jin keeps a school there in a later scene. So the recommendation's premise that 'three canon sources agree' Sum-gol still stands is false. Option A contradicts the Primate's card, and Vol I cannot be written as a youth in a living Sum-gol court without overturning it. Revised recommendation: B, with Sum-gol emptied and the Mahuo 'house at Sum-gol' surviving as a lineage and seat-name, which fits Kwon Mu-jin.md:162 and Ara:158. That makes Vol I a memoir of a lost home, with the terrace and valley scenes set before the emptying. The Sum-gol dating conflict (Primate, Ara and the school scene) and the 'Eastern Concord' header should get rows in CONFLICTS.md; neither is logged there now.
findings.verify_evidence: Aurelian Prudentius Custos Clausorum · The Primate.md:23, :30, :161, :245; Kwon Mu-jin.md:25, :26, :162, :185; Ara Min Mahuo.md:158; imports/lore/clusters/c09.md:254-256; CONFLICTS.md (no Sum-gol or Eastern Concord row); Continuity map.md:84 ('Darius in the ash at Sum-gol').

findings.topic: Malphas's geography, and when in his life he writes the Necrocursica
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:5: "Authored under compulsion ... during his confinement at the Genesio Monastery". Necrocursica:37: two men "arrived at my apartment in Genesio".
findings.canon: Malphas was born in flax country (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Malphas · Ferment of Stars.md:119). He trained at the Pyraeon Forge Academy and was expelled (:125-127). The Academy has no location and is otherwise unattested (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Zeraphine Drowl · The Black Vat Regent.md:17). After the expulsion he "answered to no school and no house" (Malphas:128). Greyshaft Nine is "a disused coldhouse on a main capped four years" (The Mother.md:58), and the Night Watch walks "the northern timber" (Night Watch.md:31). He has been a lich since the Becoming (Malphas:136). Canon already links him to Genesio: the Heresiology "describes him without naming him", and its tell is "crowned with achievements" (Malphas:142). That tell is the lesson of case IV, the Genesio Activation Sequence (Heresiology:211). Canon places neither Pyraeon nor Greyshaft relative to any Alftian place.
findings.why_it_matters: The Necrocursica's preface has others compelling him in Genesio. Being compelled by another person clashes with his card, and the date must fit his path through Invocation and the Becoming.
findings.question: Where, and at what point in Malphas's life, was the Necrocursica written?

options.label: A. Between the expulsion and Invocation, alive, compelled by Gillus in Genesio
options.consequence: The preface stays as written. It clashes with the card's "answered to no school and no house".

options.label: B. After Invocation and before the Becoming, alive, written in Genesio; the "compulsion" is whatever answered him at Invocation
options.consequence: Fits the card ("the thing he had handed that answer to had signed nothing"). Genesio lands on Malphas's road, and the Heresiology's Genesio tell becomes literal. The preface's compulsion by Gillus must be rewritten.

options.label: C. After the Becoming, as a lich at Greyshaft Nine
options.consequence: A dead man's treatise on the dead. The Genesio lines move to Greyshaft, and it must fit the Withering-era present.

findings.recommendation: B. It is the only option that keeps the compulsion without contradicting the card, and canon already hangs the Genesio case on him.
findings.correction: The auditor missed the decisive canon line. Heresiology case II, 'The Compelled Author and the Necromantic Manuscript', already says the Necrocursica's author was 'pulled by access and manipulated through need'. That is compulsion by others, which option A keeps and option B rewrites away. The claimed clash between A and the card is weak. Malphas:128 says he 'answered to no school and no house', and a coercing individual (Gillus) is neither. The Genesio tie is also overstated. 'Crowned with achievements' is the lesson of case IV, the Genesio activations, which is Thom's work, not the author's. Malphas's card links him to the Fermentation Perverted type (:45-47), not to being in Genesio. Add one geography fact: before the Becoming his threat rating was 'Tier-C across Outer World jurisdictions' (Malphas:108), so his living career ran in the Outer World. If ws-05 A puts Genesio in the Inner World, a Genesio confinement pulls him off that ground. Revised recommendation: A, alive and after the expulsion, coerced through need or access by Gillus. It matches Heresiology case II word for word, and Isaac should confirm the Outer-to-Inner World move.
findings.verify_evidence: Heresiology of Alchemy.md:209 (case II), :211 (case IV), :111-121 (Fermentation Perverted); Malphas · Ferment of Stars.md:21-24, :45-47, :108, :119, :125-128, :132, :136, :142; The Mother.md:43, :58; Zeraphine Drowl.md:17; Necrocursica:5, :37.

findings.topic: Internal chronology (six years against twelve, and the Necrocursica citing later works)
findings.doc_claim: Gillus waited "six years" (Vol III docx:66; Corrant:255), and Thom learned the method from that commission (Vol III docx:122). Yet Thom's submission sat "in the Genesio Archivum for twelve years" (Vol III docx:150; Corrant:101), it "postdates [the Necrocursica] by approximately twelve years" (Corrant:75), and Thom "spent twelve years activating" (Vol III docx:298). Corrant holds "the final two volumes" (Corrant:23) but cross-references "Vol. I and Vol. II" (Corrant:6). The Necrocursica, which comes before the Codex's events (Vol I:86), cites Volumes I–III and the Corrant Papers (Necrocursica:93, :109, :173, :465-477).
findings.canon: Canon is silent. It gives no dates for any of these events. The texts' span must now fit Mu-jin's known window, age 24 at the camp (Kwon Mu-jin.md:26) to 38 at the Academy (State of Play — Kwon Mu-jin Aetherion Academy.md:13).
findings.why_it_matters: The relative dates cannot all be true. Thom cannot have deposited, twelve years ago, a method he learned six years ago. The span also has to fit about 14 years of Mu-jin's life.
findings.question: Which single timeline do the five texts share?

options.label: A. Anchor on the commission as Year 0
options.consequence: Necrocursica first edition about Year −1, Thom's activations Years 1–6 with his submission about Year 4, Vol III at Year 6. Every "twelve years" becomes about five. The supplied Necrocursica becomes a revised later edition, stated on its title page. Everything fits inside Mu-jin's 24 to 38 window.

options.label: B. Anchor on the twelve years
options.consequence: The commission moves to about Year −12 and Gillus waits twelve years. The Codex spans about 13 years and fills Mu-jin's whole window up to the Academy.

options.label: C. Cut every number that isn't needed
options.consequence: The least bookkeeping, at the cost of vaguer texts.

findings.recommendation: A. It keeps the six-year letter, which the Codex is built around, and leaves room for Mu-jin's other canon years. "Final two volumes" at Corrant:23 should be "first two volumes" whichever option is chosen.
findings.verify_evidence: Vol III docx:66, :122, :150, :298; Corrant:6, :23, :75, :101, :255; Necrocursica:93, :109, :173, :465, :477 ('Vis sent me the third volume'); Volume the First.md:86; Kwon Mu-jin.md:26; State of Play — Kwon Mu-jin Aetherion Academy.md:13.

missed.topic: The Heresiology already records the texts' events as past 'Historical Cases', which constrains era and timeline
missed.detail: Heresiology cases I–V are the Codex's own events. I is the king (Vol I:130). II is the compelled author of the Necrocursica. III is the eastern commission for the dead wife (Vol II docx:27). IV is the Genesio activations. V is the Tempus drift. Canon presents them as history used for teaching. Whatever era Isaac picks in ws-01, the Heresiology must be written after all five events, and the Heresiology is undated. If the texts move to the present (ws-01 A) and Mu-jin is 24 now, the events must fall before the Heresiology was issued. That squeezes ws-20's span or makes the Heresiology a very recent document.
missed.evidence: wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:206-212 ('Historical Cases for Instruction'), :209 'pulled by access and manipulated through need', :210 'A dead woman's likeness was reconstructed'; header :13 (no date).
missed.question: Is the Heresiology written after all five documents, so that the events come before it, or should its cases be read as warnings that anticipate them? Option A: after. The Heresiology dates to the present and the texts' events end before it; consequence: ws-20's span must close before the Heresiology's issue. Option B: the cases describe earlier, similar incidents, not these ones; consequence: the five cases need rewording so they no longer match the texts one to one. Recommendation: A. The cases match the texts too closely to be read as coincidence.

missed.topic: Canon says the Alftian codices cite no Age
missed.detail: The Errata names 'the Alftian codices' among the principal registers the Guild examined and finds 'not one of them cites an Age'. The texts' 'Era of Voyagers' stamps contradict this directly, and the stamps are the only place any of them names an era. Dropping the stamps would agree with canon exactly and needs no ruling on which era. This is folded into the ws-01 correction as option D.

missed.topic: Sum-gol's end is a logged-nowhere canon conflict that the Codex conversion will hit
missed.detail: The Primate's card has Sum-gol finished emptying about 49 years ago. Ara's scene has it gone when she was nine, about 12 years ago. A Mu-jin scene still has him keeping a school there. The character-lore notes list these clashes, but CONFLICTS.md has no row, and Vol I cannot be rewritten as Mu-jin's youth until the date is fixed. Under the repo's standing rule this needs a CONFLICTS.md row and an agent ruling or Isaac's call.

seams.title: Kwon Mu-jin as Codex author
seams.summary: The attribution works, and the evidence for it is strong. Mu-jin's matured Anamnesis "reads inherited intention and unfinished formulae". His summoning is described as correspondence with "archived intention". At Rimward he asked without a Draft and "Something answered". Those three things are almost exactly the Codex's Volitional Trace and its Correction. The problems are about who he is and when things happened, not about ideas. The Codex narrator is an Elfin farmer's son who walks away from other people's mistakes, gives himself titles, and ranks below a Stage VII. Mu-jin is a human court prodigy who never lets an error stand and never uses a title, and he is Stage XII by 24. The timeline is the key open question. His age at the Ashgate road is itself contested in canon (24 on the card, 38 in the ruling's wording, "eleven years" of school and "forty years" in scene 10), and no CONFLICTS.md row records this. Under the working reading of 24 at the Ashgate road and 38 at the Academy, the Codex's 12 to 16 years only fit if it is split: Volumes I–II in the road years, Volume III after the Ashgate road. The wiki calls the author "a dead man" in one line and implies a finished life in five others. The Heresiology page itself never names him, so it survives unchanged.

findings.topic: Every claim the narrator makes about himself, checked against canon
findings.doc_claim: Across Vols I–III the narrator claims he is Elfin, a terrace-farmer's son, one of four friends facing a nameless illness, and a Mausoleum visitor. He studied at the Herald's Medical University and had his degrees revoked. He lodged in Castlefall 'above the tanner's workshop' (Vol II docx:19). He had Jabir's amulet, the Monastery and its Prior, Tat, Asclepius and the king's hall. He 'mapped [Tempus] for three years from my Alftian terrace' (Vol II docx:213). He spent eleven months in Urbis, six years of silence, and received a 260-year Trace. He calls himself 'Sage of the Anamnetic Line' (Vol III docx:5).
findings.canon: CONFLICTS with canon: (1) Elfin, against 'Human — Mahuo court line' at wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:25 (see km-02). (2) Farmer's son, against card:162 and Ketsuen:58 (see km-03). (3) Junior to a Stage VII, against Stage XII at card:40 (see km-07). (4) Walks away from errors, against card:117 (see km-11). (5) Self-given titles, against card:137 (see km-14). (6) 'Final Testimonies' and 'life's work' written about a living man (see km-16). FITS AS WRITTEN: teaching the Monastery's higher classes (Vol II docx:67), since he is 'The Teacher' (card:14). Medical training suits a diagnostician (card:48; Diagnosis 585 at card:57). The king's hall matches Heresiology Case I, which names nobody (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:208). Monasteries teaching the Great Work is canon (Heresiology:218). CANON SAYS NOTHING, and each fits once dated: the three friends and the illness (a hook at scenes/WOTR_Vaeloris_Sequence.md:1808, 'three of them are dead'); the Mausoleum; the Prior; the university and the revoked degrees (a mirror of the title-writ, card:32); the Castlefall rooms (these clash only if dated inside the Sum-gol school years, scenes/10_mujin_the_name_of_your_killer.md:95); the Tempus-watching; the eleven months; the six years; Jabir's amulet. The amulet does not contest the lens as 'the one thing he took from court' (card:126), but it is missing from his equipment list (card:126-127). Tat and Asclepius are covered in km-10. UNCLEAR: the Trace (km-06).
findings.why_it_matters: This is the index for the questionnaire. Six claims break canon outright. Most of the rest are neither right nor wrong until Isaac dates the Codex.
findings.recommendation: Settle km-04 (his age) and km-05 (the dating) first. Most of the claims canon says nothing about sort themselves out once each volume has a date.
findings.correction: The index is sound, but fix three things. (1) The flaw line is card:118, not :117; :117 is the table rule. Colophon: 'Elfin practitioner of the Hermetic and Anamnetic traditions' (Vol III docx:402; wiki Volume the Third.md:233). Letter note signed '— V.T.' (Vol II docx:203).

findings.topic: Origin: farmer's son of the Alftian lowlands, or Mahuo court child of Sum-gol
findings.doc_claim: 'I — a creature of the Alftian lowlands, son of terrace-farmers… The Trans-Alftian region is not a place that produces men of esoteric learning' (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:20). The same claim is repeated at Lore & History.md:23 and meta:25.
findings.canon: He was born into the Mahuo court line at Sum-gol and trained in alchemy at court under Doryun until 14 (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:162-164). Canon recognises Mahuo Wellspring knowledge as expertise (wiki/The Inner World — The Northern Shield/The Sovereign Enclave of Ketsuen — The Crow's Reach.md:58), and Sum-gol contributes 'river-valley agriculture' (:68). He 'grew up eleven miles from a mountain… how cold takes a hand' (card:162). The Sum-gol teaching house has a terrace above pines (scenes/wotr_the_warrior_nurse.md:13). 'Alftian' appears elsewhere in canon only as 'the Alftian codices' (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/Errata to the Received Registers.md:39).
findings.why_it_matters: Chapter the First is built on a humble outsider being ambushed by learning. Mu-jin is the opposite: a prodigy the court made into a symbol. The opening sets the whole memoir's self-image.
findings.question: The Codex opens on a farm boy who was 'never meant' for learning. Mu-jin was a court prodigy from a house known for its learning. What should Chapter the First become?

options.label: A. Sum-gol boyhood
options.consequence: The terraces, the frost and three years of watching the sky become his boyhood on the house terrace (about ages 11–14). The friends arrive after he leaves court. All the imagery survives, backed by canon. The joke about 'no men of learning' goes. 'Alftian' becomes the country he travels to, and the title stays.

options.label: B. Deliberate reticence
options.consequence: He writes as if he were nobody and leaves out his court birth because of the Ledger-Prince wound (card:152), which fits 'unreliable by construction' (Lore & History.md:32). He still cannot state a false parentage, so 'son of terrace-farmers' goes anyway.

options.label: C. Open on the Catalyst
options.consequence: Chapter the First becomes the corrected Fixation array at fourteen and the day of the title-writ (card:28-32). This is the tightest fit with the card. The terrace chapter and its tone are lost, and the Codex becomes a story of escaping court.

findings.recommendation: A, with a light touch of B's reticence. Canon already gives Sum-gol the frost, the mountain and a terrace, so the chapter's imagery survives without the false parentage.
findings.correction: The terrace cite is wrong. 'pines below the terrace' is at scenes/wotr_the_warrior_nurse.md:11, not :13, and :3 places the scene at 'The teaching house at Sum-gol'. That is the school he ran as an adult (nine students), not proven to be his boyhood home, and the court where he trained under Doryun is never placed on that terrace. Option A's 'boyhood on the house terrace' therefore invents canon. It should instead use what canon does give: the mountain and the frost (card:162) and Sum-gol's 'river-valley agriculture' (Ketsuen:68). Or it should move the terrace images to his adult teaching house. The question stays Isaac's, and the recommendation (A with a touch of B) stands.

findings.topic: Mu-jin's age on the Ashgate road, contested inside canon
findings.doc_claim: The Codex covers roughly 12–16 years of the narrator's life. It includes three years of sky-watching (Vol II docx:213), a six-year silence (Vol III docx:66) and 'eleven months' of writing (Vol III docx:16).
findings.canon: The card gives 'Age 24' and 'the ten years since' (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:26, :32). The ruling reads 'Kwon Mu-jin is 38, not 24' and says the ten years 'becomes twenty-four years' (RULINGS.md:518). The Academy State of Play gives 'roughly thirteen years later (… Mu-jin 38)' (wiki/The Table — Running Pieces/State of Play — Kwon Mu-jin Aetherion Academy.md:13). The Night Watch book bible reads 24 as the Hon-guk era and 38 as the Academy (book/night-watch-zombification/bible.md:151). Scenes give 'twenty-four years old' (scenes/wotr_the_warrior_nurse.md:17) and 'Kwon Mu-jin, 24' (scenes/WOTR_Vaeloris_Sequence.md:39). Against that: 'run a school for eleven years' (scenes/10_mujin_the_name_of_your_killer.md:95), 'forty years being unable to name' (:73), and 'forty years in the discipline' (scenes/mujins_interjection_aetherion_arena.md:13). Geturo is 15 when Mu-jin is 38 (RULINGS.md:518), so Geturo was born when Mu-jin was about 23. That is before the kiss Frithia steals and admits to a sleeping Mu-jin (wotr_the_warrior_nurse.md:75). No row in CONFLICTS.md records any of this.
findings.why_it_matters: The Codex's placement depends on this. The first reading gives about 10 years between 14 and the Ashgate road. The literal ruling gives 24 years. The repo rule says this conflict should be recorded in CONFLICTS.md before anything relies on it.
findings.question: How old is Mu-jin on the Ashgate road (the date on his card)?

options.label: A. 24 on the Ashgate road, 38 at the Academy
options.consequence: This is the reading four later sources assume. Scene 10's 'eleven years' and 'forty years', the elderly Mu-jin in the Arena interjection, and the children's birth years all need repair. The Codex gets only about 10 years before the Ashgate road.

options.label: B. 38 on the Ashgate road, as the ruling's words read
options.consequence: The whole Codex fits comfortably between 14 and 38, and scene 10's figures roughly hold. The '24' in the Vaeloris and Warrior Nurse scenes has to change, along with Ara's 21 and Frithia's relative age. The Academy moves to about 51.

options.label: C. 24 on the road, 38 at the Academy, plus a later elder era
options.consequence: The interjection's white-haired forty-year veteran becomes a third era in his 50s. All sources are kept, at the cost of one more era to track.

findings.recommendation: A. It matches the card, both 24-year-old scenes, the Academy State of Play and the book bible. Record the conflict in CONFLICTS.md first so the Codex has a fixed base.
findings.correction: All the citations check out, and no CONFLICTS.md row exists. The framing understates the ruling, though. RULINGS.md:518 is Isaac's own ruling, and it amends the card itself, whose As Of is 'before the Ashgate road': 'the ten years since phrasing becomes twenty-four years'. Option B is therefore the literal text of his 2026-09-18 ruling. Option A is how later pages (the Academy State of Play, bible.md:151) reinterpret it. Choosing A means Isaac overturns or narrows his own ruling, recorded as a new ruling, and the question should say so plainly. Two further points. The Hiromi card still says Geturo and Hiromi are twins and Lily is older, which the same ruling struck; see missed. Also, 24 + 'roughly thirteen years' gives 37, not 38. The recommendation can stay A because of the four sources behind it, but it must be labelled as an overturn of the ruling's wording, not as 'matching the card'.

findings.topic: When the Codex's events happen and when each volume is written
findings.doc_claim: Vol I is a retrospective ('I have since come to believe', Volume the First.md:33). Vol II is a working journal ('the small journal I keep in my coat', Vol II docx:75). Vol III is 'Final Testimonies… written in his own hand' (Vol III docx:5) after 'eleven months' in Urbis (docx:16).
findings.canon: Canon milestones: catalyst at 14 and left the court at Glory, Stage VI (card:28, :147). On the road with Ara, copying a book at 15, facing a Legion working 'with a piece of chalk and a book' at 22 (card:176; scenes/wotr_the_warrior_nurse.md:67). Dallae finished at 19, which is originated and pending ruling (scenes/xanelor_dallae.md:134). At 24: 'had not slept properly in something like six years' (warrior_nurse.md:17), then Rimward, the orchard and the Ashgate road (card:178-184). After the Ashgate road he has one lung and a polearm wound (card:184). The Hon-guk thread is thin (State of Play — Kwon Mu-jin Hon-guk.md:13-17). The Academy comes about 13 years later, with Frithia and three children (Academy State of Play:13). The Heresiology's cases I–V are the Codex's own events (Heresiology:208-212), and cards cite it as working doctrine (Silas Briarend Wytherm III · Gravebinder.md:89; Serai Linthra · The Serpent Alchemist.md:149).
findings.why_it_matters: Every canon-silent claim in km-01, the physical-state fixes in km-07 and the 'dead man' lines in km-16 all depend on this answer.
findings.question: Under km-04 option A (24 on the Ashgate road), when do the Codex's events take place and when does he write each volume?

options.label: A. All three volumes between 14 and 24
options.consequence: The Codex's years must be squeezed into about ten, overlapping his school years. Vols I–II can be 'the book' he held at 22. The six-year silence matches the six sleepless years. The Correction comes before Rimward, so Rimward becomes a test of the doctrine rather than its source.

options.label: B. Split: Vols I–II in the road years, Vol III after the Ashgate road
options.consequence: Vols I–II fall around ages 15–19. The six-year silence runs roughly 19–25, matching the six sleepless years. The eleven months in Urbis become his convalescence after the Ashgate road. Rimward's 'Something answered' becomes the question the Trace answers. The words 'Final' and 'life's work' must go. Vol III crosses the thin Hon-guk thread and has to account for Frithia and young children.

options.label: C. A late memoir after the Academy (38+)
options.consequence: This fits 'Final Testimonies' and the elderly interjection Mu-jin. Vol II's journal voice has to become recollection. The Heresiology, which draws on the Codex's events, would then postdate 38, which collides with the cards that already cite it as working doctrine.

findings.recommendation: B. It is the only placement that fits both the road years and the six sleepless years, gives the eleven months a cause, and makes the Correction answer Rimward.
findings.correction: There is no 'six-year silence' in the Codex. Vol III docx:66 says Gillus 'has been corresponding with you through your own text for six years without signing his name'. The letter itself sat unopened for 'four months' (docx:78), after 'three years carefully not looking for' the name. So Option B's '19–25 silence matches the six sleepless years' rests on a misreading and should be dropped. The real constraint is that the circulated manuscripts (Vols I–II) must precede Vol III by at least six years. That still suits B: Vols I–II in the road years, Vol III after the Ashgate road. Option C's claimed collision with the Silas and Serai cards is unproven, because neither card's As Of is dated against Mu-jin. The concrete constraint comes from the Malphas card instead (see missed). The Heresiology 'named him without naming him' before his Becoming, and Malphas is already teaching at the Academy as Salter when Mu-jin is 38. The Codex's Case IV events and the Heresiology therefore have to predate that, which works against C. Recommendation B stands.

findings.topic: The 260-year Trace aimed at 'your exact Aetheric signature', and the tomb bearing the narrator's name
findings.doc_claim: 'Its harmonic signature is Elfin in constitution' and 'The Trace has been waiting… for someone with your exact Aetheric signature' (Vol III docx:160, :168). A Mausoleum coffin is labelled 'Vis, Alchemical Astronomer' (Volume the First.md:42), which is the narrator's own name. (A Volitional Trace is the record of a decision someone died in the middle of making.)
findings.canon: Geuk-hon tells Mu-jin that 'nobody in four hundred years has taken enough away from you' (scenes/03_wren_three_deliveries.md:183). Kaalabad, chained since before living memory (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kaalabad.md:135-139), shouts 'GEUK-HON', and Mu-jin answers 'That is not my name.' (scenes/10_mujin_the_name_of_your_killer.md:123-125). 'He is Mu-jin's own prior soul' appears only in an author-facing, non-canon note (03_wren:228). His branch of the family lost the ability to host a soul population (wiki/The Disciplines/The Open Crucible — Kwon Mu-jin's Book of Summons.md:20), so Geuk-hon is not a soul living inside him. The Hon-guk thread is set in the 'Soul Kingdom… after meeting Geuk-hon' (State of Play Hon-guk:14). The Mahuo have taught the same law 'for six hundred years' (Vaeloris:1864). Dallae is a pattern 'half-written… by two hands', which is pending ruling (xanelor_dallae.md:134).
findings.why_it_matters: In the original, the Elfin Trace matched an Elfin narrator. With a human Mahuo narrator, 'exact signature' needs a reason, and the name on the coffin now points at nobody.
findings.question: Now that the narrator is a human Mahuo, whose unfinished decision is the Trace, and why is it aimed at him?

options.label: A. His own earlier life (the name Kaalabad uses)
options.consequence: The coffin and the Trace belong to the soul called Geuk-hon, which keeps 'Elfin' for that earlier life. This pays off the four hundred years, Kaalabad's naming and the Soul Kingdom, and gives Rimward a source. It commits canon to reincarnation and to what Geuk-hon is, which today rests only on an author note.

options.label: B. His house
options.consequence: A Mahuo ancestor (Dallae's 'one other' hand) aimed the Trace at the family signature. The Trace becomes Mahuo and the coffin names that ancestor. It uses his 'inherited intention' reading (card:48) directly and needs no reincarnation. It would also ratify Dallae and lose the link to Kaalabad.

options.label: C. Leave it unexplained
options.consequence: This adds the least new canon. 'Exact signature' reads as a hole for a human narrator, and the coffin name has to be dropped.

findings.recommendation: A. Three pieces of canon prose already point to an old soul under a name he refuses, and the original Codex was built around the narrator finding his own name in a tomb. Choose B if Isaac is not ready to fix Geuk-hon's nature.
findings.correction: (1) 'That is not my name.' is at scenes/10_mujin_the_name_of_your_killer.md:127, not :125. (2) Option A overstates its cost when it says it 'commits canon to reincarnation'. Canon already allows 'reincarnational echo' as one route for inheriting a Trait (FoW VIII:26; Trait System Law:62). What A actually commits is Geuk-hon's nature, which today rests only on the author note at 03_wren:228. (3) Option A has a number to reconcile: the Trace is 'two hundred and sixty years' old (Vol III docx:160), while Geuk-hon speaks of 'four hundred years' (03_wren:183). Either the soul's span covers more than one life or one figure moves. The question is still Isaac's, and the recommendation is still A, with B as the fallback.

findings.topic: His Stage, rank, body and lens at the date of each volume
findings.doc_claim: Gillus's Stage VII signature is something 'I have only read about in theoretical texts' (Vol III docx:50). Asked about Stage VII Anamnesis, he answers: 'Theoretically.' (docx:110). He holds the coffee 'in both hands' (docx:44). No lens appears anywhere in the Codex.
findings.canon: His Stage ladder: VI at 14, VII–XI while on the road, XII by the card's date (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:147, :40). Analysis 620 (card:57). Anamnesis 'matured' (card:48). Right eye lost at Rimward: 'The right side of the world was gone' (scenes/WOTR_Vaeloris_Sequence.md:1784). Right arm dead from the orchard (scenes/03_wren_three_deliveries.md:179). One lung and a white left eye after the Ashgate road (scenes/12_mujin_open_crucible.md:25, :163). Right hand working again at the Academy (scenes/xanelor_dallae.md:21). The lens rides his left eye (card:115) and comes off when he reads a working (card:96, :124).
findings.why_it_matters: At any date from 24 on, a Stage XII Archmagus with SS Gnosis cannot know Stage VII only 'theoretically'. The power gap between him and Gillus reverses.
findings.mechanical_fix: After km-05 sets the dates: (1) Give his Stage at each volume from the card:147 ladder. (2) If Vol III falls at 24 or later, cut the 'only read about in theoretical texts' clause (docx:50) and the reply 'Theoretically' (docx:110), and let him read Gillus's double signature at a glance. (3) Match his body to the date: one eye after Rimward; no right hand between the orchard and its return. 'Both hands' (docx:44) stands only if the arm has recovered. (4) Show the lens coming off when he reads the Genesio hollow (docx:204).
findings.correction: Only docx:110 is a Stage conflict: to 'How much do you know about Anamnesis attunement at Stage VII and above?' he answers 'Theoretically.' A matured-Anamnesis practitioner who is himself past VII cannot say that. Docx:50 is different. It says he has only read about one rare signature, 'a quiet, double-register harmonic… Mortalis primary… Anamnesis secondary', not about Stage VII in general, so it can stand at any Stage. Drop it from the mandatory cut. The body-by-date list also leaves out his breathing: after Rimward Ara says 'You cannot breathe past halfway'. Everything else stays mechanical once km-05 sets the dates.

findings.topic: Ara is missing from a memoir of years she spent at his side
findings.doc_claim: No sister appears in any volume. He meets the illness alone: 'He did not tell them he was doing so.' (Volume the First.md:35). Vol III is 'at the request of no one' (Vol III docx:5).
findings.canon: 'Ara travelled his circuit with him' (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:176). She is 'itinerant alongside her brother's teaching circuit' (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Ara Min Mahuo.md:24). She is a healer whose Mortalis treats 'an ending as a passage' (Ara:42, :104). About what answered him at Rimward, he told her: 'When I have something worth saying I will say it to you first.' (scenes/WOTR_Vaeloris_Sequence.md:1880).
findings.why_it_matters: If Vols I–II fall in the road years (km-05 A or B), leaving her out contradicts both cards. His promise to her also gives Vol III an obvious recipient.
findings.question: Where does Ara appear in the Codex?

options.label: A. The healer in the illness chapter
options.consequence: Her doctrine of ending as passage becomes the seed of the Monastery's 'Death is not the opposite of life'. She takes pages from the invented friends.

options.label: B. The person Vol III is written to
options.consequence: Vol III keeps his Rimward promise, replacing 'at the request of no one'. This is the strongest emotional frame, and a letter carries its writer's voice (R51-33, rules/doc-vocabulary-law-2026-09-26.yaml:839).

options.label: C. The hand in the Vol II margin
options.consequence: The note 'in handwriting that is not Vis Trismegistus's' (Vol III docx:10) becomes hers. This is small and elegant, but the aphorism must suit her plain voice (Ara:128). Geturo, who copied his father's margins for four years (scenes/geturo_ignite_tide.md:68), is an alternative if Vol III is late.

options.label: D. A deliberate omission he admits
options.consequence: This follows the Mahuo habit of quietly settling a person's life without asking them (card:163). It reads as a gap unless he says so on the page.

findings.recommendation: A and B together. C costs nothing extra if Isaac likes it.
