findings.topic: Mu-jin's friend Noxinus once the Necrocursica becomes Malphas's
findings.doc_claim: Noxinus set the primer on his table (Volume the First.md:24). Noxinus is 'older and considerably wiser than me' (:87). Noxinus brings him the manuscript: 'Tell me what I wrote.' (Vol II docx:91).
findings.canon: Malphas teaches at the Academy as 'Doctor Osric Salter' (book/night-watch-zombification/bible.md:33). 'Mu-jin and Salter share a building for eight chapters… does not decide whether Mu-jin ever reads Salter' (bible.md:153). In the Arena scene Mu-jin knows the archive methods but not the man; the note calls it dramatic irony (scenes/mujins_interjection_aetherion_arena.md:17, :64). Malphas is not among the ties on Mu-jin's card (card:187-205).
findings.why_it_matters: If the Necrocursica's author is Mu-jin's youthful friend, then Malphas's alias at the Academy becomes a question of whether an old friend recognises him. That affects the Night Watch book and the Malphas conversion.
findings.question: With Malphas writing the Necrocursica, what is Mu-jin's personal tie to its author?

options.label: A. Noxinus stays a separate friend who is not the author
options.consequence: Noxinus becomes the go-between who brings Mu-jin Malphas's text, and the friendship and the night scene survive. The Malphas seam must agree on how the text reached him.

options.label: B. Noxinus becomes Malphas
options.consequence: Mu-jin's oldest friend becomes the lich, which is a huge payoff. It forces the Night Watch book to settle whether Mu-jin recognises Salter (bible.md:153), rewrites Malphas's youth, and breaks the impersonal irony of the Arena scene.

options.label: C. No personal tie
options.consequence: Mu-jin reads Malphas's work as a text only, and the 'Tell me what I wrote' night goes to Paracelsus or is cut. The book plan and the Arena irony stay intact, but Vol II loses its most human scene.

findings.recommendation: A. It keeps Vol II's friendship and leaves the Academy plan untouched. Check it against the Malphas seam's ruling.

findings.topic: Which existing people stand behind the Codex's cast
findings.doc_claim: A 'narcissistic senior lecturer manufactured plagiarism evidence' and took a strike to the sternum (Volume the First.md:62). Tat 'had recently lost his cat and was somewhat undone by it' (:116). Jabir gave him an amulet that turned his Crystal 'toward a frequency it had always possessed' (:97). Asclepius 'did not convert. She listened' (:122). There is also a king (:130).
findings.canon: DORYUN: 'court mentor, estranged — heavy, unresolved' (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:105); 'patience without honesty' (:121); 'Doryun stayed patient' (:170); the Citation is built from his voice (wiki/The Disciplines/The Open Crucible — Kwon Mu-jin's Book of Summons.md:119). The court credited the child rather than stealing from him (card:30). DOYUN: the last of the nine (card:198); aged 15 when Mu-jin is 24; earnest, and quotes lessons back to him (scenes/WOTR_Vaeloris_Sequence.md:41, :1904-1922); marked 'canon-eligible pending approval' (:41). The other students died when the yard wall fell (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kaalabad.md:148). GEUK-HON: speaks in 'a room with a table… two cups', like 'a man describing something he had already watched happen once' (scenes/03_wren_three_deliveries.md:179), and was met after the orchard, when Mu-jin was 24. FRITHIA: a skeptic won over when he faced a Legion working 'with a piece of chalk and a book' (scenes/wotr_the_warrior_nurse.md:67); 36 when he was 24 (:31); from the ice country. KING: a royal court exists (card:30; Ara Min Mahuo.md:24), but nothing is said of the king himself. THE THREE FRIENDS: 'three of them are dead' (Vaeloris:1808).
findings.why_it_matters: Mapping the cast onto existing people is what makes the book read as Mu-jin's life. Each mapping also turns a canon silence into new canon.
findings.question: Which Codex figures should be existing people from Mu-jin's life?

options.label: A. Light: Tat becomes Doyun
options.consequence: This only fits if Tat's scenes fall when Mu-jin is 21 or older (Doyun 12 or older). Otherwise Tat is one of the eight students later killed, which gives 'None of the things that are, are truly destroyed' its weight. All other figures stay new.

options.label: B. A plus Doryun as the lecturer
options.consequence: The plagiarism is recut as quiet dishonesty: he signs his pupil's later work as his own, with no brawl. Doryun gets an on-page scene. It must be a separate act from the Catalyst, which the court credited to Mu-jin.

options.label: C. Full mapping
options.consequence: B plus the king becomes the monarch of the Ledger-Prince court, Jabir becomes Geuk-hon and Asclepius becomes Frithia. Canon says nothing about the king. The Jabir meeting must move to age 24 or later. Asclepius, a High Elf teacher, would need a heavy rewrite.

options.label: D. None
options.consequence: The Codex cast stays wholly new. This is the cleanest for canon and the weakest attribution.

findings.recommendation: B. Keep the king, Jabir and Asclepius as new people. Use Geuk-hon for the Trace instead (km-06). The three friends could optionally be the 'three of them are dead'.
findings.correction: Three fixes. (1) Kaalabad.md:148 says only that the teaching house's yard wall went down 'with people beneath it'. It does not say the students died. 'One of them was left, Doyun' (card:176) is the only canon on the other eight, so the wall is an inference. (2) The Codex's king is 'Elected to govern a city-state in the Urbis orbit' (Volume the First.md:130), which undercuts option C's mapping of him onto the Mahuo court monarch. (3) Tat is a Monastery 'partner' (:116), so Tat→Doyun also moves those scenes from the Monastery to the Sum-gol school. The recommendation (B) stands. Its Doryun recut still has to move the plagiarism from a university lecturer's office to the court.

findings.topic: The narrator's failing, Separation Perverted, against Mu-jin's defining flaw
findings.doc_claim: At the café he says: 'I left the building. I finished my meal outside on the step.' (Volume the First.md:74). Later: 'I was clear about what I saw. I had simply decided not to be responsible for it.' (Vol II docx:241).
findings.canon: His flaw: 'Cannot let an error sit uncorrected, even when correcting it costs him the room' (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:117). 'He never lets an error stand unspoken' (card:137). His loop repeats this (card:120). Turned on himself, though: 'I have decided that is a fault rather than a virtue, and I have not done anything about it' (scenes/WOTR_Vaeloris_Sequence.md:1898). He also refuses to discuss what answered him (:1876; card:178). The Heresiology lists Non-Commitment and Sanitized Truth ('I am only recording facts') as separate corruptions (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:271, :274).
findings.why_it_matters: The Codex's whole arc rests on the narrator's Third Corruption. Aimed at other people's errors, it contradicts the card for his entire adult life. Aimed at himself, canon already shows it.
findings.question: The narrator fails by walking away from other people's mistakes. Mu-jin never does that, but he does walk away from himself. Which failing is his?

options.label: A. Turn it inward
options.consequence: He confronts Paracelsus and Gillus plainly and still fails to stop them. The error he won't look at is his own: what answered him at Rimward, and the letter about his own signature. Vol III's 'understanding everything except itself' (docx:30) becomes literal. The corruption's order in the Codex is kept.

options.label: B. Change his corruption to Distillation Perverted (Sanitized Truth)
options.consequence: This is fresh and sharp, and it matches his Distillatio Seal, whose cost falls on the person asking (card:99). It breaks the Codex's order, where Vol II names Separation as the Third from his own life.

options.label: C. Keep the outward failing as his younger self
options.consequence: This leans on 'Now he simply corrects them' (card:123). The card's flaw still covers every year from 14 on, so the conflict remains.

findings.recommendation: A. Canon's own Mu-jin already says this about himself.
findings.correction: The flaw is card:118, not :117. The Heresiology reading is also slightly off. Heresiology:271 does not list Non-Commitment as a separate corruption: it is the Separation inversion itself ('Innocence through distance', 'It is complicated'). That is exactly the Codex's Third Corruption, and it supports option A, which keeps Separation and turns it inward. Sanitized Truth (:274) is the Distillation inversion, which is option B's alternative. The question and the recommendation (A) stand.

findings.question: How much of the Codex's elegant, ironic narration survives as Mu-jin's written voice?

options.label: A. The titles belong to the frame, not to him

findings.topic: Echoes that make the attribution land
findings.doc_claim: The Correction: 'The Great Work is the practitioner learning to ask a question that the universe is already in the process of answering' (wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:75). Anamnesis keeps what souls 'were committed to' (Vol III docx:112).
findings.canon: His Anamnesis 'reads inherited intention and unfinished formulae' (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:48). His summoning is 'a trained correspondence with the Continuum's own archived intention' (wiki/The Disciplines/The Open Crucible — Kwon Mu-jin's Book of Summons.md:20), and he says 'A Draft-circle is not a door. It is a request form.' (:23). The corrupt version of him 'simply takes one' (:34), matching the house law 'A summoner cannot compel' (card:163). At Rimward: 'He asked without one… Something answered.' (card:178). Fixation Anchor Sense lets him feel seals 'the way most people feel a held breath' (card:82), which fits the sealed letter he leaves unopened for four months (Vol III docx:78). Dallae was an unfinished pattern he finished (scenes/xanelor_dallae.md:134, pending). 'Six years' without proper sleep (scenes/wotr_the_warrior_nurse.md:17). An unknown 'two syllables' spoken in his sleep (:57). 'Mu-jin's would not die with Mu-jin' (:67). He keeps his own record: 'not to be repeated' (scenes/11_mujin_second_law_held_open.md:107). His stress habit is to go 'very still' (card:124), matching 'I am very still.' (Vol III docx:166). The Second Corruption's 'the product bears their name' (Vol II docx:165) mirrors the title-writ scar (card:150-152). Copper appears in his workings (Open Crucible:173). The Heresiology's 'Academies' duty applies to him as a teacher (Heresiology:220).
findings.why_it_matters: These are the reasons the attribution feels inevitable rather than pasted on. The conversion should lean on them.
findings.recommendation: Use them in the conversion: Rimward as the question the Correction answers; the sealed letter felt through his seal sense; the unopened letter as the six sleepless years. The two-syllable name could be 'Gillus', but that is only available, not assumed.
findings.correction: The canon echoes all check out. The recommendation's 'the unopened letter as the six sleepless years' is wrong: the letter was unopened for four months (Vol III docx:78), and the six years are Gillus's unsigned correspondence through the text (docx:66). Recast it as: the four unopened months, felt through his seal sense (card:82), plus the 'three years carefully not looking for' the name. The copper echo is only a smell ('old copper on the air', Open Crucible:173) and is weak.

missed.topic: The Heresiology already names Malphas, which fixes both the dating and Mu-jin's diagnosis of the Necrocursica's author
missed.detail: The Malphas card says the Heresiology 'named him without naming him' and gives its tell as a corruption that 'arrives crowned with achievements'. That is Heresiology Case IV, the Genesio Activation Sequence, which is the Codex's Vol III events. Two consequences follow for a Mu-jin Codex. (1) Dating: the Codex's Case IV and the Heresiology must come before Malphas's Becoming, and Malphas is already at the Academy as Salter when Mu-jin is 38. This rules out a late memoir (km-05 C) and a posthumous Heresiology (km-16 B) more firmly than the Silas and Serai cards do. (2) Diagnosis: in Vol II, Mu-jin files the Necrocursica's author under Dissolution Perverted (the compelled author, capitulation), while Malphas's card files him under Fermentation Perverted. Once Malphas writes the Necrocursica, Mu-jin's own analysis in the Codex contradicts the Malphas card unless one of them changes.

A: keep Dissolution Perverted, the compelled author. This keeps the Codex and Heresiology Case II but contradicts the Malphas card. C: Dissolution for the Necrocursica itself, with Malphas's later Fermentation as a separate Case IV. This keeps both, but only if Malphas's Becoming comes after the Codex. seams.title: Malphas as Necrocursica author
seams.summary: Most of the Necrocursica's narrator fits Malphas, and some of it fits very well. The text has no verbal contractions, which matches his fingerprint (contraction rate 0.0). It is dry and darkly funny. Its compulsion story lines up almost exactly with his Invocation catalyst (Stage IX, the point where he stopped working alone): he wrote for people who stayed unnamed and "did not sign anything", and "relief" turned to worse within a year or two. Its warnings name his later life one by one: the Fifth Corruption (preferring the dead), the Sixth (naming as a weapon), the Third (a work that keeps growing under a seal), and the Bureau's cover word "bleed". The hard conflicts sit elsewhere: an institutional office against "unbound in life"; the Heralds Medical University against the Pyraeon Forge Academy; a Voyager-era date against his Withering-era present; a poet's confessional warmth against the scene's opaque, bill-of-lading voice; and a treatise with no category for a lich, written by a man who became one. The Heresiology's Case II (the Compelled Author, a case of Dissolution Perverted, the Corruption of Submission) fits him if Isaac lets one life hold two corruptions: Dissolution is his primary Wellspring. Most of the chain is canon silence, not conflict: Gillus De Raits, Paracelsus, the Genesio Monastery and the Trans-Alftian Accord appear only in the Codex texts. The repo-root "The Night's Watch.md" named in the brief no longer exists; the scene is scenes/the_nights_watch.md (book bible line 5 gives the equivalence). Two unlogged canon tensions surfaced for CONFLICTS.md. Malphas's card has "As Of" set at the coldhouse (line 18) while its stats are the lich's (line 62). R60-24 (RULINGS.md:2061) makes The Mother a following of the Becoming, but the Greyshaft Nine culture exists before the Becoming.

findings.topic: Ledger of every biographical claim about the author (merged index; open items route to later findings)
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:5 "Authored under compulsion by Noxinus Ren, Alchemist-Scribe of the Trans-Alftian Accord, during his confinement at the Genesio Monastery"; Necrocursica:37 "alchemist, sometime astronomer, unwilling expert"; Codex I (wiki):87 "He was older and considerably wiser than me".
findings.canon: Compulsion at Genesio by Gillus and a titled person (Necrocursica:5,37,45): Genesio Monastery is silent in canon, appearing only as "the Monastery" in the Codex (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:91). The compulsion fits the Invocation pattern at wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Malphas · Ferment of Stars.md:21-23 (see mn-02, mn-04). Left hand hurt by their persuasion (5): canon silent. His hands are notable in canon for keeping a living colour in the cold (scenes/the_nights_watch.md:183). Mu-jin carries left-wrist scars (scenes/mujins_interjection_aetherion_arena.md:7) (see mn-04). Alchemist-Scribe of the Trans-Alftian Accord: CONFLICT with card:20 "Unbound in life" and card:128 "He answered to no school and no house" (mn-07). Sometime astronomer: silent, and the epithet "Ferment of Stars" (card:19) supports it. Poet (Codex I wiki:86; Codex II docx:121,211; wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:43): silent, and the scene voice is anti-lyrical (mn-12). "Retired from morally proximate territory" (41,45): fits either his solitary post-expulsion years (card:128) or the nine-year gap in the book (book/night-watch-zombification/bible.md:86) (mn-02). Fourteen months (53): silent, and fits card:23 "within a year or two". Saw four Corruptions (53): silent. He carried Mortalis while alive (card:54 "no longer the decay half of him"), so it is plausible. Paracelsus's colleague at the Heralds Medical University (121,169): Paracelsus and the University exist only in the Codex (Volume the First.md:59, which puts the narrator and Paracelsus there). The card's Making names only Pyraeon (card:125) (mn-07). Admits Nomenclature in his own early writing (333): FITS his naming method (wiki/Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/The Mother.md:51; scenes/the_nights_watch.md:227) (mn-09). Saw the Seventh Corruption on a platform (365-373): silent for Malphas. The man matches Gillus De Raits on the Castlefall platform (Codex III docx:50,88) (mn-04). From the Codex: older (silent on Malphas's age); set the primer on the table (conflicts with Kwon Mu-jin.md:164, see mn-06); stayed in Castlefall (Codex II docx:211; wiki Volume the Second.md:166): silent.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the full inventory the questionnaire needs. Each claim is sorted as a fit, a conflict or canon silence, so no claim is dropped between findings.
findings.recommendation: Use this as the index. Every open item names the finding that carries its decision.
findings.correction: The ledger is useful, but three entries are wrong. (1) The Necrocursica never names the Heralds Medical University. Line 121 says only "Paracelsus Furveus, my colleague", and line 169 is the Category Two protocol, not a Paracelsus line. Codex I puts the narrator and Paracelsus at the University (wiki Volume the First.md:59), and the Vol I extract leaves Noxinus behind at Genesio (scratchpad vol1_vault.txt:27, "left Noxinus and Neros at Genesio"). So nothing here conflicts with Pyraeon for Malphas. (2) Genesio is not absent from canon: Heresiology:211 names "The Genesio Activation Sequence", and the meta page (Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:84) has the "Genesio Archivum". Only the exact phrase "Genesio Monastery" is absent. (3) The Seventh-Corruption man stands at "a Genesio waystation" (Necrocursica:365). Codex III's Gillus is on the Castlefall railway platform (Codex III docx:40,88). The match to Gillus is an inference and should be marked as one. The summary's line that he wrote for people who "did not sign anything" merges the card's catalyst wording (card:23) with the Necrocursica. The Necrocursica's compellers are two persons whose names he agreed to omit (37). The status stays ambiguous.

findings.topic: When Malphas wrote it: before Invocation, between Invocation and the Becoming, or as a lich
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:21 "I began writing this under protest... By the fifth I was writing sections they had not asked for." The title page (5) says the compellers "will remain, for now, unnamed".
findings.canon: Invocation (Stage IX, when a practitioner stops working alone and something answers): card:21-23 "what answered was not a Wellspring... the thing they handed responsibility to did not sign anything", and the relief comes first. Card:128 "Then he stopped working alone", so Invocation comes before Greyshaft Nine, where he runs a cell of four (card:134). Card:79 says his Conversion froze at Stage IX. The Becoming (his death into lichdom at Stage XIV) comes after the coldhouse (card:136), and the book bible has him alive at the coldhouse (book/night-watch-zombification/bible.md:32). Nine years later he teaches at the Aetherion Academy as Doctor Osric Salter (bible.md:13,86,167). That book is planner-originated and ungated (book/night-watch-zombification/GATES.md:5). Unlogged tensions: R60-24 (RULINGS.md:2061) makes The Mother "a religious following of the Becoming", while its Greyshaft culture predates the Becoming (RULINGS.md:2031); and card:18 sets "As Of" at the coldhouse while its stats are the lich's (card:62).
findings.why_it_matters: The date decides whether the warnings are sincere foreshadowing, cover for a man already running The Mother, or a lich lecturing on the dead. It also sets the tone of every other fix.
findings.question: At what point in his life did Malphas write the Necrocursica? Invocation is Stage IX, when he stopped working alone and something answered him. The Becoming is Stage XIV, when he died into a lich.

options.label: At Invocation, before The Mother
options.consequence: The compulsion is the day he stopped working alone. The fourteen months of writing past the brief are the recorded "relief", and the "worse" a year or two later is The Mother. The text stays close to how it reads now, and its warnings become tragic foreshadowing.

options.label: In the solitary years before Invocation
options.consequence: This keeps the "retired... you are avoiding" exchange, but the compulsion stops being his turning point and the catalyst match is lost. His Mortalis casework has to happen while he let no hand but his own near the bench.

options.label: In the nine years between Greyshaft Nine and the Aetherion Academy
options.consequence: This fits "You have not retired. You are avoiding" perfectly, but he writes every warning after Project Zombification, so the candour reads as cover. The book's nine-year gap has to hold a fourteen-month confinement at Genesio.

options.label: After the Becoming, as a Stage XIV lich
options.consequence: Nobody compels a Level 475 Archmaster, and a lich's hand wound "not yet fully healed" needs explaining. Its author refutes the text's thesis that the dead do not think. Not workable without a rewrite.

findings.recommendation: At Invocation for the core text. The match with the catalyst is almost word for word: output he was not solely responsible for, unnamed parties who did not sign, relief, then worse. The title page already allows a later layer ("Annotated against his will and then with growing enthusiasm by the same", line 9), so the lich's voice can live in the margins (see mn-09 and mn-11).
findings.correction: The question and the options stand. The claim that the Necrocursica matches the catalyst "almost word for word" does not. The card's Invocation answerer is not a person. card:24 says it "had been waiting the entire span between for him to run out of body", which makes it the power that took him at the Becoming. The Necrocursica's compellers are two humans: Gillus and a titled person (37). "Did not sign anything" is card wording and does not appear in the Necrocursica. The fit is thematic: relief, then something worse. Isaac should also be asked whether the compellers are the human face of what answered at Invocation (see mn-04). Citation fixes: the book being planner-originated comes from bible.md:165 ("Originated in this plan"). GATES.md:5 says only that chapter 1 waits on Isaac's gate decision. The repo-root equivalence is at bible.md:3, not line 5. Also note bible.md:32: in the book, no Stage is named or implied for the living man. Stage IX rests on the card alone. The recommendation (Invocation for the core text, with a later margin layer) remains reasonable.
findings.verify_evidence: card:21-24,79,128,134,136; Necrocursica:9,21,37; book/night-watch-zombification/bible.md:3,32,86,165,167; book/night-watch-zombification/GATES.md:5 ('blocked — chapter 1 is written and gated; Isaac has not decided')

findings.topic: Era: the Codex chain is dated to the Voyager Era, but Malphas lives in the Withering Era
findings.doc_claim: wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:14 "Transcribed from the Archivum of the Heralds, Urbis — Era of Voyagers". Necrocursica Appendix II (477) replies to Codex Vol III.
findings.canon: The Voyager Era runs 000 to 070 IC and the Withering Era 645 IC to the present (wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Concordance of Ages.md:130,159). Malphas's cell is in the archive's present, in the Withering Era (imports/lore/clusters/c35.md:5, from scenes/the_nights_watch.md). He is alive at Greyshaft Nine and nine years later (book/night-watch-zombification/bible.md:13,32). Canon gives no age that would span six centuries alive.
findings.why_it_matters: A living Malphas cannot write a Voyager-era text and then run a Withering-era cell while still alive. Mu-jin, the new Codex author, also lives in the present.
findings.mechanical_fix: Date both layers of the Necrocursica to the Withering Era, and drop any Voyager-era dating the Necrocursica relies on. The Codex seam must move the Codex's "Era of Voyagers" labels to match, because Appendix II answers Codex Vol III.
findings.correction: The Voyager Era is at Concordance:110 and 157 (000–070 IC). Lines 130 and 159 are the Withering Era. The Necrocursica itself has no era label: a grep for 'Era' finds nothing. So there is no Voyager dating in it to drop, and the mechanical fix is not a Necrocursica edit. The 'Era of Voyagers' labels sit in the Codex (Volume the First.md:14, Volume the Second.md:14, Volume the Third.md:235, meta page:14) and belong to the Codex seam. What the Necrocursica does need is a Withering-Era date that fits R60-09 (the Guild Accord is forming now), and that is a decision (see missed item). Keep this finding mechanical only as a cross-seam note: "Era of Voyagers" cannot stand once both authors are Withering-Era people.

findings.topic: Who compels him: Gillus De Raits and a titled person, or a canon candidate
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:37 "one of whom is named Gillus De Raits and the other of whom goes by a title I will not reproduce here". Line 5: the persuasion "left an impression on his left hand".
findings.canon: Gillus has no card and appears only in the Codex pages and wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md. Codex III (docx:50) makes him Stage VII with Mortalis primary; line 88 has him look at the mountains from the platform. That matches the Necrocursica's Seventh Corruption man (345, 365-369), so the compeller is the man the author saw on the platform. The Corrant Papers docx:255 has Gillus say "The Necrocursica was my project." Canon candidates: Sancta Lux Inquisitors, who may "pronounce sentence in the field" (wiki/The Magic System/The Gate Who May Learn Magic.md:61). Unlicensed high working is punished by "branding" and Crystal sealing (Gate:76; R60-17 live). Enforcement lists "the Inquisition" (R60-16 live). The Pyraeon Forge Academy declared him "a metaphysical threat" (card:20). Zeraphine Drowl was that Academy's tactician before she betrayed it for him (Zeraphine Drowl card:25,28). The Night Watch is a poor fit, because the book premise says it never gets the hand (bible.md:13,17).
findings.why_it_matters: The compeller decides whether the Necrocursica is a private coercion, a state sentence, or the Academy's doing. It also decides what the wound on his hand is.
findings.question: Who forces Malphas to write? The text names Gillus De Raits (a figure only in the Codex books) and an unnamed person with a title.

options.label: Keep Gillus and the unnamed titled person
options.consequence: The Codex and Corrant links stay intact, and Gillus stays the platform man of the Seventh Corruption. The title stays a blank, and the hand wound stays unexplained.

options.label: Gillus plus a Sancta Lux Inquisitor; the hand mark is a brand
options.consequence: This ties the text to live rules R60-16 and R60-17 and to the Gate page. The Necrocursica becomes a sentence served, a controlled text written for the Gate he later breaks. Sancta Lux enters his backstory.

options.label: Gillus plus an officer of the Pyraeon Forge Academy, possibly Zeraphine
options.consequence: The Academy gets its first face (imports/lore/clusters/c23.md:181 asks for one) and Zeraphine's later betrayal is planted. It fixes her timeline to this meeting.

options.label: Replace Gillus entirely with a canon figure
options.consequence: Codex II and III and the Corrant Papers lose the villain they share, which means a heavy rewrite across three documents.

findings.recommendation: Gillus plus a Sancta Lux Inquisitor. It keeps the Codex spine, turns "a title I will not reproduce" and the half-healed hand into live canon (branding under the Gate), and gives Malphas a reason to hate the Gate. It also avoids echoing Mu-jin's left-wrist scars, since a brand reads differently from scars on the wrist.
findings.correction: This is a real decision and the citations check out (Gate:61 Inquisitor, Gate:76 branding "in the Accord cities", R60-16 and R60-17 live, Corrant docx:255 signed "— G. De Raits" at ~271, Zeraphine card:17,25,28). One fix: the Necrocursica's platform man stands at "a Genesio waystation" (365), not Castlefall. The author also says "I did not approach him that day" (373), which reads oddly if this is the man who compelled him. Present the Gillus identification as a possible reading, not a fact. Add an option: the titled compeller fronts for, or is, what answered at Invocation (card:21-24). That ties the compulsion to his canon catalyst without importing Sancta Lux. The Sancta Lux recommendation is defensible, but it adds new canon to his backstory, and Isaac should see it that way.

findings.topic: What name is on the title page
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:69 "— N. Ren, Genesio" (also 5, 449, 489). Codex II docx:211 says his poetry was published in Trans-Alftian literary journals.
findings.canon: Malphas treats names as evidence: "a name is the only thing in this world that the Accord can actually prosecute" (scenes/the_nights_watch.md:223) and "I would prefer the file be built off a word I chose" (scenes/the_nights_watch.md:229; The Mother.md:51,86). The Heresiology "named him without naming him" (card:45). He takes an alias later, Doctor Osric Salter, which is planner-originated (bible.md:167). The card treats Malphas as his given name (card:19,119).
findings.why_it_matters: A sealed treatise signed "Malphas" hands the Register the one thing his method refuses to give it. The Codex and Corrant texts cite "Noxinus Ren" dozens of times.
findings.question: What name does Malphas sign the Necrocursica with, and publish his poetry under?

options.label: His own name, Malphas
options.consequence: The sealed text becomes a file with his real name on it. The Heresiology's "without naming him" weakens, and every cross-reference in Codex and Corrant changes.

options.label: "Noxinus Ren" kept as a pen name he chose
options.consequence: The character Noxinus is gone, as Isaac directed, but the name survives as a mask. Codex and Corrant references need few edits, and the mask fits his naming discipline and his later Salter alias.

options.label: Unsigned, or a descriptive signature
options.consequence: His identity is hidden, but the banter between the two authors and the marginal notes lose their anchor.

findings.recommendation: Keep "Noxinus Ren" as a pen name Malphas chose. It honours the replacement, because no separate Noxinus exists any more, and it is the most in-character choice: the file gets built off a word he picked.
findings.correction: This is right in substance. One citation fix: "I would prefer the file be built off a word I chose" and "looked mildly around the room" are at scenes/the_nights_watch.md:227, not 229. The same quote also appears at card:135. The question is Isaac's to make, and the pen-name recommendation stands.

findings.topic: Malphas and Kwon Mu-jin: how the two authors know each other
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:437 "I wrote it with him in mind"; 477 "Vis sent me the third volume"; 485 "File them adjacent." Codex I (wiki):24 "Noxinus set an Alchemical primer on my kitchen table."
findings.canon: Mu-jin learned alchemy at court: "He went into alchemy at the court, under its Senior Alchemist, Doryun" (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:164). Primers are controlled texts issued only on registration (Gate:57). Handing one over outside that system is The Mother's recruitment method: "It recruits by offering what the state has refused" (The Mother.md:22,33). In Mu-jin's Arena scene he describes Malphas's methodology without knowing him (scenes/mujins_interjection_aetherion_arena.md:64). The book puts both men at the Aetherion Academy and "does not decide whether Mu-jin ever reads Salter" (bible.md:153).
findings.why_it_matters: The Codex and the Necrocursica as written are the letters of two close friends. That relationship decides what Mu-jin knows in his Arena speech and in the Aetherion years.
findings.question: How do Malphas and Mu-jin know each other, now that they wrote the two paired books?

options.label: Old companions, and Mu-jin knows who Malphas is
options.consequence: The Codex's portrait of his friend stays warm. The Arena speech becomes knowing, Mu-jin keeps a secret about The Mother's founder, and Aetherion has to decide whether he recognises Salter.

options.label: Strangers who only exchanged manuscripts
options.consequence: The Codex's intimate Noxinus scenes (the terrace, the primer, the night reading) must go to someone else. The Codex seam carries the rewrite.

options.label: Mu-jin knows the pen name, never the man
options.consequence: They correspond as "N. Ren" and Mu-jin never learns that Ren is Malphas, which gives the strongest irony at the Arena and at Aetherion. It needs the pen-name choice from mn-05, and the primer scene either moves or becomes a later forbidden text rather than his first alchemy.

findings.recommendation: Mu-jin knows the pen name, never the man. It keeps the Codex's affection and Appendix II, respects bible.md:153 and the dramatic irony in the Arena scene, and avoids contradicting Mu-jin's court training under Doryun. The primer becomes a later, unlicensed text rather than his introduction to alchemy.
findings.verify_evidence: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Kwon Mu-jin.md:164 (Doryun); Gate:57 (Apprentice's Primer issued against registration); The Mother.md:22,33; scenes/mujins_interjection_aetherion_arena.md:64; bible.md:153; wiki Volume the First.md:24; Necrocursica:437,477,485. See the missed item on Arena lines 5, 17 and 25, which strengthens this finding.

findings.topic: His standing and his schools: the Alchemist-Scribe office, the Pyraeon Forge Academy, the Heralds Medical University, Genesio
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:5 "Alchemist-Scribe of the Trans-Alftian Accord"; 169 "Paracelsus developed the primary stabilization protocol during our years at the Heralds Medical University".
findings.canon: Card:20 "Expelled from the Pyraeon Forge Academy and declared a metaphysical threat. Unbound in life." Card:125-128: he worked alone at the Academy's benches, was expelled over the ferment in his stillroom, and after that "answered to no school and no house". The Academy has no place or face in canon and is not yet ratified as attested (imports/lore/clusters/c23.md:181,195; Zeraphine card:17). The Heralds Medical University appears only in Codex I (Volume the First.md:59), where the narrator and Paracelsus study, not Noxinus. "Trans-Alftian Accord" and "Alchemist-Scribe" appear nowhere in canon. The Guild Accord is still forming (R60-09 live). The book's Aetherion post is Doctor of the pouring (bible.md:167, originated).
findings.why_it_matters: An institutional office and a second university contradict "unbound" and "no school" on the card, and the title page is where a reader meets the author.
findings.question: Which schools and offices belong in Malphas's life as the author, given the card says he answered to no school after his expulsion?

options.label: Pyraeon only; drop the office; Paracelsus was never a classmate
options.consequence: The title page describes him by his canon standing (expelled, declared a threat), which is darkly funny. "Our years at the Heralds Medical University" becomes Paracelsus's years alone, and Malphas knows him as a correspondent. The card is untouched.

options.label: Pyraeon, then the Heralds Medical University under a false name
options.consequence: This keeps the Paracelsus friendship intact and foreshadows the Salter alias, but it adds a second school to the card's Making and bends "no school".

options.label: The office is imposed by his compellers as a leash
options.consequence: This keeps "Alchemist-Scribe" as a sentence title he mocks, and fits the Submission reading (mn-08). It invents a "Trans-Alftian Accord" canon lacks.

findings.recommendation: Pyraeon only. It changes nothing on the card, gives the title page a line in his own dry voice, and keeps Genesio as the place of confinement (canon is silent there, not contradicting). Flag the Pyraeon Forge Academy for ratification at the same time.
findings.correction: The doc_claim quote is not in the Necrocursica: the words "Paracelsus developed the primary stabilization protocol during our years at the Heralds Medical University" appear nowhere in it. Line 169 is Category Two. The nearest text is the Appendix I title (455, Protocol "as Developed by Paracelsus Furveus and Modified... by Noxinus Ren"), and line 121 calls Paracelsus only "my colleague". The University belongs to the Codex narrator (Vol I wiki:59), and Noxinus stays at Genesio (vol1_vault.txt:27). So there is no Pyraeon-versus-Heralds conflict for Malphas, and option 1's consequence rewrites a sentence that does not exist. Genesio is also not canon-silent (Heresiology:211). The real conflict is narrower: the office "Alchemist-Scribe of the Trans-Alftian Accord" (5) against card:20 "Unbound in life" and card:128 "answered to no school and no house". Note too that "Trans-Alftian" is the Codex's region (Vol I wiki:20) and "the Accord" exists in canon as the Guild Accord (scene:223; R60-09). Narrowed question: does the title page keep an office at all, and if so is it a sentence title imposed by his compellers? Recommendation: drop the office and state his canon standing. 'Colleague' needs no change.

findings.topic: The Heresiology's Compelled Author: Dissolution Perverted (Submission) as Malphas's first corruption
findings.doc_claim: Codex II docx:165: Dissolution Perverted "is the stage that produces Noxinus writing the Necrocursica because Gillus De Raits created the conditions for capitulation."
findings.canon: The Heresiology is the in-world treatise on seven ways alchemy goes wrong. Its Case II reads: "A talented writer, pulled by access and manipulated through need... The warning survived as a footnote" (wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:209). It lists the signs of Submission, including "someone would have done it anyway" (Heresiology:74), which Codex II docx:111 has him say. Malphas's primary Wellspring is Dissolution (card:53), and his named corruption is Fermentation Perverted (card:45; Heresiology:111). The Mother's aims include getting "a sealed text" (The Mother.md:31). The Necrocursica's own preface tells a coercion story with no bargain for access (Necrocursica:37-45).
findings.why_it_matters: If Malphas is the author, the Heresiology describes him twice without naming him, and the "access" story versus the "compulsion" story must agree.
findings.question: Is Malphas the Heresiology's "Compelled Author"? That case is Submission: a talented person who dissolves into someone else's will, traded for access. It would sit before his better-known corruption, Fermentation Perverted, which values rot as productive.

options.label: Yes: Submission first, then Catastrophic Germination (Fermentation Perverted)
options.consequence: Case II stays as written and one life shows two corruptions. Submission is the perverted form of his own primary Wellspring, Dissolution. The preface should add the access bargain for the sealed stacks alongside the coercion.

options.label: No: pure coercion, not submission
options.consequence: Case II must be re-pointed or cut, and the Codex author's diagnosis becomes a friend's misreading.

options.label: Case II stands as the Heresiology's misdiagnosis
options.consequence: In-world scholars thought he submitted, but he wanted the stacks all along. This is subtle, and it asks readers to distrust a canon doctrinal text.

findings.recommendation: Yes. It fits Dissolution as his primary Wellspring and his canon want for sealed texts, and it lets the Heresiology describe his whole arc in two entries. It also explains why Case IV (Thom's Genesio work, Heresiology:211, which supplies his tell "crowned with achievements") sits beside his own case.
findings.correction: The Heresiology does not name the corruption behind Case II. Only Codex II docx:165 (a source being converted, not canon) calls it Dissolution Perverted. Canon supports two readings. For Submission: the signs at Heresiology:74 and the "court scholar engineering taboo procedures in exchange for archive access" at :75. For Distillation Perverted: its Common expressions at :127 are "Necromantic manuals whose warnings survive only as footnotes", which is Case II's footnote exactly (:209). The Heresiology also never names Thom in Case IV. Case IV is "The Genesio Activation Sequence" (:211), and its instruction "crowned with achievements" is the tell the card already gives Malphas (card:47; The Mother.md:43). The question should offer Distillation as a third reading, and should note that canon already links Malphas to the Genesio case (see missed items). The recommendation to treat Submission as his first corruption stays reasonable, since Dissolution is his primary (card:53), but it is a choice, not something canon settles.

findings.topic: Where his later life walks into his own warnings (The Mother against the text)
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:305 "if I describe the echoes of the dead as more interesting than the people in the room, treat this document as a confession"; 445 "you come back out".
findings.canon: Fifth Corruption (preferring the dead, 289-305): he ends standing in Mortalis "the whole of the ground he stands on" (card:54, 24-26). But the Fifth's victims are "absent" and "not dangerous" (293), while his canon corruption is the dangerous Fermentation Perverted (The Mother.md:40-43). Sixth (Nomenclature, 311-333): he later names things deliberately so the file is built on his word (The Mother.md:51; scenes/the_nights_watch.md:227-229). Third (Incomplete Sealing, 239-257; an unsealed made-body "noticeably more itself"): the Ferriby wedge grew a quarter inch inside a sealed Fixatio tin (scenes/the_nights_watch.md:277-279); "It does not know it has finished" (:165); The Mother's tell is "Growth under a sealed lid" (The Mother.md:77). Yet he says "Without an anchor it cannot persist" (:223), against his own line 245. Fourth, the Aetheric Bleed (263-277): "bleed" is canon's cover word, "Wellspring bleed... no operator indicated" (:19; The Mother.md:49). Revenant doctrine (141-149: "The revenant does not think"): he later says "I do not need a reason. I need a gradient" (:215). The Gate: the text urges handing copies to Accord archivists (61), while The Mother teaches what the Gate forbids (The Mother.md:33; R60-25). Category Three names Thom's scaled work (173), which is the Heresiology's model case of Fermentation Perverted (Heresiology:211).
findings.why_it_matters: These echoes are the strongest payoff of the new attribution. The anchor contradiction and the word "bleed" will read as mistakes unless someone decides they are deliberate.
findings.question: How openly should the Necrocursica foreshadow the man Malphas becomes, and does The Mother use it?

options.label: Leave the doctrine as written and let the ironies stand unspoken
options.consequence: Minimal edits. The anchor contradiction reads as Malphas later revising his own doctrine, and "bleed" as a private joke.

options.label: Add the later annotation layer: the lich writes in his own margins
options.consequence: It uses "Annotated... with growing enthusiasm by the same" (line 9). Short notes against the Fifth, the Third and Category Four let the reader watch the author cross his own lines. The text becomes a document in two voices.

options.label: Make it The Mother's scripture
options.consequence: It ties R60-24 (a cult following the Becoming) to a text. It requires fixing the order problem: the Greyshaft culture predates the Becoming.

findings.recommendation: Add the annotation layer, and keep the core warnings exactly as a sincere Stage IX man would write them. The margins carry the lich's view, including a note that tissue without a Trace or Crystal needs no anchor, which settles the contradiction with line 245. Keep "bleed" as deliberate. Leave the scripture question until R60-24's ordering is logged.
findings.correction: The echoes are real and the question is Isaac's. The "anchor contradiction", though, is not established, so the recommendation's margin note "settling" it is not needed. Necrocursica:245 and 249 concern an absent Sealing Glyph (the chain that closes a working). An unsealed body "becomes progressively more coherent" (245) and is "noticeably more itself" (249, not 245). Malphas's line at scene:223 (also card:135) is about an anchor, which he calls a binding and a name. The two are different glyph functions, and the text never says an anchorless working persists. The Third-Corruption echo in the Ferriby wedge (scene:277-279) stands, as do the "bleed" cover word (scene:19; The Mother.md:49), the Fifth (293, 305) and the Sixth (333; The Mother.md:51). Drop the anchor item, or ask it only as a mechanism question for the magic-system seam.

findings.topic: The treatise has no category for a lich, and its author becomes one
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:181 "Full resurrection is Category Four. Category Four is not authorized." 145: "The revenant does not think. It is not the deceased."
findings.canon: "Death is almost always permanent; the only exceptions are liches, the undead and their kind" (RULINGS.md:1999). Liches are necromancers bound to phylacteries (wiki/Aberrations/Lich.md:16). Malphas "did not seek out a lichdom in the conventional sense" (card:26). His Essence Core is split between his chest and the Golden Remnant (card:42), which is "Cannot be destroyed and killed him outright the way a phylactery... works" (card:99).
findings.why_it_matters: The Necrocursica's taxonomy of the dead leaves out the only kind of death canon allows to be undone, and that kind is the one its author later enters.
findings.question: Should the Necrocursica discuss lichdom, where the dead person is still himself, and if so in which layer?

options.label: Silent, deliberately
options.consequence: The author's own fate is the hole in his system. This is elegant, but readers may think the omission is an oversight.

options.label: A short passage in the core text dismissing lichdom as old stories
options.consequence: His younger self is visibly wrong. It needs doctrine on how a lich differs from Category Four.

options.label: Only in the later margins
options.consequence: The lich corrects his own thesis in his own hand. This depends on the annotation layer (mn-09).

findings.recommendation: Only in the later margins. The core stays true to what he knew at Stage IX, and the correction arrives in the voice of the one practitioner qualified to make it.
findings.verify_evidence: RULINGS.md:1999 (R60-04 live); wiki/Aberrations/Lich.md:16; card:26,42,99; Necrocursica:145,181. One nuance: R60-04 also exempts 'the undead and their kind', and the Necrocursica's revenant (141-145) is arguably that kind, so the treatise does not omit undeath entirely. It omits only a dead person who is still himself.

findings.topic: Two Necrocursicas: the manuscript the Codex describes and the sealed edition we have
findings.doc_claim: Codex II docx:99 describes "three categories" (Harmonic Imprint, Sympathetic Bond Trace, Parunic Echo) plus a footnote "Never claim it is the soul". Necrocursica:93-109 lists four different categories and has no such footnote.
findings.canon: Canon is silent beyond the documents. wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:58 and the wiki Codex II follow the three categories. The Heresiology depends on the footnote: "The warning survived as a footnote" (Heresiology:209). The Necrocursica cites Codex I to III and the Corrant Papers (109, 497) and answers Codex Vol III (477). Yet Codex I already has it written (Volume the First.md:86), and Corrant docx:75 dates it about twelve years before Thom's submission.
findings.why_it_matters: This decides whether Malphas writes once or twice, which fixes both of his writing dates (mn-02) and where the Heresiology's footnote lives. The residue-category naming belongs to its own seam; only the authorship timing is raised here.
findings.question: Did Malphas write one Necrocursica or two: a first manuscript, then a later sealed edition?

options.label: Two editions: a manuscript at Invocation and a sealed Genesio edition years later
options.consequence: The Codex's three categories and footnote belong to the first. The four categories, the appendices and the margins (mn-09) belong to the second. Little of either document has to change.

options.label: One text, with the Codex conformed to it
options.consequence: Codex II, the Lore meta page and Corrant are rewritten for four categories. The footnote must be added, and Appendix II still postdates Codex III.

options.label: One text, conformed to the Codex
options.consequence: The Necrocursica loses the Volitional Trace as its own idea, and Appendix II has to go.

findings.recommendation: Two editions. The title page already implies later annotation, Appendix II needs a later date anyway, and it lets the Stage IX man and the older Malphas each have a layer.
findings.correction: This is right in substance, with one line fix: the footnote "Never claim it is the soul" is at Codex II docx:103, not 99. Supporting detail for the two-edition option: Necrocursica:93 says the four categories were formalized "through the collaborative work of De Raits, Thom, and Trismegistus", so the surviving sealed text postdates the Codex events. The decision stands, and the recommendation of two editions is sound.
findings.verify_evidence: Codex II docx:99,103,167; Necrocursica:93-109,477,497; wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:58; Heresiology:209; Corrant docx:75-77; wiki Volume the First.md:86

findings.topic: Voice: the card has no Voice block; the scene voice against the Necrocursica voice
findings.doc_claim: Necrocursica:13 "this warning has been ignored before and will presumably be ignored again"; 369 "He looked like the mountains themselves had sent for him."
findings.canon: R52-03 (live in out/rules.resolved.json) requires every major card to carry a full voice block. Malphas's card has none (no "Voice" heading in the file). Fits: contraction rate 0.0 (table/voices.yaml:308), and the Necrocursica has no verbal contractions either (only possessives). Dry dark humour is present in the scene: "Then they will have a bad spring in a ledger" (scenes/the_nights_watch.md:175). Divergences: in the scene he is opaque, "seen, never entered" (bible.md:21), speaks "the way a man reads a bill of lading" (:197) and looks "mildly" around the room (:229). The Necrocursica, by contrast, is confessional (305, 333), warm toward Paracelsus (121, 397), lyrical on the platform (369-373), and claims "honesty is a principle I hold" (53), while his craft is making readings come out clean.
findings.why_it_matters: Without a voice block there is no fixed standard to convert the text against, and the Necrocursica's warmth could either give Malphas an inner life or break his opacity.
findings.question: Whose voice governs: the cold, opaque commander at the coldhouse or the dry, confessional writer of the Necrocursica? And what goes into his missing voice block?

options.label: Two registers, one man
options.consequence: Write the voice block with command as his default and the Necrocursica's candour as his grief and joy shifts, the man before The Mother. Trim the chatty tics and keep the confessions. His fall becomes visible in his voice.

options.label: Conform the text to the coldhouse
options.consequence: Colder and shorter, with the humour bone-dry and the confessions cut. That loses the Fifth-Corruption "confession" line, which is the best payoff of the new attribution.

options.label: The candour is strategy
options.consequence: Every self-accusation is a word he chose for the file. This is consistent with his naming method, but it makes the whole text untrustworthy and flattens the tragedy.

findings.recommendation: Two registers, one man, and write the missing R52-03 voice block in the same pass. The shared traits (no contractions, dry wit, precision) already bridge the two voices, and the Stage IX date (mn-02) explains why the warmth is there and why it is gone by Greyshaft Nine.
findings.correction: Status should be ambiguous, not conflict. Canon keeps Malphas opaque by point of view: he is seen only from Vesk, Nuvalik, Foss and Deming until Movement VI (bible.md:21). That is a choice about how others see him, not a statement that he has no inner life, so a first-person treatise does not contradict it. Citation fixes: bible.md:21 reads "stays opaque", and the phrase "seen, never entered" is not in the bible. "Looked mildly around the room" is at scene:227, not 229. Also relevant: R52-04 (live) sets contractions per card, and his card sets none. The 0.0 rate (voices.yaml:308) is measured, not set, so the new voice block should set it to 'never'. The question and the recommendation (two registers, one man, and write the block) stand.

missed.topic: The Guild Accord is 'forming now', but the Necrocursica assumes a mature Accord
missed.detail: The Necrocursica takes a settled Accord for granted: Level IV to VI clearances, authorized Categories I to III, "the Accord's theoretical canon", Accord archivists and Accord channels. Live canon says the Guild Accord is forming during the story and binds only where a circle has signed. Mu-jin's Arena speech also describes a period "before the Accord existed to enforce alchemical law". If a living Malphas writes in the Withering-Era present (mn-02, mn-03), that apparatus has to be rewritten around a forming Accord or put in someone else's system. The auditor mentions R60-09 only in passing, under mn-07.
missed.evidence: out/rules.resolved.json R60-09-ACCORD_FORMING_NOW live ('The Guild Accord is forming now'); R60-18-ACCORD_FORMING_IN_CIRCLES live; Necrocursica:13,61,93,169,173,181,455,497; scenes/mujins_interjection_aetherion_arena.md:17; scenes/the_nights_watch.md:223
missed.question: The Necrocursica is full of Accord clearance levels and authorized operation categories. Canon says the Guild Accord (the league of hunting guilds, still being negotiated) is only forming now. Whose system do the clearances belong to? Options: (a) Keep them as the forming Accord's early protocols, binding only in circles that have signed. Few edits, and they show the Accord in formation. (b) Move them to a crown office or to Sancta Lux. The compeller question (mn-04) settles which. (c) Make them the compellers' private classification system, which Malphas mocks. That is darkly funny and fits the coercion. Recommendation: (a). It keeps the text intact and matches R60-18.

missed.topic: Canon already ties Malphas's tell to the Heresiology's Genesio case
missed.detail: The card says the Heresiology "named him without naming him", and gives his tell as "it arrives crowned with achievements". That phrase exists only in Heresiology Case IV, "The Genesio Activation Sequence" (old traces activated in pursuit of unfinished good). In the Codex and Corrant texts, the Genesio activation is Thom's Volitional Trace work, with Gillus. With Malphas confined at Genesio, the reader will ask whether he took part in the Genesio activation or was only its theorist. The auditor calls Case IV "Thom's Genesio work", but the Heresiology never names Thom.
missed.evidence: card:45-47; wiki/Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/The Mother.md:43; wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:211; Necrocursica:173 ('This is what Vaughaus Thom replicated at scale'); Corrant docx:255
missed.question: Is Malphas part of the Genesio Activation Sequence (the Heresiology's case where old death-traces were activated for good ends and slowly damaged the region)? Options: (a) Theorist only: he wrote the architecture and Thom ran it. The card's tell becomes irony, since he wrote the warning for a case that later becomes his own. (b) A silent partner: his Category Three protocol is what Thom scaled, which is the start of Fermentation Perverted and the seed of The Mother. (c) He replaces Thom as operator. That is a large rewrite of the Corrant Papers and Codex III. Recommendation: (a), which keeps the Codex and Corrant plots and makes the card's tell a line he lives into.

missed.topic: Mu-jin's Arena speech: an old Mu-jin, the same source material, and marginal notes
missed.detail: In the canon Arena scene, Mu-jin is white-haired and "older than anyone else present". He says the perpetrator (Malphas, by the scene's own note) "has studied the same source material I have studied". That source is marginal notes in a controlled archive (the Zettari archives, originated) recording forbidden Mortalis experiments. Now that Mu-jin writes the Codex and Malphas the sealed, marginally annotated Necrocursica, this passage is either the payoff (the source they share is the Necrocursica and the Codex) or a contradiction (Mu-jin speaks as if the material were anonymous and centuries old). It also bears on the Codex's claim that Noxinus was "older" than the narrator (Vol I wiki:87), against a very old Mu-jin at Aetherion while Malphas teaches there as Salter.
missed.evidence: scenes/mujins_interjection_aetherion_arena.md:5,17,25,51,64; Necrocursica:21 ('Marginal note, Noxinus Ren, undated'),13; wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:87; bible.md:43,153,167
missed.question: Is the Necrocursica part of the forbidden source material Mu-jin says he and the culprit both studied? Options: (a) Yes: the sealed Necrocursica sits in the controlled archive beside the Zettari notes. The Arena speech gains a buried confession, which fits mn-06's 'knows the pen name, never the man'. (b) No: the Zettari notes are separate and older, and the Necrocursica stays a private manuscript. There is no link at the Arena. (c) The Zettari marginal notes are the Necrocursica's own margins. That merges two canon threads, but it changes an originated detail in an archived scene. Recommendation: (a). It uses canon as it stands and needs no edit to the scene.

missed.topic: The Necrocursica makes the Codex author a co-formalizer of the doctrine the villains use
missed.detail: The Necrocursica credits the four residue categories (including the Volitional Trace used in Category Three operations) to "De Raits, Thom, and Trismegistus", and names Trismegistus at four other places. Replacing Vis with Kwon Mu-jin is mechanical in itself. But it makes Mu-jin a co-author, with Gillus and Thom, of the doctrine behind the impression-bodies, which sits hard with his canon Arena stance of condemning the culprit's method. The auditor did not raise it.
missed.evidence: Necrocursica:93,437,465,477,497; scenes/mujins_interjection_aetherion_arena.md:25; out/rules.resolved.json R52-21-KWON live
missed.question: When 'Trismegistus' becomes Mu-jin, does Mu-jin keep his credit as co-formalizer of the four residue categories alongside Gillus and Thom? Options: (a) Keep it: Mu-jin helped build the theory he later condemns, which deepens his Arena guilt. (b) Cut him from line 93 and credit only De Raits and Thom; he stays the outside witness the Appendix calls him (465). (c) Credit him as annotator only, as in the cross-reference at 497. Recommendation: (c). It matches the Necrocursica's own cross-reference and Appendix II, and keeps the Arena speech honest.

seams.title: Internal contradictions, versions, open docket
seams.summary: The five texts disagree about their own timeline. The Necrocursica as supplied cites Codex Volumes I to III, the Corrant file and a "formalized" four-residue canon, yet Volume II has the narrator read it before the commission. The Thom submission is dated twelve years old, yet Thom derived it from a commission about two years old. Authorship is claimed five ways for the Volitional Trace and four ways for how the Necrocursica was written. The Aphorism of Mortalis exists in two versions, and the Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions exist as two unrelated lists; canon (the Heresiology, the God Hand page) backs only the stage-based list. The wiki pages quote faithfully but drop almost every line that carries a date, a place or an authorship claim, switch to a mixed third-person voice, change one meaning, and silently drop two canon errors the docx still carries. A Volume I docx does exist (~/wotr-vault/true-canon/THE-ALFTIAN-CODEX.docx), so the supplied "duplicate" was the wrong file. No conflict row or docket item is open on alchemy, Mortalis, Anamnesis, the Codex, the Necrocursica, the Heresiology, Mu-jin or Malphas. The ruled items that bear on the conversion are the Alchemical Index rulings, C-084 and R60-09 (the Accord forming now), R57-01 (Mu-jin is 38; the wiki mirror still reads 24) and the Malphas/Mother rulings. The texts' "Era of Voyagers" stamp clashes with canon's Voyager Era (000 to 070 IC) and with an author who is 38 today.

findings.topic: Chronology: the Necrocursica postdates the Codex that reads it
findings.doc_claim: Vol I docx L88: "The Necrocursica — Noxinus's compelled treatise. I have not read it." Vol II docx L89-103: the narrator reads the finished manuscript before the commission and quotes its footnote "Not the soul. Never claim it is the soul." Necrocursica L93: residues "now formalized... through the collaborative work of De Raits, Thom, and Trismegistus"; L109: "central to Volumes I through III of the Alftian Codex"; L173 cites "the Alftian Codex and the Corrant Papers"; L477: "Vis sent me the third volume". L25 marginal: "He sent me a copy when it was finished... did not open it for four months", against Vol II L89, where Noxinus brings it "under his arm". The footnote Vol II quotes appears nowhere in the supplied Necrocursica.
findings.canon: wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:209: "The warning survived as a footnote." :127: "Necromantic manuals whose warnings survive only as footnotes." Canon is silent on editions and dates.
findings.why_it_matters: As supplied, the Necrocursica cannot exist when Volumes I and II say it does. The Heresiology's Case II also depends on a footnote the supplied text lacks.
findings.question: The Necrocursica we have quotes all three Codex volumes and the investigator's file, yet the Codex narrator reads it before any of that happens. How do we fix the order?

options.label: Two editions
options.consequence: The Codex reads a first edition (three residues, with the footnote). The supplied text becomes a revised edition written after Volume III. It gains a short edition note, and the footnote is restored. Every event in all five texts stays.

options.label: Strip the forward references
options.consequence: Cut the Volume I to III and Corrant citations, the 'formalized' line and Appendix II. This loses the 'file them adjacent' pairing, and its four-residue scheme then contradicts Volume II outright (see ct-08).

options.label: Move composition after Volume III
options.consequence: Volume II chapter 6 (the reading scene and the footnote exchange) goes, and Volume I's 'I have not read it' goes too. The Heresiology's Case II loses its source scene.

findings.recommendation: Two editions. It needs the fewest edits, a revised edition by Malphas is natural, and it restores the footnote canon already relies on.
findings.correction: The inversion is real, but two details need fixing. (1) Vol II L89 itself says "I resisted reading it for some months" before Noxinus brought the manuscript. That partly matches Necrocursica L25's "did not open it for four months", so L25 against L89 is a smaller clash than stated. (2) There is a third clock the finding misses. Corrant L75 dates the Thom submission "approximately twelve years" after the Necrocursica, and Corrant L101 says the submission has sat twelve years. Together they put the Necrocursica about 24 years back, which cannot fit Vol II's fresh manuscript at a two-year-old commission. The two-editions recommendation stands, but the first edition's date has to be set together with ct-02.

findings.topic: Chronology: the Thom submission is 'twelve years' old but comes from a two-year-old commission
findings.doc_claim: Corrant L75: the submission "postdates it by approximately twelve years"; L101: "sitting in a sealed stack for twelve years". Vol III L150: "sitting in the Genesio Archivum for twelve years". Vol III L298, Thom: "I spent twelve years activating". Against that, Vol III L122: Thom "observed what I did with Madeleine Ault's commission and extracted the theoretical framework"; L188: "You should have stopped two years ago". Vol II L187, Gillus: the fourth category is "Not described anywhere I have found in the Herald's tradition or the Trans-Alftian Archivum". Vol III L280: Madeleine "documented it more completely than Vaughaus managed". Merged minor item: Vol III L30 says Thom "scaled it to regional catastrophe", while L132 says "He is doing good".
findings.canon: Canon is silent on dates. wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:211: "Works were completed. Benefits were undeniable. So too were the accumulating distortions". :86 names the Separation Perverted archivist "who knows a manuscript is dangerous and shelves it".
findings.why_it_matters: The order of discovery (Madeleine, then Gillus, then Thom) and the start of the Tempus drift both hang on this number. As written, Thom files a paper on an idea about ten years before the event he learned it from.
findings.question: Thom's paper on the fourth residue (the Volitional Trace) is twelve years old in two texts, but he learned the idea by watching a commission that happened about two years ago. Which clock wins?

options.label: Anchor on the commission (about two years)
options.consequence: Change 'twelve years' at Corrant L75 and L101 and Vol III L150 and L298. Madeleine's priority, Gillus's Volume II claim and the drift first appearing at the commission all hold. Corrant's shelved-paper beat shrinks to under two years but survives.

options.label: Keep twelve years
options.consequence: Thom found it first and independently. Cut Vol III L122's 'observed... extracted', rewrite Vol III's attribution chain and Gillus's 'my work', and explain why Tempus drifted only at the commission after twelve years of activation.

options.label: Twelve-year paper on activation only
options.consequence: Thom's old paper covers crude activation. A fourth-residue addendum is dated after the commission. This keeps the long shelving beat but needs a new addendum sentence in Corrant and a rewrite of the review note at L93.

findings.recommendation: Anchor on the commission. It changes four numbers, leaves every authorship line intact, and fits the drift and the 'last eighteen months' of anomalies (Corrant L205).
findings.correction: Three fixes. (1) Corrant L75 does not say the submission is twelve years old. It says the submission "postdates" the Necrocursica by twelve years, so any fix to the date also moves the Necrocursica (see ct-01). (2) Drop the merged item about Vol III L30 and L132. At L132 Gillus says "He is doing good" "with precise emphasis on the verb. This is the difficulty": that is deliberate irony, not a contradiction. (3) The option costs are wrong. Vol III already treats Thom's twelve-year paper as early, independent work: L150, L298, L340 ("independently described") and L280 (Madeleine documented the category in the Thom submission "more completely than Vaughaus managed"). Gillus's Vol II L187 is hedged ("anywhere I have found"), and the paper sat sealed and unread. So 'Keep twelve years' needs only L340's 'first' and L122 read as the completion method. 'Anchor on the commission' needs Corrant L75, L101, Vol III L150, L298 and a reread of L280, not just four numbers. The choice is still Isaac's. The recommendation should favour option 3: the old paper covers the residue and crude activation, and the completion framework comes after the commission. This is the reading the texts already half-support.

findings.topic: Authorship claim: how and where the Necrocursica was written
findings.doc_claim: Vol I docx L44: Noxinus was "forced with his considerable poetic talent to write treatise after treatise on their studies" (Gillus and Thom). The wiki Vol I :86 changes this to "compelled by his considerable poetic talent". Vol II docx L85: an exchange for "access to the Archivum's restricted Aetheric stacks", and "The exchange was, from the outside, clean." Necrocursica L5: "Authored under compulsion... during his confinement at the Genesio Monastery", with a hurt left hand; L37: visitors "arrived at my apartment in Genesio", one of whom "goes by a title". Corrant L255, Gillus: "The Necrocursica was my project." Merged: Necrocursica L169 says "our years at the Heralds Medical University", but Vol I docx L27 sends only the narrator and Paracelsus there.
findings.canon: wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:209: "A talented writer, pulled by access and manipulated through need". This matches Volume II; canon is silent on confinement. Context: R60-25-WHAT_MALPHAS_WANTS (rules/doc-combat-society-politics-law-2026-09-26.yaml:533), 'to obtain the unattainable'.
findings.why_it_matters: With Malphas as the new author, the origin story decides his motive and whether the Heresiology's 'compelled author' case (Case II) still describes him.
findings.question: The texts give four origins for the Necrocursica: a clean trade for library access, pressure from Gillus and Thom, confinement with an injured hand, or Gillus's own project. With Malphas writing it, which is true?

options.label: Trade for access (Volume II, and the Heresiology)
options.consequence: Malphas writes it in exchange for sealed stacks he could not otherwise reach. Heresiology Case II stands unchanged. The Necrocursica's title page and preface lose 'under compulsion' and the hand.

options.label: Coercion (the Necrocursica's version)
options.consequence: Heresiology Case II must be reworded. A Stage XIV Zenith undead (Malphas card :62) being confined and hurt needs an explanation, or the book must be dated before his Becoming.

options.label: The patron's project
options.consequence: Gillus's replacement commissions it and Malphas writes it willingly. The Heresiology's Case II loses its subject, and Volume II's example of the Second Corruption (Submission) has to change.

findings.recommendation: Trade for access. Canon already says it, it fits what R60-25 says Malphas wants, and it keeps both the Heresiology case and the Second Corruption example. On reconversion, restore Volume I's 'forced with' meaning or drop the line.
findings.correction: Vol II does not describe a clean trade. L85 says "The exchange was, from the outside, clean", and then "What the Necrocursica became was less clean." At L165 Vol II makes Noxinus its example of Dissolution Perverted (the Corruption of Submission), because "Gillus De Raits created the conditions for capitulation". Canon's Case II is headed "The Compelled Author" and says "pulled by access and manipulated through need". So canon's version is pressure plus access, not a free trade. The recommendation is also wrong that option 1 keeps the Second Corruption example. With Malphas as author (Stage XIV Zenith, and tied in canon to Fermentation Perverted), a writer 'absorbed by someone else's will' before he was ready no longer fits. Relabel option 1 as 'pressure plus access (Vol II and the Heresiology)'. Add to the question whether Vol II's Dissolution-Perverted example survives the change of author, or moves to someone else.

findings.topic: Authorship claim: who found, named and built the Volitional Trace, and who designed the commission
findings.doc_claim: Vol II App L261, narrator: "I have since developed a theoretical framework for it. I call it the Volitional Trace". Corrant L255, Gillus: "The Volitional Trace theory is my work, however Noxinus wrote the architecture and Paracelsus proved the initial method." Corrant L175 credits "what Noxinus Ren recorded in a footnote". Vol III L340: "first documented by Madeleine Ault and independently described by Vaughaus Thom and theoretically named by Gillus De Raits". Necrocursica L93 credits "De Raits, Thom, and Trismegistus". On the commission: Vol II L23, "Paracelsus has taken the commission"; Corrant L187, Gillus "commissioned Paracelsus"; Vol III L66, Gillus "designed the Volitional Trace method"; Vol III L274, "She designed the commission"; Necrocursica L465, "Cassian Ault's commission".
findings.canon: Canon is silent. wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:210 (Case III) names no designer. The overview page wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:63 repeats Volume III's chain as fact.
findings.why_it_matters: The Codex's central discovery has five owners, two of whom claim the name. The overview page states one chain as settled fact.
findings.question: Who first found the 'fourth residue' (the Volitional Trace, the record of an unfinished decision), who named it, and who designed the grief-commission?

options.label: Layered credit
options.consequence: Madeleine found it and designed the purpose. Gillus framed the theory and built the mechanism. The narrator (Mu-jin) coined the name in Volume II. Thom found it independently. Paracelsus executed and Cassian paid. Edit Vol III L66 and L340 and the overview :63; Gillus's 'my work' stays as his own boast. Mu-jin gains a real contribution.

options.label: Gillus owns it
options.consequence: His letter to Corrant is true and Volume III's chain is the narrator's generosity. Volume II's 'I call it' goes, and Madeleine's priority shrinks.

options.label: Leave the disagreement as deliberate unreliable narration
options.consequence: No text edits (Lore & History :32 calls the Codex 'unreliable by construction'). The Necrocursica and the overview page must stop stating one chain as fact.

findings.recommendation: Layered credit. Small edits make every text true at its own level, and the new author gets the naming.

findings.topic: The Aphorism of Mortalis: two texts, and two claimed origins
findings.doc_claim: Vol I docx L43: the Aphorism is "a knowledge-limiting doctrine embedded inside the necromantic tradition": the practitioner is "a debtor who had taken a loan from the Wellspring of Mortalis". Vol II docx L33: "I wrote this down once, in a paper I did not circulate", followed by a different text, "He summons himself, arranged in their image". Vol III L24: "the Aphorism of Mortalis, which I wrote in the second volume". Corrant L181: "Vis Trismegistus wrote that."
findings.canon: Canon is silent on the Aphorism. wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:170 (Mortalis row): "The dead may leave traces. The trace is not the soul."
findings.why_it_matters: One named doctrine has two contents (a cost owed by the practitioner's Soul Crystal, and self-deception) and two origins (an old tradition, and the narrator's own paper). The conversion to a new narrator makes the authorship line load-bearing.
findings.question: Is the Aphorism of Mortalis an old necromantic doctrine about a debt the practitioner pays, or the narrator's own sentence about self-deception?

options.label: Both, in sequence
options.consequence: Volume I's is the tradition's old 'debt' Aphorism. The narrator's Volume II sentence is his restatement, which took the name. Add one clause in Volume II saying so. The debt version stays available for the alchemy-cost rewrite.

options.label: Only the narrator's
options.consequence: Rewrite Vol I L43 and the appendix L88 to foreshadow the Volume II text. The debt idea is lost.

options.label: Only the tradition's
options.consequence: Volume II's text becomes the old doctrine, quoted. Strike 'I wrote this down once', Vol III L24's 'which I wrote' and Corrant L181's 'Vis Trismegistus wrote that.'

findings.recommendation: Both, in sequence. It costs one clause and keeps the debt framing, which suits the Fracture of Worlds cost model.
findings.correction: Vol II does not give a rival text of the Aphorism. L33 says that Vis's uncirculated paper ends with "The Aphorism of Mortalis is not a prohibition. It is a warning.", followed by the self-summoning sentence. That is Vis glossing the traditional Aphorism of Vol I L43. The 'Both, in sequence' reading is therefore already in the Vol II text, and no new clause is needed there. The real friction is in three places: Vol III L24 ("which I wrote in the second volume"), Corrant L181 ("Vis Trismegistus wrote that"), and the overview wiki/Lore & History/The Alftian Codex.md:55, which prints the gloss as the Aphorism itself. These make the gloss look like the doctrine. The question is still Isaac's, because the new author inherits it: is the debt version kept as the doctrine for the alchemy-cost rewrite? The edits needed are to Vol III L24 and overview :55, not Vol II.
