findings.topic: Two unrelated lists both called the Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions
findings.doc_claim: The Codex (Vol II docx L145-171, L231-241) lists stage inversions: Calcination Perverted (Conviction), Dissolution Perverted (Submission), Separation Perverted (Non-Commitment). The Necrocursica's title and ch3 (L3, L199-389) list 'the Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions Arising from the Misapplication of Mortalis Law': Mirror Trace, Nospheric Resonance Lock, Incomplete Sealing, Aetheric Bleed, Inversion, Nomenclature, Completion. Vol I docx L90 makes them the subject of the narrator's own forthcoming volume; Necrocursica L53 claims them as its documented cases.
findings.canon: wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:23 ("Each of the seven stages possesses a lawful expression and a corrupt inversion") and :57-134 (the seven, Calcination to Coagulation Perverted). wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Crossing and the Making of the God Hand.md:71: the Heresiology's seven "are inversions of the seven stages of the Great Work"; conflating two sevens is "the standard error".
findings.why_it_matters: The Necrocursica's list uses canon's name for something canon defines differently, and canon already calls such conflation an error.
findings.question: The Necrocursica uses the name 'Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions' for seven Mortalis failure modes, but canon reserves that name for the seven perverted stages of the Great Work. What do we do with the Necrocursica's seven?

options.label: Rename and map
options.consequence: Call them, say, the Seven Unmoorings (the word its own ch4, L425, uses). Drop 'Cacodaemonic' from the title and file each under its Great Work stage per the Heresiology. The content survives and canon holds.

options.label: Keep the name as an in-world error
options.consequence: Malphas deliberately or carelessly misuses the term, and a gloss says so. This is flavourful, but it adds a third 'seven' next to the God Hand page's warning and invites the confusion canon condemns.

options.label: Cut the Necrocursica's chapter 3
options.consequence: It loses the text's strongest material (Completion, Nomenclature, Bleed), and Appendix II's comparison with the Codex falls.

findings.recommendation: Rename and map. It keeps the best material and obeys the Heresiology and the God Hand page.

findings.topic: The four promised Corruptions never arrive, and the Third Corruption changes meaning
findings.doc_claim: Vol II docx L269: "The remaining four Cacodaemonic Corruptions... are subjects for the third volume". Vol III L402: "Thus ends the Alftian Codex, in three volumes", without them. The Third Corruption: Vol II L235, "can see clearly but will not commit to what they see"; Vol III L30, "the inversion that insists on understanding everything except itself"; Necrocursica L469, "the Cacodaemon of Nomenclature, partially". Lore & History :36 and the overview :64 say the Heresiology finishes "a book a dead man left unfinished".
findings.canon: wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:81-90, Separation Perverted: the practitioner "exempts themselves from consequence by retreating into analysis". This fits Volumes II and III. :92-134 give the remaining four.

findings.question: Volume II promises the last four Corruptions in Volume III, and Volume III never gives them. Should the converted Codex name them, or leave them to the Heresiology?

options.label: Volume III names them
options.consequence: A short appendix entry gives Conjunction, Fermentation, Distillation and Coagulation Perverted under the Heresiology's names. The Codex becomes complete, and the Heresiology becomes the doctrinal expansion rather than the completion.

options.label: Leave the gap, openly
options.consequence: Volume III says the four were left undone. Lore & History :36 and the overview :64 are reworded without 'dead man'. The humility arc stays.

options.label: Cut the promise
options.consequence: Remove Vol II L269. The Heresiology's link to the Codex weakens.

findings.recommendation: Leave the gap, openly. It keeps canon's framing with the least new text. In all options, the Necrocursica's Appendix II should call the Codex's Third Corruption Separation Perverted, matching canon.
findings.correction: The 'dead man' line is at wiki/Lore & History/Lore & History.md:35, not :36. The overview :64 does not say 'dead man'. It says "the finished version of a book this man left open", which stays true when the author is Mu-jin. Only L&H :35 needs rewording. The rest stands: Vol III never names Conjunction, Fermentation, Distillation or Coagulation Perverted.

Corrant uses the same names (L57, L171). Necrocursica L93-109 gives four "canonical" categories: Corporeal Residue, Aetheric Shell, Nospheric Echo, Volitional Trace.
findings.canon: Canon is silent on residue categories. wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:126 mentions "residue classes" generically. The Soul Crystal layers are canon: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VIII. Traits, Soul Crystal Tiers, Domains (Parts Twenty–Twenty-Two).md:20 (Essence Core, Attraction Layer, Aether Shell) and wiki/The Magic System/The Ladder and the Draft — Temperance, Advancement and Essence Drafts.md:46. findings.why_it_matters: The Codex claims the Necrocursica describes three residues, and the Necrocursica describes four different ones. Any alchemy rewrite has to pick one set.
findings.question: What remains of a person after death: the Codex's three residues (imprint in places, bond to loved ones, glyph-echo), or the Necrocursica's four (body, outer Aether Shell, mind-echo, unfinished decision)?

options.label: The Necrocursica's four are canonical

options.label: A merged list
options.consequence: More complete, but heavy. Every text needs editing, and the 'fourth residue' label (the core of Volumes II and III) no longer counts correctly.

findings.recommendation: The Necrocursica's four are canonical, with the Codex's three kept as first-edition names. This fits canon's layers and ct-01's two-edition fix.

findings.topic: The Tempus drift: cause and course
findings.doc_claim: Vol II docx L223-229: the drift followed the commission's Mortalis opening. Vol II App L263: "It has stabilised at its new position." Vol III L86: Anamnesis "has been accelerating"; L142: drift caused by "the increase in Anamnetic Wellspring pressure in the Genesio region"; L310: "Tempus will return to its correct position over the next quarter-year". Corrant L27 first suspects the commission, then L209-211 suspects the Anamnesis Wellspring.
findings.canon: wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:212: "Astronomical deviation followed repeated pressure upon a regional metaphysical field." This sides with Volume III's cause. Canon is silent on the drift's course.
findings.why_it_matters: Canon backs Volume III's cause, so Volume II's explanation has to read as a mistake or as a contributing cause.
findings.question: What moved Tempus, and did the drift settle, speed up, or reverse?

options.label: A sequence, with Volume II's cause as the narrator's first wrong guess
options.consequence: The commission's small nudge settles (Volume II), resumes and speeds up with Thom's activations (Volume III), and reverses after the old Trace completes. Add one sentence in Volume III naming the earlier error. This matches the Heresiology.

options.label: Both causes contribute
options.consequence: Keep both explanations as true. The Heresiology's 'repeated pressure' still covers it, but readers get no correction beat.

options.label: Volume II's cause is right
options.consequence: Rewrite Vol III L142 and L310 and the Heresiology's Case V.

findings.recommendation: A sequence, with Volume II's cause as the narrator's first wrong guess. Each text's statement holds at its own date, and canon's case wording stays.

findings.question: Was there one letter from Gillus or two, and which one sat unopened?

options.label: One letter, never intercepted
options.consequence: Cut Corrant's 'original... intercepted' and Volume III's delivery by the investigator. The investigator's doorway beat in Volume III goes.

findings.recommendation: Two letters. It keeps every scene and needs about three phrase edits.

findings.topic: The 'Era of Voyagers' dating against canon's calendar and a present-day author
findings.doc_claim: The texts use the Era of Voyagers as their own present: Vol I docx L3 and L92; Vol II L5 and L281; Vol III L354 and L406; Corrant L107, L125 and L286. They run on railways (Vol I L27, Vol II L213, Vol III ch1, Corrant L39) and a mature Accord bureaucracy (the Research Archives Division, clearance levels, 'the Accord's theoretical canon' at Necrocursica L81). Vol III L122 has the Genesio Wellspring 'pre-dating the current Accord'.
findings.canon: wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Concordance of Ages.md:110: "The Voyager Era · 000 to 070 IC"; :113, "The first decades built nothing"; :104, the Imperial Age is 715 years old; :130, the Withering Era runs from 645 IC to now. R59-04-VEHICLES (rules/doc-era-apparatus-law-2026-09-26.yaml:73) puts railways in the present span. R60-09-ACCORD_FORMING_NOW (rules/doc-combat-society-politics-law-2026-09-26.yaml:186) and C-084 (CONFLICTS.md:1109, ruled at RULINGS.md:2087) say the Accord communion is forming now. R57-01-KWON_MU_JIN_IS_38 (rules/doc-backfill-rulings-2026-09-26.yaml:10).
findings.why_it_matters: Canon puts the Voyager Era 645 to 715 years ago, before any railway. A 38-year-old Mu-jin cannot have written a Voyager-Era text.
findings.question: The texts date themselves to the 'Era of Voyagers', which canon places about 700 years ago, yet they have railways and the new author is 38 today. Re-date them?

options.label: Re-date to the Withering Era, the present
options.consequence: Mu-jin's authorship, the railways (R59-04) and Mu-jin's age all fit. Accord references are read as the old Codex machinery under C-084, with the communion forming now. Every era stamp changes (about ten places).

options.label: Keep the Voyager Era
options.consequence: The texts are about 700 years old, so Mu-jin can only be an editor or transcriber, not the writer. Railways and Accord divisions are anachronisms.

options.label: Remove all era stamps
options.consequence: This avoids the clash but leaves the dating vague, and the colophons lose their archival texture.

findings.recommendation: Re-date to the Withering Era, the present. It is the only option that lets Mu-jin write the Codex without contradicting canon.
findings.correction: The conflict with Mu-jin's age is real, but the canon picture is incomplete. (1) wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/Errata to the Received Registers.md:69 says the Accord's 'Codex articles, the Divisions, the Tiered Path, and the Gate network all date to the Voyager Era'. The Four Ceilings :156 says the same. Under C-084 these are the old Codex machinery, so in the 'Keep the Voyager Era' option the Accord divisions are not anachronisms. (2) Errata :39, copied at imports/BRIEFS/common.md:92, says of 'the Alftian codices' that 'not one of them cites an Age'. The colophons' 'Era of Voyagers' stamps contradict that. Re-dating to the Withering Era would too, unless the Errata line is also edited. Option 3 (remove the stamps) is the only one that agrees with Errata :39 as written. Add Errata :39 to the pages to edit under options 1 and 2. The recommendation (re-date to the present) can stand, since R57-01 still rules out a Voyager-Era author.

It changes 'forced with his considerable poetic talent' to 'compelled by' (wiki :86). Volume II drops 'fourteen Temperance stages' (L67), 'Glory, Sovereignty, Zenith' (L149), 'texts I had brought from Genesio' (L75), 'circulated manuscripts' (L187) and the promise of four more Corruptions (L269). findings.canon: The wiki pages are marked verification "unverified" (wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md:8 and siblings). Canon is silent on which version governs.
findings.why_it_matters: The wiki looks consistent mainly because it omits the lines that contradict. Converting from the wiki would hide the problems in ct-01 to ct-15, not fix them.
findings.question: Which version is the base for the conversion: the full first-person docx, or the shorter wiki pages?

options.label: Docx as base, wiki rebuilt from it
options.consequence: Every contradiction is visible and gets decided here. The converted text is first person throughout, and the wiki pages are then regenerated as condensations of the new text.

options.label: Wiki as base
options.consequence: Faster and already shorter, but it inherits the mixed voice, one changed meaning, and silence on facts later texts depend on (Volume III's references to the investigator's notes, the Genesio distance).

options.label: Docx as base, keeping the wiki's cuts where they removed canon errors

findings.recommendation: Docx as base, keeping the wiki's cuts where they removed canon errors.

'Six years' is his ethics and annotation (Corrant L255, Vol III L66), while the letter sat unopened four months (Vol III L78). Vol I L51: "a script I could not then decipher, though I recognised it as a Parunic dialect older than anything catalogued in the Genesio Archivum". Corrant L17 describes Halveth. Vol I L82 says "after his passing or departure", and no text kills the narrator.

Lore & History :36 and overview :64: drop 'dead man'.

(2) Overview :86 already describes Halveth from Vol III; only its tag is wrong (see ct-14). (3) Overview :29 and :33 ('single unanswered letter') cannot be fixed mechanically until ct-10 decides whether there are one or two letters. What remains mechanical: :29 and :33 must not start the letter in Volume I; :47's 'no Genesio archive could decipher' becomes the Parunic-dialect wording that wiki Vol I :96 already uses. For :45, 'Waits six years' is a defensible summary of Vol III L66 ('corresponding with you through your own text for six years'), not an error, so leave it.

gaps.topic: cc-01 The Codex's closing Correction set against canon's Four Theories of why a Wellspring answers
gaps.question: The Codex ends on 'the Correction': Correspondence is not a mirror but a delayed answer. Canon already has four rival explanations of why a Wellspring answers a practitioner (the Four Theories), and one of them is a Correspondence Position. Where does Mu-jin's Correction sit among them? No seam asks this, yet it is the thesis of all three volumes and the only thing on offer that explains how a working on the ground could move Tempus in the sky.
options: A. Mu-jin's own amendment to the Correspondence Position. It stays one contested school, and the Accord keeps enforcing the Consent Doctrine. Consequence: no system page changes, and L&H:24's line that the formal literature 'does not contain' it stays true.

B. A merger of the Correspondence and Debt Positions: the answer comes late, on credit, and is settled out of sight. Consequence: this ties in the Aphorism of Mortalis's debt reading (ct-05) and the eastern commission, since the Debt Position is 'held mostly in the eastern quarter'. The Physical Account gains a line.

C. Canon law: this is how Wellsprings actually answer. Consequence: it contradicts the Physical Account's statement that the other three theories are not refuted, and it forces rewrites of Vocatia's definition, the Veil's Residue theory and the Accord's licensing basis.
D. Cut the Correction and keep only the story. Consequence: the Codex loses its thesis, the meta page's Correction section goes, and the Tempus drift needs a separate explanation.
gaps.recommendation: A, or B if Isaac wants the Aphorism tied in. Canon deliberately keeps these as positions none of which has been refuted. A living author's memoir cannot settle what makes Wellsprings answer without undoing the Accord's licensing basis. As a school's reading, it can still carry the Tempus drift: moving a sky body is far above the top Tier Ladder output, so R48-17 wants a metaphysical explanation, and a contested one serves.

gaps.topic: cc-02 Whether the texts' doctrine becomes system canon or stays one school's reading
gaps.question: The meta page says the Codex 'establishes' a fourth residue and that Mu-jin's testimony entered it 'into the formal canon'. Should the Volitional Trace (the record of an unfinished decision), the residue list and the rules for building an impression-body (the animated likeness made from a dead person's residue) become facts on the system pages (the Lexicon, the Crossing, the Magical Categories)? Or should they be what the Accord teaches inside the story, recorded on system pages as one school's reading? Every seam placed these ideas on the Soul Crystal without first asking this.
options: A. System canon. Consequence: the Lexicon, The Crossing and the Magical Categories each need new entries, and the Heresiology must agree line for line.

B. In-world doctrine only. The fiction's Accord teaches it; system pages call it a school's reading and leave the question open (R47-12). Consequence: least canon churn, but the Death seam's layer-mapping questions become questions about what the school claims.

C. Mixed. Impression-bodies and residues are canon (the Heresiology and The Crossing already use them), while the Volitional Trace stays a contested finding with rival readings. Consequence: the seams' layer mappings apply to the residues only, and the Trace becomes a live mystery players can investigate.
gaps.recommendation: C. The Heresiology already treats impression-bodies as real (Heresiology:66). A single disputed case history resting on one man's testimony is exactly what fair-play says should remain an 'interestingly wrong' school hook.

gaps.topic: cc-03 Fair-play treatment for every working the texts describe: cost, limits, counter, tell, Stage floor
gaps.question: Isaac's standing rule is that every working has a cost that hurts, stated limits, a counter someone can find, a tell and numbers within its band. Where does that play layer live for Mortalis Categories I to IV, the impression-body, the Genesio Trace activation and Mu-jin's own acts, and which counters apply? Canon's Counterplay page never mentions alchemy or Drafts. No seam asks how a player at the table spots or beats an impression-body.
options: A. Both. The texts carry the pieces in prose (the law, the cost, the tell), and each operation also gets a companion entry in the field format R47-2 prescribes (a Codex line with Craft and Stage floor, costs as a share of reserve, counters stated as facts). Consequence: more pages, but every counter can be found, as fair-play requires.
B. Companion entries only (the operation table from ae-10); the texts stay as lore. Consequence: this breaks R57-07, under which in-world documents must carry the full metaphysics.
C. Texts only, with no companion entries. Consequence: players cannot look anything up, which fails the 'every counter can be found' rule.
gaps.recommendation: A. Canon already supplies most of the answers. Waste radiates as heat (R47-8), so a regional Genesio activation scorches ground and can be seen for miles. 'The room pays' and a depleted site is the counter (Essence Ledger:266). Works inherit their Wellsprings' failures and opponents can induce them (R47-9); Anamnesis's inherited failure is that reading erases what it reads (Veil:76). Mending costs more than breaking (R47-11), so an impression-body must cost more than a Dissolution. Governing Sub-Stats belong to the practitioner (R47-10), which partly answers ae-06. Essence Ledger:298 lists 'alchemical treatment' as active recovery, which bears on ae-04. Echo Beasts (Veil:60) are canon's precedent for residue that condenses with no practitioner, which bears on Death:ws-10. The Veil's Drift Scale (Veil:89) is the canon cost for the threshold that L&H:41 says the Codex 'spends three volumes crossing'.

gaps.topic: cc-04 How many measured figures (EU, AU/s, η) the converted prose itself carries
gaps.question: The five texts give no numbers at all. R57-07 says every in-world document is fully metaphysical, and R48-16 says anyone with an instrument or a trained eye states figures as often as they would. Mu-jin has a signature instrument, Sight Through the Glass, which gives a full diagnostic overlay. How much of the arithmetic belongs inside each document? EU is the unit of Essence, AU/s is output rate, and η is efficiency.
options: A. Each author states figures as their instruments would give them. Mu-jin reads EU, η and site density whenever he takes off his spectacles. Malphas's treatise gives each Category's cost as a share of reserve, by Stage. The investigator logs readings taken at scenes. Consequence: every number must come from the Essence Ledger bands (R47-4), and none may be invented.
B. Figures in the Necrocursica only; the memoir and the field notes stay mostly literary. Consequence: this reads more naturally but leaves the Codex out of line with R57-07.
C. Figures in the companion entries only (cc-03 A). Consequence: this contradicts R57-07 and R48-16.
gaps.recommendation: A. It follows the rules as written, it fits each author's instrument and voice, and it gives players the pieces fair-play wants. It also forces the missing numbers (the impression-body's cost, the Genesio site's density, the scale of the drift) to be derived from the Ledger rather than guessed.

gaps.topic: cc-06 Which Craft carries the Mortalis operations, and which Craft Mu-jin and Malphas practise
gaps.question: Canon has five Crafts: Magicraft, Spellcraft (spoken), Runecraft (cut into a surface), Draftcraft (poured into a vessel) and Chantcraft (sung). It says every named practitioner gets one. Neither Mu-jin's card nor Malphas's names a Craft, and nothing assigns one to the impression-body or to Categories I to III. The Craft fixes the failure mode. Runecraft 'misfires continuously' until someone finds and breaks it, which is the Third Corruption's seal that keeps growing. Draftcraft 'works on the wrong person', which is the grief commission. Spellcraft 'dissipates'. The Craft also fixes who can hold the result: Draftcraft needs a Soul Crystal only at the moment of making, so a grieving non-practitioner could hold a bottled working.
options: A. Draftcraft for all Mortalis operations; Mu-jin Draftcraft; Malphas Draftcraft. Consequence: an impression-body is a poured product with provenance and paperwork, so it can be traced through the ledger, as ae-11's 'Draft product' reading suggests.

B. Runecraft for the Category III seal (inscribed, so it carries the cutter's hand, which fits the Glyphica seam's point on attribution) and Draftcraft for the vessel. Mu-jin is Draftcraft; Malphas is Runecraft-leaning. Consequence: the Third Corruption becomes a continuous misfire, and De Raits can be traced by his hand.
C. Spellcraft (spoken, as Vocatia is) for the summoning of the impression. Consequence: no author mark, so the Bench of Attribution cannot place the operator, and the investigation loses its trail.
gaps.recommendation: B. It gives each Corruption the failure mode canon already describes, keeps De Raits traceable for the Papers, and matches gcm-06 option 1 and the Glyphica seam's note that cut work carries its cutter's hand. Record the Craft in each operation's Codex line (cc-03).

gaps.topic: cc-07 The new Papers author as a person, not just a name and an office
gaps.question: Isaac wants a newly invented author for the Corrant Papers. The seams cover only the name swap (ct-16) and the office held (Setting:ws-12). Who is this person? That means a want, a refusal, a lie, a voice, a culture and naming register, a Stage (or none), a card or a roster entry, and the house style their document follows.
options: A. A full character card: Fracture of Worlds loadout, Voice block, pronunciation line, a card header dated to a stated moment (R54-11), and a voice fingerprint and casting entry. Consequence: the most work, but the investigator of a Malphas-adjacent case becomes a playable NPC with counters.
B. A roster NPC made through the wotr-npc build (want, refusal, lie, inventory, voice) with a short FOW line. Consequence: lighter, but it can be upgraded later.
C. A minimal named role inside the Papers only. Consequence: this falls below R50-27, because an author who 'matters' must be a person.
gaps.recommendation: A, or B if Isaac wants speed. The author carries a whole canon document, investigates the Genesio and Tempus case, and is the reader's route to Gillus. Also decide the house style (R51-33): Accord chancery, which is formal and Latinate, or 'letters in the writer's voice'. The current Papers are wry and personal, which clashes with a chancery document.

gaps.topic: cc-08 Real historical names on in-world people and texts: Paracelsus, Jabir, Trismegistus, the Emerald Tablet
gaps.question: The texts name people after real historical figures. There is 'Furveus, called Paracelsus'. There is 'Jabir', a roadside astrologer with an 'Emerald Principle', a nod to Jabir ibn Hayyan and the Emerald Tablet. There is 'Trismegistus', from Hermes Trismegistus. The meta page's epigraph paraphrases the Emerald Tablet. The naming law allows borrowed idea-names anywhere and real god, demon or saint names on beings, but says nothing on real historical persons. 'Paracelsus' means 'beyond Celsus', and there is no Celsus in the world. Which of these stay?
options: A. Keep them all as in-world names and epithets. Consequence: this is the quickest route, but a reader recognises Earth figures inside the world. It extends R51-06 (Earth-derived words are legal) to persons, which no rule yet covers.

B. Keep the ideas and the lens terms (Tria Prima, spagyric, Hermetic, Correspondence, the Emerald Tablet's wording). Give the people in-world names and credit the Earth sources in the author notes (R48-27). Consequence: the 'called Paracelsus' joke and Jabir's name change; km-14 settles Trismegistus in the same way.

C. Keep the epithets only where they have an in-world meaning (Trismegistus is glossed in-world as 'three parts of the wisdom'), and rename the rest. Consequence: a mixed result, with each name judged case by case.
gaps.recommendation: C. It keeps what the texts already explain in-world, drops the names whose sense depends on Earth history (Paracelsus, Jabir), and follows R48-22 and R48-27 for the ideas. Canon already uses 'Hermetic Principle' (Principle Overwrite:17), so that term stays.

gaps.topic: cc-09 Real-language correctness of the texts' coined Latin and Greek, and a Mahuo name for Mu-jin's book
gaps.question: The naming law requires borrowed names to be correct in their source language. It corrects a published name 'where the name keeps its sound', and it gives every item a name in each culture's tongue. Which of the texts' coinages should change? 'Necrocursica' pairs Greek necro- with a word that is not Latin. 'Anamnetic' has 'anamnestic' as its standard form, and canon never uses the adjective. 'Nospheric' reads as a misspelling of 'noospheric', but canon already uses 'Nospheric' on the Sub-Stats page. 'Urbis' is the Latin genitive, 'of the city', used as a city's name. And should Mu-jin's book carry a Mahuo true name beside 'The Alftian Codex'?
options: A. Correct everything that can keep its sound (Anamnetic becomes Anamnestic; Nospheric becomes Noospheric, and the Sub-Stats page is updated too). Leave Necrocursica and Urbis as they are, because R50-02 only corrects a name where the sound survives. Add a Mahuo true name for the Codex (R50-13, R50-23). Consequence: a small canon ripple on one Sub-Stats line.

B. Correct only the words that appear only in these texts (Anamnetic); keep Nospheric, since canon already uses it. Add no Mahuo title. Consequence: the fewest changes, but a known misspelling of a real word stays.
C. Rename the Necrocursica to a correct Latin or Greek form. Consequence: a new title for a canon book, and the Heresiology's and meta page's references change with it.
gaps.recommendation: A. It is what R50-01 and R50-02 already direct. The Mahuo name follows R50-13 now that a Mahuo court scholar is the author. Pronunciation lines (R50-34) go on any new place page (Castlefall, Genesio, Urbis).

gaps.topic: cc-11 How the documents reach the reader: the 'recovered journal' frame and the unknown marginal hand
gaps.question: The whole framing assumes an author who is gone and a text that was lost. The Codex is a 'Recovered Journal', 'Transcribed by the Silent Archivists' and 'Recovered from the sealed lower stacks'. Vol III opens on a marginal note in 'handwriting that is not' the author's. The author is now a living Archmagus of 38 (R57-01). Why are his journals recovered from sealed stacks, and whose hand is in the margin? km-16 asks only whether the author is dead, and ws-11 asks only about 'Naln'.
options: A. The Accord sealed his private journals because they are Mortalis-adjacent. Consequence: this fits the restricted classification, the investigator's reading them in a case file, and ct-13's clearance scheme. The 'recovered' wording becomes 'withdrawn' or 'sealed'.

B. He deposited them himself as a teaching record under his Dawn Guard teaching vow. Consequence: the texts become public-facing, the Restricted stamp needs a reason, and the Papers' access story changes.

C. Keep a far-future archival frame, with the transcription done long after his death. Consequence: this conflicts with the Withering-era dating (Setting:ws-01) and with the Heresiology's position after the events.
gaps.recommendation: A. It is the smallest change that fits a living author. Separately, give the marginal hand to Malphas. That pays off the Arena scene's 'marginal notes in a controlled archive' (Malphas seam missed-3) and ties the two authors together (mn-06, km-09) through an object the players can examine.

gaps.topic: cc-12 How much working procedure the Necrocursica spells out, and its empty Appendix I
gaps.question: Fair-play says documents give 'pieces, not solutions', and ability entries never say how to use a working (R47-1). The Necrocursica's Chapter the Second is billed as 'A Practitioner's Compendium': it gives complete glyph chains, Authorization to Sealing, for Categories One to Three. Its Appendix I, the Stabilization Protocol, contains only a pointer to a 'Technical Supplement' that does not exist. How complete should the procedures be?
options: A. Keep the full chains; the treatise is a how-to. Consequence: players and NPCs get a working recipe for impression-bodies, and the challenge of piecing it together is gone.

B. Give the law, the roles and the cost of each Category, but withhold the completion steps in-world. Leave Appendix I as the sealed Technical Supplement, a piece that can be found elsewhere, perhaps in the Accord archive or on the marginal-hand copy. Consequence: this matches 'documents give pieces', and the missing supplement becomes an in-world objective.
C. Write Appendix I out in full as a stabilisation protocol, which is a counter rather than an attack. Consequence: players get a defensive piece and the offensive chain stays partial.
gaps.recommendation: B, plus the defensive half of C. The stabilisation protocol is the natural findable counter to a failing Category Three seal, and the completion steps stay withheld. Appendix I's heading also credits Paracelsus and 'Noxinus Ren', so it follows the attribution decisions.

gaps.topic: cc-13 Write-back to the cards and downstream pages, and whether the rename is swept automatically
gaps.question: The conversion adds events to two canon lives: the commission, the Genesio hollow and the Codex years for Mu-jin, and confinement at Genesio and the treatise for Malphas. Neither card's Lore or Ties mentions any of this. Should the cards absorb these events, with the character-lore pass checking them against the cards, or do the texts stay documents the cards do not cite? And should the renames go into build/renames.yaml so that stale_names and the Notion sweep catch leftovers?
options: A. Write back and register. Both cards gain the events in Lore and Ties, and renames.yaml gains Noxinus Ren→Malphas, Oren Corrant→[new name] and 'Research Archives Division'→'Research and Archives Division'. 'Vis Trismegistus' is swept only as the full name, never the bare 'Vis', which is a Latin word and is the tomb label km-06 has not yet decided. Consequence: the sweep is fully consistent, but any old name kept on purpose (Noxinus surviving as a person, km-09) must be left out.
B. Write back to the cards; hand-edit the pages with no renames entry. Consequence: leftovers are likely in the hub, the meta page and the Heresiology cross-references.
